          • Rewards
            • A central figure or system for reporting quests and earning rewards is essential.
            • ? Quest Giver: Mayor Hiroshi Takeda oversees adventurer rewards. He
            • delegates through a steward, often found in Takeda Manor.
            • ? Adventurer's Guild (The Path of Blades): A small, informal guild hall where
            • adventurers report completed tasks and find new ones. The guildmaster, Kana
            • Yoshiro, is a retired swordswoman.
            • ? Religious Rewards: The Temple of the Three Moons rewards spiritual services
            • or rare relics for quests tied to the kami or yokai disturbances.
          • Rest
            • Options for safe lodging and rest are diverse, giving players flexibility and roleplay
            • opportunities.
            • ? The Jade Lantern: A mid-tier inn with modest accommodations and a lively
            • tavern. Owned by Yuto and Aiko Mori , who gossip about local happenings.
            • ? Temple Sanctuary: The Temple of the Three Moons offers free lodging for the
            • devout or those serving the community. Simple mats and shared quarters.
            • ? Local Hospitality: Villagers sometimes open their homes to travelers. Aya the
            • Weaver or Taro the Hunter might host adventurers in exchange for small favors
            • or news.
            • ? Camping: Near the Frostwood Outpost, adventurers can camp safely under
            • militia protection.
          • Resupply
            • A variety of shops and services allow players to trade, sell, or restock.
            • ? Market District: Vendors offer general goods, local produce, and small magical
            • trinkets.
            • ? Artisan's Row
            • ? Haruto's Forge: A blacksmith inspired by Master Hideo, Haruto crafts
            • weapons and tools with care.
            • ? Ayame's Apothecary: Specializing in herbal remedies and basic potions,
            • Ayame is known for her knowledge of Frostwood flora.
            • ? Special Items: Players can commission unique items, such as charms blessed
            • by the temple priests or custom blades forged from rare materials.
          • Research
            • Opportunities to gather information and investigate the world's mysteries.
            • ? The Temple Library: A modest collection of scrolls on local lore, kami, and
            • yokai. The head priest, Reiko Matsuda , can guide research efforts.
            • ? The Storyteller's Hearth: A small alehouse where locals gather to share tales.
            • Renji Sato , a former bandit, knows much about hidden paths and old legends.
            • ? Village Elders: Knowledge of the Frostwood and its peculiarities is passed down
            • orally. Villagers like Yumi Harada , a retired hunter, can provide insights.
          • Recreation
            • Unique leisure opportunities immerse players in the culture and life of Nagano.
            • ? Seasonal Festivals:
            • ? The Spring Equinox Festival happens during the adventure, with music,
            • dances, and ceremonial offerings to the Earth Kami.
            • ? Combat Training:
            • ? The Frostwood Dojo offers sparring matches and lessons. Run by Riku
            • Matsunaga , it's a good way to spend downtime.
            • ? Gambling and Games:
            • ? The Jade Lantern Tavern hosts dice games, card games, and storytelling
            • competitions.
            • ? Artisan Workshops:
            • ? Players can participate in pottery, weaving, or smithing as a creative
            • break.
          • Key NPCs of Nagano
            • ? Mayor Hiroshi Takeda: Leader of Nagano, a calm and pragmatic administrator
            • with deep respect for Hideo's legacy.
            • ? Kana Yoshiro: Guildmaster of the adventurer's guild, a sharp-witted retired
            • swordswoman who knows the political and spiritual undercurrents of the region.
            • ? Reiko Matsuda: Head priest of the Temple of the Three Moons, who serves as a
            • spiritual guide and historian.
            • ? Haruto the Blacksmith: Inspired by Hideo, Haruto is determined to uphold the
            • smithing traditions passed down to him.
            • ? Renji Sato: Former bandit indebted to Hideo, Renji now works as a guide and
            • informant, though his past still haunts him.
            • Mayor Hiroshi Takeda
          • Unique Features of Nagano
            • ? The Whispering Glade: A serene cemetery outside Nagano, where Hideo is
            • buried. It's a site of spiritual power, tied to both the kami and yokai of the
            • Frostwood.
            • ? The Frostwood Outpost: Manned by Nagano's militia, this outpost protects
            • travelers and merchants while monitoring the Frostwood's unpredictable dangers.
            • ? The Weaver's Market: Held every ten-day, this market attracts merchants from
            • nearby villages, offering exotic goods and opportunities for intrigue.

TLW + Shuigari Omnibus

Consolidated notes for The Last Whisper of Steel (TLW) and Shuigari.

Session Notes

Session 019: The Steel Tablet's Summons (2025-12-17)

Kazuki reveals Hideo's steel tablet, the party takes the citadel job, and a ledger heist exposes guard corruption.

Session 019: The Steel Tablet's Summons

Arc: The Iron Court (Arc 2)
Session Number: 19
Date Played: [Insert Date]
Session Type: Revelation, Investigation, Heist
Status: COMPLETED

Review the Characters

  • Fox: Hideo knew about the implanted memories and lost master. Validate the hunt for identity.
  • Shigeo: Kento reappears; Saan disrespects him. Greed's Embrace is named in the prophecy.
  • Aoshi: Last Waban, visions, oni blood called out on the tablet.
  • Thornbringer: "Walker between wild and steel." The vault may tie to the Well of Life.
  • Kanji: "Resolver of guilt." Investigation spotlight with the ledger and cipher.
  • Yasei: Hikari's servant named; "voice of the silenced kami."

Strong Start

Read Aloud (tea house entry):

The door slides open with a whisper of wood on wood. Warm air embraces you, fragrant with jasmine tea and incense. Low tables dot the room, paper lanterns cast amber pools of light, and rice-paper screens divide the space into private alcoves.

A woman in a practical indigo kimono steps forward, her eyes sharp and calm. "Welcome to the Whispering Willow," she says. "You carry something that marks you as expected guests."

She leads you to a secluded alcove. A lacquered table, six silk cushions, a steaming tea service, and a scroll that reads: "Water wears away stone." Through a half-open shutter, the Upper Citadel looms above the Middle Terrace like a crown of iron.

Possible Scenes

  • The Whispering Willow Tea House: Kazuki's arrival, the two curses, Hideo's final request.
  • The Steel Tablet: prophecy revealed, the twenty names, warnings about Lady Hana and the boy heir.
  • Iron Rest Inn: Mama Tora, sake, Starcall Table reunion.
  • Hidden Lotus reveal: Kaoru's role, missing blacksmith's daughter.
  • Guard Tower: meet Saan, discover Kento, steal a ledger.
  • Ledger crisis: decode the cipher, retrieve the key book.

Fantastic Locations

  • Whispering Willow Tea House: warm lantern light, privacy screens, incense and jasmine.
  • Iron Rest Inn: cursed street, shuttered buildings, wards on doorframes.
  • Middle Terrace Guard Tower: official stone and steel, lax discipline inside.
  • Upper Citadel (off-screen): looming presence, festival clock ticking.
  • Iron Market: forge smoke, missing girl thread.

Secrets and Clues

  • Master Hideo chose death by Kazuki to deny the Circle his secrets.
  • The steel tablet prophecy names the party and twenty others; steel cannot lie.
  • The Circle seeks "the first chain" beneath the Upper Citadel.
  • The boy heir's blood is the key; protect him, but don't trust what speaks through him.
  • Lady Hana Arashi is named as a danger on the tablet.
  • Kaoru Sugimoto leads the Hidden Lotus Society.
  • The guard ledger hides a coded message; a book cipher key sits in Saan's office.
  • A missing blacksmith's daughter may tie to guard corruption or Circle activity.
  • Renji Sato is listed as a potential ally who was "broken."

Important NPCs

  • Kazuki Takemura: Twice-Cursed Samurai; employer and bearer of the tablet.
  • Mama Hoshiko: Tea house proprietor; calm, observant, neutral ground.
  • Mama Tora Kaneshiro: Iron Rest Inn owner; named ally on the tablet.
  • Kaoru Sugimoto: Hidden Lotus leader; Starcall Table cover.
  • Master of the Watch Saan: Corrupt guard commander; ledger owner.
  • Kento: Shigeo's son; guard caught between family and duty.

Monsters

  • None planned. Potential opposition: Obsidian Circle agents, corrupt guards.

Treasure

  • 500 gold advance from Kazuki (500 more on completion).
  • Stolen guard ledger with a coded message.
  • Wooden token with Hideo's maker's mark (summons).

Session Recap

The party answered Master Hideo's summons at the Whispering Willow and met Kazuki Takemura, who revealed he ended Hideo's life at the smith's request. Kazuki presented a steel tablet containing Hideo's prophecy, naming the party and a list of allies and threats. He hired them to infiltrate the Upper Citadel, protect the boy heir, and find the "first chain" before the Festival of Ascending Iron.

At the Iron Rest Inn, the party met Mama Tora and reunited with the Starcall Table. Kaoru revealed herself as a Hidden Lotus Society leader and asked for help finding a missing blacksmith's daughter. The party confronted Master of the Watch Saan at the guard tower, discovered Kento, and stole a ledger containing a ciphered message. The session ended with a plan to retrieve the cipher key book and return the ledger before the theft is discovered.

TLW Session 018 - Tea House Tithe (2025-12-10)

Prep beats for Session 018, from the road ambush to the tea house tithe.

Arc Position

  • Arc: 2 -- Takashima Front
  • Session Number: 018 (first session of the arc)
  • Base of Operations: Takashima Fortress City (refugee quarter near the southern gates)

Session Overview

On the road from Nagano to Takashima, the party stumbles onto a lacquer-slick killing ground: four travelers torn apart and a six-armed troll looming over Iseri, who is unconscious and bound in resin strands. This ambush tees up the cost of Lady Arashi's neglect before the party even sees Takashima's gates. Surviving the road hazard leads into the city's pressure cooker of refugees, ration lines, and the Dust Petal Tea House summons from the Twice-Cursed Samurai, who offers intel and aid--but only if the party steals the miracle ledger tying Lady Arashi to Obsidian Circle smuggling.

Strong Start Options (Wednesday opener)

  • Six-Arm Road Ambush (default): Six chitinous arms crank a prayer wheel made of bones as a troll hoists Iseri's limp form. Black resin bandages her torso; the troll hums a broken shrine song and snaps its mandibles toward the party. Four bodies hang from lacquered branches, each clutching a different shrine token. ? Immediate combat/skill split: free Iseri before she takes death save failures; optional flashback to how she got snared (failed scout roll, cursed milepost?)
  • Tea House Ultimatum (if the road is skipped): Steam curls off cracked teacups as masked patrols drag a street-preacher into the mud outside. Inside, the ronin kneels alone beneath a shrine of guttering candles, steel mask resting on the tatami. His curse bleeds black lacquer across the floorboards as he rasps: "Takashima rots from within. Help me carve out the infection--and I will help you cleanse your shrines." ? He slides a new missive onto the table: an Obsidian Circle resupply slips through the southern gate at dusk.
  • Gate Stampede: Refugees surge as gate inspectors sound an alarm; a Circle courier tries to burn his ledger to avoid capture. The party can intervene, grab the courier, or ride the chaos to slip beyond the walls.
  • Shrine Dawn Failure: At first light the warding bells stutter and a sheet of black lacquer rain falls over the shrine quarter. Spirits wail as magic fizzles. Immediate skill challenge to stabilize a warded shrine; reward favor with shrine wardens.

Major Beats & Outcomes (last session recap)

  • Dust Petal Parley: Negotiated terms with the Twice-Cursed Samurai; he admitted killing Master Hideo on Lady Arashi's orders but swore to expose her Circle ties. Party accepted the job to recover Arashi's miracle ledger from the Silk Ledger Guildhall.
  • City Texture: Witnessed shrine wardens struggling with failing rituals; Fox's prayer faltered, confirming the arc theme of dwindling magic. Shigeo brokered food for refugees, earning quiet goodwill.
  • Stealth Ledger Heist: Infiltrated the guildhall during a midnight accounting shift. Kanji and Yasei used festival masks to slip past guards while Thornbringer's druidcraft muffled the windows. Aoshi neutralized a Circle scribe branded with obsidian prayer beads.
  • Evidence Secured: Retrieved the miracle ledger detailing Arashi's payments to Circle couriers and a manifest of shrine reagents bound for "Project Heirloom." Captured scribe revealed code phrases for Circle dead-drops in the shrine quarter.
  • Ronin's Aid Unlocked: Delivered the ledger to the ronin; he provided a cache of silent-step tabi (+1 Stealth) and a password for passing through his covert tunnel to the outer walls.

Scene Options (pick 2-3 beats for Wednesday)

  • Roadside Recovery: Secure Iseri, interrogate the troll's shrine tokens, and track whether the victims were couriers or refugees. Clue: one token bears Arashi's crest scorched black.
  • Gate Interdiction: Intercept the Obsidian Circle resupply at the southern gate; choices: stealth swap crates, intimidate officials, or cut a deal with the desperate inspector on duty.
  • Dead-Drop Gamble: Use the phrases ("the wind carries lacquer" / "the lacquer cracks at dusk") to plant false orders that redirect Circle operatives into an ambush near the shrine quarter.
  • Shrine Triage: Help wardens stabilize a sputtering shrine; skill challenge with corruption risks that foreshadow Project Heirloom's drain.
  • Tunnel Crawl: Traverse the ronin's covert tunnel to the Okug?ri; hazards include collapsing masonry, lacquer seep, and blind oni catfish.
  • Court Intrigue: Present or threaten to leak the ledger to rival magistrates; social contest reveals Arashi's next move and potential allies.

Character Review (PCs)

  • Kanji: Masked infiltrator; excels at deception and disguise. Give chances to exploit festival masks and bureaucratic loopholes.
  • Yasei: Agile scout; likes rooftop angles. Offer vertical paths during gate or tunnel scenes.
  • Thornbringer: Nature/druidcraft; can muffle, root, or cleanse lacquer corruption. Spotlight during shrine triage.
  • Aoshi: Precise striker; effective at neutralizing key targets. Set up a single high-value Circle courier or lacquer spawn to shut down.
  • Fox: Spiritual connection; prayers faltering. Let Fox sense the kami's pain and gain visions about Project Heirloom.
  • Shigeo: Quartermaster/face; good with supplies and people. Tie him to refugee morale and negotiations with inspectors.

Relevant Foes & Challenges

  • Six-Arm Lacquer Troll (opener boss): Multi-grapple plus resin restrain; lashes out with bone prayer wheel (disadvantage aura on Concentration saves if within 10 ft). Regeneration only halted by fire/radiant or breaking the lacquer prayer wheel.
  • Obsidian Circle Couriers (skirmishers): Poisoned knives, smoke pellets, panic button (signal flare that calls 1d2 reinforcements if not silenced).
  • Gate Inspectors (neutral, swayable): Start cautious; can become allies if protected or bribed with food slips.
  • Lacquer Wraith (hazard for shrine triage): Uses grapple + corrosive drain; becomes vulnerable if blessed water or druidcraft cleanses lacquer coating.
  • Blind Oni Catfish (tunnel beast): Burrows through wet stone; low-light blindsight, hates bright flame or thunder damage.

Key NPCs in Play

  • Iseri: Found unconscious and resin-bound by the six-arm troll; waking her yields fragmented visions of a cursed milepost humming with lacquer.
  • Twice-Cursed Samurai (ally/patron): Curse worsens when he lies; can provide covert tunnel access and pressure on Arashi's guards.
  • Lady Arashi (off-screen antagonist): Project Heirloom architect; wants to present "miracles" to keep power. Will retaliate if ledger leaks.
  • Kazuo Himura (refugee retainer): Knows which inspectors are bribeable; fears Arashi but respects the party's mercy.
  • Whisper-Book Scribe (prisoner/contact): Has dead-drop phrasing and knows Circle couriers' shift rotations; can be coerced or turned.

Fantastic Locations

  • Nagano-Takashima Forest Road: Cursed mileposts ooze lacquer; trees hung with bone prayer wheels; a shallow ravine offers partial cover against the troll's reach.
  • Takashima Southern Gate: Four-tiered checkpoint with brass prayer wheels, incense braziers, and refugee cattle-chutes; under each platform run lacquer-streaked sluices feeding the undercaverns.
  • Dust Petal Tea House (safe meet): Candlelit shrine alcove, lacquer-stained tatami, hidden trapdoor to the ronin's tunnel.
  • Shrine Quarter Wards: Cracked jade bells, rain of black lacquer at dawn, kami visages flickering in puddles that whisper bargains.
  • Under-gate Caverns: Flooded maintenance shafts beneath the gate; echoing water, blind oni catfish, and forgotten shrine plaques that can be used as cover or leverage.

Treasure & Boons

  • Troll Salvage: Bone prayer wheel (counts as holy symbol; shatters to suppress regeneration in a 10-ft aura for 1 minute, single use), resin cords (50 gp; advantage on one grapple check when used as fetters).
  • Circle Resupply Crates: Smoke pellets, obsidian prayer beads worth 50 gp each, 1-2 vials of shadow-ink (advantage on a single Stealth check in dim light).
  • Shrine Favor: Blessing of the Bell--once per day, one PC can reroll a failed Wisdom save against fear or charm until corruption is cleansed.
  • Gate Inspector's Ledger: Contains names of bribed officials; leverage for court intrigue or blackmail.
  • Tunnel Cache (ronin): Spare silent-step tabi pair or lacquer-eater salve (neutralizes one lacquer-based hazard on contact).

NPCs Featured

  • Twice-Cursed Samurai: Now a reluctant patron; curse worsens when he lies, giving the party a leverage point.
  • Kazuo Himura: Lady Arashi's retainer, hiding among refugees; confirmed Arashi's private audiences with Circle envoys.
  • "Whisper-Book" Scribe: Low-level Circle operative captured at the guildhall; knows dead-drop phrases and believes the boy heir is already "anointed."

Discoveries & Clues

  • Lady Arashi funds falsified miracles through Silk Ledger intermediaries.
  • "Project Heirloom" requires shrine reagents being redirected away from Takashima's failing wardings.
  • Circle dead-drops in the shrine quarter use the phrase "the wind carries lacquer" for pickup, "the lacquer cracks at dusk" for delivery.
  • Shrine wardens report spells sputtering at dawn, implying the kami drain is accelerating.

Rewards & Mechanics

  • Silent-Step Tabi: Treated as light footwear that grants advantage on the first Stealth check made each infiltration scene (once per scene).
  • Cache Refill: Minor healing herbs replenished; each character starts next session with one free use of a common healing kit.

Threads for Next Session

  • Use the dead-drop phrases to plant forged instructions and misdirect Circle couriers.
  • Decide whether to expose Arashi publicly or trade the ledger to a rival faction in Takashima's court.
  • Investigate the shrine reagent manifests to locate "Project Heirloom" and the boy heir's current hiding place.
  • Explore the ronin's tunnel to the outer walls to reach the Okug?ri without alerting the city guard.

Hideos-Steel-Tablet-Last-Will

Master Hideo's Last Will and Testament - The Steel Tablet

Item: Hideo's Steel Tablet of Final Instructions
Bearer: Kazuki Takemura (The Twice-Cursed Samurai)
Significance: Last will, mission directive, and list of trusted allies
Revelation: The party is named on it - Hideo knew about them before he died

[Full content as created above...]

Iron-Rest-Inn-Mama-Tora

The Iron Rest Inn - Cursed Street Scene

Location: Middle Terrace, Takashima City
District: East of Smiths' Quarter, near the abandoned warehouse district
Reputation: "The Cursed Street" - locals avoid after dark
Current State: Nearly empty, struggling to survive, haunted by yokai
Scene Type: Eerie downtime, celebration in isolation, yokai investigation hook

THE STREET: WHISPERS AND WARNINGS

Approaching the Inn (Read Aloud - 2 minutes)

The streets grow quieter as you walk east from the bustling Smiths' Quarter. The forge-song fades behind you. The lamps grow fewer. And then... you're here.

This street feels wrong.

It's not abandoned - there are buildings, shops, homes. But they're... closed. Shuttered. Silent. Even though the sun hasn't fully set, every window is dark, every door barred. You see chalk marks on doorframes (Religion DC 12: protective wards against spirits). Prayer strips flutter from eaves, their ink faded by weather and time.

The cobblestones are clean - too clean. No refuse, no debris, as if even the wind won't linger here. Your footsteps echo strangely, carrying farther than they should.

And at the end of this street, standing alone: The Iron Rest Inn.

It's the only building with lights burning. Three stories of dark wood and stone, it looks solid enough, but... worn. Paint peeling. Roof tiles cracked. One shutter hangs at an angle, creaking in the breeze that shouldn't exist here. The sign above the door shows an iron bed frame, but someone has scratched marks across it - claw marks? Or desperate attempts to warn travelers away?

Through the windows, you see lamplight. Movement. Someone is inside.

As you approach, a voice calls from a nearby house - an old woman's face appears briefly in a second-story window: "Don't stay there after dark! The tea house weeps!" Then her shutters slam closed.

      • High Forgemother Saeko -- stern priest-smith who blesses blades before the Festival of Ascending Iron.
      • Acolyte Ren -- anxious clerk who tracks tithe ledgers and fears Circle tampering.
    • What They Know:
      • Vault Entrances: Temple archives mention eight sealed approaches; two are described as "forge-warm paths" tied to smithing guild tunnels.
      • Hikari's Grove: Saeko records a temple legend: the grove is hidden within the vault's maze, appearing only to those who fight beyond exhaustion and capacity--true heroes.
      • Stream of the One Tree: Ren heard rumors of a silver-thread stream used to temper soulsteel; source noted as "beneath the old distillery."
    • Quests & Hooks:
      • Missing blessing seals were stolen from the forge altar; recover them before the festival.
      • A sacred anvil cools with black lacquer; cleanse it or risk corrupted weapon oaths.
    • Shrine of Hachiman -- War and honor; samurai vows, militia rites, and vigil watch.
    • NPCs:
      • Captain Jiro Takeda -- veteran shrine-guard, distrusts nobles, respects honorable acts.
      • Novice Yui -- messenger with a network of militia rumors.
    • What They Know:
      • Vault Entrances: Jiro knows of eight entrance codes used by citadel patrols; only two are still in active rotation.
      • Hikari's Grove: Yui repeats a vow from old drillmasters: the grove only appears within the vault's maze to those who push beyond their limits.
      • Stream of the One Tree: Old war maps mark a spring-fed channel used for siege water; "One Tree" is scribbled in the margin.
    • Quests & Hooks:
      • A disgraced guard seeks public redemption through a dangerous vigil; escort him.
      • A cache of oath-scrolls vanished from the shrine armory; track the thief.
    • Sanctuary of Susanoo -- Storms and chaos; storm-watching, warding against tempests.
    • NPCs:
      • Stormwatcher Mikoto -- seer who reads wind patterns from the citadel heights.
      • Tide-Keeper Hanae -- caretaker of storm wards, secretly buying black-market reagents.
    • What They Know:
      • Vault Entrances: Mikoto saw eight storm-ward spirals on an old survey--entrances aligned to wind directions.
      • Hikari's Grove: Hanae keeps a whispered clue: follow a white moth that appears only when you are spent to the edge of collapse--it flutters through the maze and vanishes at the grove's veil. The trials beyond remain unchanged.
      • Stream of the One Tree / Distillery: Smugglers whisper about a distillery that draws from the One Tree stream, hidden below the Terrace.
    • Quests & Hooks:
      • Sudden storm surges break warding lines; gather rare reagents before the next squall.
      • A storm-omened relic is buried in the harbor mud; retrieve it before a rival cult.
  • Lower Yards -- Industrial and lower-tier neighborhoods.

TLWoS: Arc 2 Opening - Road to Takashima (2025-12-10)

Session-ready beats for launching Arc 2 on the road to Takashima.

Arc 2 Opening: The Road to Takashima

Session Setup

Opening Encounter: The Six-Armed Troll

Location: Road to Takashima
Discovery: The party encounters a six-armed troll with an unconscious man restrained. Four dead bodies litter the ground.

The Scene: - Iseri Tetsuo is unconscious, held by the troll - Four corpses surround them (identities unknown) - Combat or negotiation possible - Tetsuo's condition critical

Key Questions: - Who are the dead? - What happened here? - Is Tetsuo a victim or perpetrator?

Getting to Takashima

Options: 1. Take Tetsuo directly to the city (if stable enough) 2. Make camp and tend to wounds before traveling 3. Skip to the city gates regardless

Outcome: Either way, the story moves to Takashima's gates

The Gates of Takashima

The Situation

Takashima's gates are heavily guarded. Guards are turning away most travelers - the city is dealing with an influx of refugees from the south. Getting inside won't be easy for a random group of travelers, especially if they're carrying an unconscious stranger.

Long lines of desperate people wait, hoping for entry. The guards are tired, suspicious, and have little patience.

The Reunion

In the crowd waiting to enter, the party spots a familiar face: Kaoru Sugimoto, along with the surviving members of The Starcall Table from Nagano.

Present: - Kaoru Sugimoto - as composed as ever despite the chaos - Daisuke "Silver Pockets" Inoue - looking less charming in refugee lines - Haruki "The Boar" Takeda - uncharacteristically subdued - Aiko Hayashi - armor showing signs of recent conflict

What happened in Nagano? The Starcall Table's presence here, looking worse for wear, suggests something drove them from their usual routes. They're survivors, not just travelers.

Kaoru's Offer

Kaoru recognizes the party. She has connections - she can get them into the city. But it will cost them.

Her Price: A favor. She needs capable people, and the party has proven themselves before.

The Bargain: Entry to Takashima in exchange for completing a task once inside.

Inside Takashima

The Wild Lotus Society

Once inside the city, Kaoru reveals her true affiliations. She's not just a merchant and gambler - she's a member of the Wild Lotus Society, a group of ghost hunters and demon slayers who work on behalf of the citizenry.

The Wild Lotus Society: - Hunt supernatural threats - Work outside official channels - Serve the common people - Mix of warriors, spiritualists, and investigators - Kaoru's role within them suggests her coin trick was no mere sleight of hand

The Task: The Haunted Tea House

Kaoru needs the party to investigate an old tea house. According to reports, a vengeful spirit haunts the place, driving away anyone who enters. The owners are desperate - their livelihood is gone, and the neighborhood lives in fear.

The Assignment: - Clear out the spirit from the old tea house - Determine what it wants (if anything) - Restore peace to the location - Report back to the Wild Lotus Society

What Kaoru Knows: - Multiple witnesses have seen a figure in samurai armor - Objects move on their own - Temperature drops when the spirit manifests - No one has been killed (yet), but several have been injured - The haunting began recently - something triggered it

The Tea House Investigation

The Truth

The "vengeful spirit" is the Twice Cursed Samurai. But the party will discover he's not the monster the rumors suggest.

Key Discovery: The Twice Cursed Samurai did NOT murder Master Hideo.

The Real Story: [To be revealed during investigation] - What actually happened to Master Hideo? - Why is the Twice Cursed Samurai here? - What is he protecting or seeking? - How does this connect to larger events in Takashima?

Investigation Hooks

  • Witnesses in the neighborhood
  • The tea house owners' account
  • Physical evidence in the tea house
  • Spiritual/magical traces
  • Connection to Master Hideo
  • The Twice Cursed Samurai's own testimony (if they can communicate)

Key NPCs

  • Iseri Tetsuo - New party member, mysterious background
  • Kaoru Sugimoto - Wild Lotus Society member, party's entry ticket
  • Daisuke "Silver Pockets" Inoue - Starcall Table survivor
  • Haruki "The Boar" Takeda - Starcall Table survivor
  • Aiko Hayashi - Starcall Table survivor
  • Twice Cursed Samurai - The "spirit" haunting the tea house
  • Master Hideo - Murder victim (or is he?)

Questions for Development

  1. What drove the Starcall Table from Nagano to Takashima as refugees?
  2. What are Iseri Tetsuo's immediate goals upon waking?
  3. How does Kaoru present the Wild Lotus Society to the party?
  4. What clues lead the party to question the "vengeful spirit" narrative?
  5. What is the Twice Cursed Samurai's real agenda?
  6. How does this tea house investigation connect to the larger Arc 2 plot?
  7. Are there other Wild Lotus Society members the party will meet?

Session Flow

  1. Opening Combat/Encounter - Troll and Tetsuo
  2. Recovery/Travel - Getting to know Tetsuo (or carrying his unconscious body)
  3. The Gates - Refugee crisis, blocked entry
  4. Reunion - Starcall Table, specifically Kaoru
  5. The Bargain - Entry for service
  6. Inside Takashima - Wild Lotus Society revelation
  7. The Assignment - Haunted tea house mission
  8. Investigation Begins - First steps toward the truth

Adventures

Adventure - The Twice Cursed Act I

Adventure: The Twice Cursed - Act I, Master Hideo's Funeral

Act I opens The Last Whisper of Steel with a solemn rite in the Whispering Glade. The scene establishes relationships, tensions, and mysteries that propel the campaign.

Setting the Stage

  • Location: Whispering Glade outside Nagano, ringed by spirit-touched cherry trees that shed glowing petals.
  • Occasion: Funeral of Master Hideo Nakata during the Moonlit Reverence festival (21 Tsukinami).
  • Atmosphere: Cold breeze, distant temple bells, and an undercurrent of unease. The glade doubles as a spirit nexus.

Key Beats

  1. Arrival & Procession: Mourners assemble--Nagano villagers, Takashima retainers, Lady Hana Arashi's delegation, and wandering adventurers. Each arrival offers introductions and first impressions.
  2. Remembrance Rites: The Temple of the Three Moons leads prayers; attendees may offer eulogies or tokens. Insight checks reveal conflicting emotions among nobles and apprentices.
  3. Disruptions & Omens:
  4. A raven yokai circles overhead leaving a single black feather charged with moonlight.
  5. A tremor ripples through the glade as cherry petals drift against the wind.
  6. Whispers hint that artifacts from Hideo's shrine have vanished.
  7. Political Undercurrents:
  8. Lady Hana Arashi probes for allies while weighing Nagano's vulnerability.
  9. Lord Ichiro Kagemura deploys retainers (Akane Hiroshi, Riku Matsunaga) to monitor rivals.
  10. Kana Yoshiro and Mayor Hiroshi Takeda juggle logistics, worried about bandits and Obsidian Circle activity.
  11. The Warning: A raven yokai manifests briefly, intoning that "steel remembers" before vanishing. Arcana/Religion checks reveal ties to Tsukuyomi and impending imbalance.

Roleplay & Skill Opportunities

  • Social Scenes: Offer condolences, trade secrets, or challenge a noble's statement. Persuasion or Insight can secure future favors.
  • Ritual Participation: Players can add offerings; successful Religion checks reinforce bonds with the kami (granting inspiration or minor boons).
  • Investigation: Searching the glade uncovers disturbed earth, missing relics, and traces leading toward the Frostwood.

Clues & Leads

  • Missing Relics: Notes point to the temple storeroom, the market quarter, and possible Obsidian Circle interference.
  • Raven Feather: Functions as a focus; Divination or Identify reveals it resonates with Tsukuyomi's domain and the Twice-Cursed Samurai.
  • Contradictory Testimonies: NPCs provide partial truths--use these to seed side quests (e.g., tracking a bandit infiltrator or escorting Lady Hana's envoy).

Featured NPCs

  • Lady Hana Arashi: Diplomat seeking leverage; offers sponsorship but expects discretion.
  • Akane Hiroshi & Hiroto Masanori: Rival retainers whose shared history can spark duels or alliances.
  • Renji "Driftwood" Sato: Observes quietly; may leave a driftwood carving at Hideo's altar.
  • Reiko Matsuda: Priestess who senses the shrine's wards weakening.

Outcomes

  • Players choose how they honor Hideo, whom they trust, and which lead to follow.
  • The act concludes once the funeral rites end and immediate investigations or escort missions are assigned.

Use Act I to cement motivations, reveal stakes, and place each character on the board before the journey into the Frostwood begins.

Adventure - The Twice Cursed Act II

Adventure: The Twice Cursed - Act II, Journey Through Hisui no Mori

Act II escorts the party from Nagano's mourning into the living maze of the Jade Forest (Hisui no Mori). The goal: follow clues, earn the forest's favor, and locate the gate into the Ryuseki Peaks.

Objectives

  1. Track the Clues: Follow the raven feather's pull, missing shrine relics, or spectral footprints leading into the forest.
  2. Navigate the Living Maze: Overcome shifting paths, spirit lantern riddles, and disorienting fogs.
  3. Face the Forest's Trials: Engage kami, yokai, and environmental tests through diplomacy, wits, or combat.
  4. Unlock the Ryuseki Gate: Prove worth to the spectral guardian and secure passage toward the Twice-Cursed Samurai.

Day 1 -- Afternoon: Entering Hisui no Mori

  • First Checks: Survival (DC 12) or Perception (DC 15) to stay on the true trail. Failure introduces kitsune trickery or detours toward yokai lairs.
  • Shrine Encounter: A sorrowful Lesser Earth Kami warns "The forest remembers; tread lightly." Offerings grant advantage on future navigation checks.
  • Environmental Tone: The air hums with latent magic; characters feel watched even in silence.

Day 1 -- Evening: Shifting Paths

  • Skill Challenge: Use the "Navigating the Living Maze of Hisui no Mori" challenge (Athletics, Survival, Insight, Arcana) to push through shifting routes.
  • Spirit Lantern Puzzle: Lanterns marked with kanji for Hideo's virtues lead onward; misreading the signs attracts shikigami or shadow wolves.
  • Ambush Risk: Failing Stealth/Insight checks triggers a coordinated strike by yokai defenders testing the party's readiness.

Day 1 -- Night: Trials of the Forest

  • Trial of Wits: Reflections pose riddles tied to steel and honor. Success reveals a hidden causeway; failure inflicts exhaustion or psychic strain.
  • Trial of Honor: A kami in samurai guise challenges the group to a controlled duel or a debate on duty. Victors gain inspiration-like boons; dishonorable conduct angers the forest.
  • Optional Trial: Players can petition the forest for guidance, trading personal secrets or memories for safe passage.

Day 2 -- Dawn: Threshold of the Ryuseki Peaks

  • Ancient Gate: Stone torii carved with Soulsteel motifs hum with moonlit energy.
  • Spectral Samurai: Guardian demands proof of worth--either a duel (use the Weakened Spectral Samurai stat block) or solving the Gate of Master Hideo puzzle.
  • Consequences: Victory opens the passage and awards a blessing; failure means retreating to recover or negotiating aid from forest spirits.

Playstyle Guidance

  • Spiritual Route: Emphasize diplomacy with kami, invoking rituals and offerings to gather allies or shortcuts.
  • Martial Route: Treat encounters as a gauntlet of escalating battles culminating in the spectral duel.
  • Exploratory Route: Focus on lore discoveries--cartography, hidden shrines, and clues pointing toward the Obsidian Circle's manipulations.

By the end of Act II, the party should feel transformed--tempered by riddles, whispers, and the forest's judgment--as they ascend toward the Ryuseki Peaks and the Twice-Cursed Samurai.

Adventure - The Twice Cursed Act III

Adventure: The Twice Cursed - Act III, Labyrinth of the Twice-Cursed

Act III thrusts the party into the Ryuseki Peaks--an astral-touched fortress reshaped by the Twice-Cursed Samurai's fractured soul. The domain mixes treacherous mountain travel with a puzzle-laden dungeon crawl leading to the campaign's first major confrontation.

The Ryuseki Peaks

  • Reality Warped: Cliffs curve back on themselves, time dilates, and sudden planar rifts spew aurora-colored winds.
  • Opposition: Spectral tengu, animated basalt guardians, and lingering echoes of Soulsteel experiments challenge progress.
  • Environmental Hazards: Thin air, ice storms, and shifting gravity zones demand Constitution and Dexterity saves alongside clever spell use.

Labyrinth Highlights

  • The Blade Room: Chamber of shattered Soulsteel prototypes. Investigating reveals memories of Hideo's apprentices or grants advantage on forging-related checks.
  • Hall of Reflections: Mirror-lined hall manifesting illusions of the party's regrets. Failures produce hostile mirror doubles.
  • Chamber of Echoes: Acoustically warped arena where voices accuse and taunt. Solving the sound puzzle requires Performance or Insight.
  • Planar Distortion Nodes: Shortcuts that risk teleporting characters into side chambers haunted by yokai or free-elemental hazards.

Climactic Encounter: The Twice-Cursed Samurai

Phase 1 -- Entrance & Parley

  • Samurai appears amid crimson light, offering riddles about honor and sacrifice.
  • Dialogue seeds: "Hideo's death was a gift. Do you understand why?" / "Will you carry his burden, or break beneath it?"

Phase 2 -- Duel within the Throne Hall

  • Fractured Spirit aura: Attacks deal slashing + necrotic; failed DC 13 Charisma saves sap Charisma/Wisdom temporarily.
  • Shifting Arena:
  • Round 2: Illusions obscure line of sight (Perception DC 14).
  • Round 3: Platforms float; Athletics/Acrobatics (DC 12) to maneuver safely.
  • Ongoing: Phantom Strike (Recharge 5-6) teleports the Samurai and lashes nearby foes.
  • Challenge of Honor: Samurai marks one hero, focusing pressure and testing resolve.

Phase 3 -- Resolution Paths

  • Defeat: Samurai kneels, revealing Hideo orchestrated his own death to become his grandson's guardian spirit. Provides lore, a map fragment, or a Soulsteel shard.
  • Surrender: If convinced through honor or empathy, the Samurai yields and offers their cursed blade (powerful yet burdensome) along with reluctant cooperation.

Rewards & Fallout

  • Truth of Hideo's Sacrifice: The party learns why the funeral mattered and how the prophecy hinges on protecting the boy.
  • Labyrinth Spoils: Soulsteel fragments, planar reagents, or ritual instructions to restore corrupted shrines.
  • Continuing Threads: The Obsidian Circle's influence lingers; the Raven Yokai's omen points toward future threats in the peaks or Frostwood.

Act III should feel like the crucible that tempers the party--testing their convictions before they step into the wider politics and spiritual stakes of Shuigari.

Skill Challenge - Navigating the Living Maze of Hisui no Mori

Skill Challenge - Navigating the Living Maze of Hisui no Mori

Navigating the Living Maze of Hisui no Mori is a skill challenge tailored for level 1 characters in 5th Edition D&D, incorporating a Moderate Difficulty framework and clearer guidelines for low-level play.

The Hisui no Mori (Jade Forest) is a magical labyrinth where the paths shift like a living puzzle. To reach the forest's edge and avoid dangerous delays, the players must successfully navigate the mystical terrain using teamwork and creativity.

Challenge Setup

  • Goal: Successfully navigate the maze by achieving 4 successes before 3 failures.
  • Difficulty: Moderate (DCs 10-12 to account for low-level characters).
  • Environment: The forest shifts with illusory walls, hidden paths, and mischievous yokai.
  • Time Pressure: Optional--Add urgency by setting a 6-8 turn limit before a major storm or spiritual surge occurs.

Primary Skills

These are the most direct ways to progress through the maze. Use them to drive the narrative forward.

Survival (DC 12)

  • Purpose: Identify animal trails, spiritual disturbances, or natural landmarks.
  • Success Example: "You notice faint kodama footprints, leading toward a clearing untouched by the shifting forest."
  • Failure Example: "The tracks loop back into a dead end overgrown with thorny vines."

Perception (DC 10)

  • Purpose: Detect subtle changes in the environment, such as shimmering lights or distant sounds.
  • Success Example: "You spot faint glowing motes hovering in a line, leading toward open paths."
  • Failure Example: "You overlook an illusory wall, wasting time retracing your steps."

Arcana (DC 12)

  • Purpose: Sense and analyze magical energies shaping the maze.
  • Success Example: "The magical flow of ley lines forms a visible path where none existed."
  • Failure Example: "You misinterpret a shifting energy pattern, leading the group into a disorienting vortex."

Secondary Skills

Secondary skills offer creative or situational advantages but typically don't directly count toward success unless cleverly justified.

Insight (DC 10)

  • Purpose: Interpret signs from forest spirits or understand yokai behavior.
  • Success Example: "You recognize a bird call as a warning, avoiding a collapsing path."
  • Failure Example: "You misread the spirits' intent, angering them and causing paths to close behind you."

Nature (DC 12)

  • Purpose: Identify useful flora and fauna or safe routes based on environmental clues.
  • Success Example: "You recognize moss growing only on trees near clearings and follow the pattern."
  • Failure Example: "You mistake a toxic mushroom grove for an edible one, delaying progress as the group recovers."

Deception (DC 12) or Persuasion (DC 11)

  • Purpose: Trick or negotiate with mischievous yokai for guidance.
  • Success Example: "You convince a giggling kitsune to reveal a cryptic but useful clue."
  • Failure Example: "The yokai tricks you in return, leading the group in circles."

Complications for Failures

Introduce complications for each failure to heighten tension and consequences:

  1. Shifting Paths: "The forest twists violently, adding an extra required success to escape."
  2. Hostile Encounter: The party stumbles into a hostile creature (e.g., 1-2 Shadow Wolves or a mischievous kodama swarm). Resolve with a quick combat or roleplay encounter.
  3. Spiritual Fatigue: "The forest saps your strength. All characters suffer disadvantage on the next check unless you take a rest, losing precious time."

Completion Outcomes

Success (4 Successes Before 3 Failures)

The players navigate the maze, reaching the Ryuseki Peaks unscathed. Reward them with one or more of the following:

  • Forest Blessing: Advantage on Survival or Perception checks in forested areas for the next in-game day.
  • Kami Relic: A small magical token (e.g., a charm granting a +1 bonus to a single saving throw).
  • Narrative Advantage: Favor from a shrine fox or other spiritual being.

Failure (3 Failures Before 4 Successes)

The group becomes lost, leading to one or more of these consequences:

  • Combat Encounter: A dangerous yokai or Shadow Wolves ambush the party.
  • Exhaustion: Characters suffer a level of exhaustion.
  • Narrative Delay: The group loses valuable time, affecting other objectives.

Optional Additions

  1. Assistance Rules: Allow players to assist others by granting advantage on a roll. This consumes their action for the round and requires a narrative explanation (e.g., "I guide them through the thorny vines using my rope").
  2. Dynamic Environment: Adjust the environment after 2-3 turns to keep the challenge engaging. Example: "A sudden downpour floods low-lying paths, making Acrobatics checks necessary to avoid slipping."
  3. Random Yokai Encounters: On failures, introduce whimsical yokai that can hinder or help based on player interactions.

NPCs

Aiko Hayashi

Aiko Hayashi

Overview

A quiet, intense member of The Starcall Table gambling group, notable for being the only member who appears to be an active warrior. Her travel-worn armor suggests she's seen real combat, making her an unusual addition to a group of gamblers and merchants.

Appearance

  • Wears travel-worn armor that shows signs of use
  • Carries herself with the bearing of someone trained in combat
  • Quiet and observant demeanor
  • Intense presence despite her silence

Personality

  • Quiet and reserved, especially compared to her companions
  • Intense and focused
  • Observant - watches more than she speaks
  • Professional and composed
  • Knows her limits and when to fold

Notable Moments

During the storytelling wager between Shigeo and Kaoru Sugimoto, Aiko simply shook her head and folded without fanfare. Her quiet assessment of the situation showed the same tactical awareness she likely brings to combat - know when you're outmatched and conserve your resources.

Mysteries

  • What brings a warrior to travel with a gambling circle?
  • Is she providing security for the group, or is gambling simply another challenge she enjoys?
  • Her combat experience seems significant - what battles has she fought?
  • Why does someone who appears to be a capable fighter spend her time at card tables on the Silver Road?

Connections

  • Continues to travel with the Starcall Table

Overview

A wealthy merchant who travels alone, part of the Starcall Table gambling group encountered during the caravan journey along the Silver Road to Toriyama. Despite her understated appearance, she possesses more wealth than her companions and carries herself with effortless composure and quiet confidence.

Hidden Identity: Member of the Wild Lotus Society, a group of ghost hunters and demon slayers. Her merchant persona and gambling activities serve as cover for her supernatural investigations.## Appearance & Demeanor - Simple but elegant attire suited to someone used to refinement - Hands move gracefully, particularly when handling cards - Calm, measured speech with understated confidence that draws attention without demanding it - More refined and wealthy than she initially appears

Personality Traits

  • Appreciates stories and acts that challenge convention
  • Bold wagerer, willing to take risks
  • Competitive but gracious in defeat
  • Theatrical and dramatic in her presentations
  • Values precision and skill
  • Carries herself with quiet authority

Notable Encounters

Notable Encounters

For the full story of the Starcall Table encounter, see The Starcall Table

The Storytelling Wager (Night before the Great Stone Gate)

During a night at the Starcall Table, Shigeo wagered the Great Tortoise charm in a storytelling contest. Kaoru immediately wagered 100 gold kobans, taking the bait while others at the table folded.

The Contest: - Shigeo told the tale of Atsuko, a woman from Kagemura who defied tradition to open trade routes - a grounded, believable story of quiet perseverance - Kaoru countered with the story of Chiyo, the "Weaver of Blades" - a weaver's daughter who became a legendary warrior capable of commanding the wind itself - Shigeo won by emphasizing believability and humility over Kaoru's more fantastical tale

The Coin Trick: After conceding defeat graciously, Kaoru performed a dramatic flourish - flipping a gold koban into the air and miming a slicing motion with her hand. The coin landed on the table in two perfectly clean halves, leaving the crowd questioning whether it was sleight of hand or something more.

Her parting words: "I promise that next time, I'll not be so easily swayed. I've always liked stories with dramatic endings, haven't you?"

Abilities & Skills

  • Expert card player with remarkable dexterity
  • Possibly possesses supernatural martial abilities (the coin-splitting display)
  • Keen judge of character and situations
  • Skilled storyteller

Connections

Connections

The Starcall Table members: - Daisuke "Silver Pockets" Inoue - younger, charming gambler with silver bangles - Haruki "The Boar" Takeda - broad-shouldered, boisterous drinker - Aiko Hayashi - quiet, intense woman with travel-worn armor

For the full story of their encounter with Shigeo, see The Starcall Table

Speculation & Mysteries

  • The precision of her coin-splitting trick suggests either incredible sleight of hand or actual supernatural ability
  • Her story of Chiyo the "Weaver of Blades" may have been more autobiographical than it appeared
  • Her true wealth and purpose for traveling alone on the Silver Road remain unclear
  • Is she simply a skilled merchant, or is there more to her identity?

Campaign Notes

Campaign Notes

  • First encountered: Caravan journey to Toriyama, along the Silver Road
  • Lost 100 gold kobans to Shigeo in the storytelling wager
  • Left a strong impression on Shigeo with her theatrical display
  • Shigeo feels curiosity about whether her abilities are real or illusion
  • Arc 2: Reunited with party at the gates of Takashima, appearing as a refugee with the Starcall Table survivors from Nagano
  • Revealed membership in the Wild Lotus Society
  • Bargained party's entry into Takashima in exchange for investigating the haunted tea house
  • Her supernatural abilities (coin trick) now explained by Wild Lotus training

Kazuya

Kazuya - The Brother

Identity & Roles

Full Name: Kazuya [Family name - brother of the collections officer Iseri killed]

Multiple Identities: 1. The Vengeful Brother - Seeking revenge for Iseri's first kill 2. Akemi's Killer - Murdered Akemi Takahashi to protect secrets 3. Fox's Former Comrade - Member of Fox's assassin group/organization

The Triple Threat

Kazuya represents the convergence of three PC storylines: - Iseri's nemesis - The brother who wants revenge - Kanji's target - The one who killed Akemi - Fox's betrayer - Someone who knows Fox's true identity

Background

The Collections Officer Brother

  • Kazuya's brother was a collections officer killed by Iseri at age 19
  • The brother may have been corrupt, or simply doing his job
  • Kazuya believes his brother was murdered by a vigilante criminal
  • His quest for revenge has consumed him

The Assassin

Kazuya is (or was) part of Fox's group, which means: - He knows Fox's fighting style, weaknesses, methods - He may know Fox's real face and name - He has assassin skills comparable to Fox - He understands how Fox thinks and operates

Questions: - Is Kazuya still officially part of Fox's group? - Did he leave? Go rogue? Is he deep cover? - Does the group know what he's doing in Takashima? - Is Fox's group hunting him, or do they support his mission?

Akemi's Murder

Why Kazuya Killed Akemi: Akemi Takahashi was investigating something in Takashima - likely: 1. The vault beneath the city 2. The Oniwaban massacre 3. Circle infiltration 4. Connection between all of the above

Akemi got too close to the truth. Kazuya killed them to: - Protect the vault's location (for his own purposes) - Prevent exposure of Circle plans (if he's working with them) - Eliminate a witness to something specific - Create a "accident" that wouldn't draw attention

The Method: - Made it look like an accident (convincingly enough to fool most) - But left clues that a skilled investigator (Kanji) could find - Professional work - assassin's kill, not a crime of passion - Clean enough that authorities closed the case

Current Situation in Takashima

Position & Resources

Kazuya has established himself in Takashima with: - Wealth or position (how did he gain this?) - Intelligence network - Connections to key figures - Ability to manipulate events

Possible Covers: - Merchant guild member - Minor noble or official - Information broker - Underground network leader - Legitimate businessman with secret activities

The Orchestrator

Kazuya is setting multiple events in motion:

Against Iseri: - Arranged the troll attack on the road - Knows Iseri is traveling with a party - Plans to use the party to access the vault - Wants Iseri to suffer before dying

Using the Party: - Manipulating circumstances to drive them toward the vault - May have influenced Kaoru's "coincidental" appearance - Creating situations that force party to investigate - Intends to use them to bypass vault defenses

The Vault Plan: - Needs something from the vault (power? Artifact? Knowledge?) - Can't access it alone (needs party? Needs specific people?) - Willing to work with/manipulate Circle if necessary - Has his own agenda separate from Circle's goals

Relationship to Tenka (The Traitor Oniwaban)

Kazuya and Tenka are counterparts - parallel but separate villains:

Similarities: - Both betrayed their "families" (Fox's group / Oniwaban clan) - Both serve their own agendas while appearing to serve others - Both have specialized combat skills - Both want access to the vault - Both are manipulating the party

Differences: - Kazuya is driven by personal revenge (brother's death) - Tenka was driven by [to be determined - survival? Ambition? Corruption?] - Kazuya kills to protect secrets - Tenka killed to gain secrets

Potential Alliance: Do Kazuya and Tenka work together? Options: 1. Yes - They're allied, making them more dangerous 2. No - They're rivals, which party could exploit 3. Complicated - They use each other but don't trust each other 4. Unknown - One doesn't know the other exists yet

Connection to Fox's Group

The Revelation

When Fox discovers Kazuya is in Takashima, multiple revelations hit:

  1. Someone from home - First person from Fox's past to appear
  2. He knows who Fox really is - Under the mask
  3. He's Akemi's killer - This means Fox's group is involved somehow
  4. He might expose Fox - To the party, to authorities, to enemies

The Questions

About Fox's Group: - What is this organization? (Name, purpose, structure) - Are they good, evil, or morally gray? - Why was Fox part of them? - Does Fox want to return, or are they running away?

About Kazuya's Standing: - Did the group send Kazuya to Takashima? - Is he rogue/expelled for killing Akemi? - Does the group know about his revenge quest? - Will other members arrive looking for Fox or Kazuya?

About Fox's Position: - Does Fox still consider themselves part of the group? - Will Fox defend Kazuya to the party despite everything? - Must Fox choose between old loyalty and new friends? - Can Fox kill a former brother-in-arms?

Combat Capabilities

As an assassin from Fox's group:

Skills: - Stealth and infiltration - Poison expertise - Intelligence gathering - Social manipulation - Close-quarters combat - Tactical planning

Advantages Over Party: - Knows Fox's abilities and counters them - Has observed Iseri's vigilante patterns - Professional killer vs. brawlers and adventurers - Prepared battlefield, chooses when/where to fight - Resources and backup in Takashima

Weaknesses: - Emotional (revenge-driven, not purely rational) - Arrogant (believes he's smarter than the party) - Divided attention (multiple plots/enemies) - Potential exposure (the more he acts, the more clues he leaves)

Personality & Motivation

The Mask of Civility

In public, Kazuya is: - Charming and sophisticated - Appears reasonable and cultured - Hides his rage behind etiquette - Uses politics and manipulation over obvious force

The Core of Rage

Underneath, Kazuya is: - Consumed by need for revenge against Iseri - Ruthless in eliminating obstacles (like Akemi) - Willing to use anyone (including Fox, his former ally) - Convinced his cause is just

The Professional

Despite emotion, Kazuya remains: - Calculating and patient - Willing to wait for perfect moment - Adaptive when plans change - Skilled at reading people and situations

Key Scenes to Plan

Scene 1: First Appearance

When/how does the party first encounter Kazuya? - Social gathering? (He's established, respectable) - Suspicious encounter? (They don't know who he is yet) - Through investigation? (Following Akemi's trail) - Dramatic reveal? (At a crucial moment)

Scene 2: Fox's Recognition

Fox recognizes Kazuya (or vice versa): - Does Fox tell the party immediately? - Does Kazuya threaten to expose Fox? - Do they speak privately first? - What secrets are exchanged?

Scene 3: Kanji Discovers the Truth

Kanji's investigation leads to Kazuya: - Direct evidence? Witness testimony? Confession? - Does Kazuya admit it? Deny it? Justify it? - Is Fox present? How do they react? - Can Kanji restrain themselves?

Scene 4: Iseri's Confrontation

When Iseri learns who Kazuya is: - Does Kazuya monologue about the brother? - Does he present "evidence" of the brother's innocence? - Does he offer Iseri a choice? (Your life for theirs?) - How does the party respond?

Scene 5: The Vault Gambit

Kazuya's endgame at the vault: - Does he arrive first? Follow the party? - Does he have hostages? Leverage? - Is he working with Tenka at this point? - What does he actually want from the vault?

Scene 6: Final Resolution

Multiple possibilities: - Death - Killed by Iseri, Kanji, Fox, or party - Arrest - Captured and handed to authorities - Escape - Gets away to return another day - Redemption? - Learns truth about his brother? Unlikely but possible - Sacrifice - Dies stopping greater threat (Tenka? Circle?)

Unanswered Questions

  1. What exactly does Kazuya want from the vault?

  2. Power to kill Iseri perfectly? Artifact? Knowledge? Revenge is the surface motive - what's deeper?

  3. How much does he know about the vault?

  4. Everything? Fragments? Wrong information?

  5. Is he working with the Obsidian Circle?

  6. Willing member? Unwitting pawn? Using them? Being used?

  7. What is Fox's assassin group called?

  8. And what is its purpose/philosophy?

  9. Why did Kazuya kill Akemi personally?

  10. Could have hired it done. Why risk getting hands dirty?

  11. Does he know about Fox's false memories?

  12. If so, does he know they contain vault information?

  13. What was his relationship with Fox specifically?

  14. Friends? Rivals? Master/student? Equals?

  15. How did his brother really die?

  16. Was Iseri's kill justified? Was the brother corrupt? Or innocent?

  17. What would make Kazuya stop?

  18. Proof brother deserved it? Greater threat? Nothing?

  19. What happens to Fox's group after this?

    • Will they come looking for Fox or Kazuya?

Connection to Other NPCs

Tenka (The Traitor Oniwaban)

  • Do they work together? Against each other? Unaware of each other?
  • Both want vault access - conflict or cooperation?
  • Could party play them against each other?

Kaoru (Wild Lotus Society)

  • Does Kaoru know about Kazuya?
  • Is Wild Lotus investigating him?
  • Did he manipulate Kaoru's "coincidental" meeting with party?

The Twice Cursed Samurai

  • Is there a connection?
  • Did Kazuya disturb/involve the samurai somehow?
  • Does the samurai know about Kazuya's crimes?

Master Hideo's Grandson

  • Does Kazuya know about the "blood key"?
  • Is the grandson in danger from Kazuya?
  • Has Kazuya already approached/manipulated him?

Character Stats/Build

[To be determined based on party level and desired challenge]

Suggested Level: CR 7-9 (matching or slightly exceeding party)

Archetype: Assassin Rogue / Shadow Monk multiclass

Key Abilities: - High DEX and INT - Expertise in Stealth, Deception, Insight - Poison mastery - Shadow Step or similar teleportation - Sneak Attack damage - Stunning Strike - Patient Defense

Signature Moves: - Brother's Vengeance - Enhanced attack against Iseri specifically - Assassin's Mark - Knows Fox's patterns, advantage against them - Shadow Kill - How he murdered Akemi (leaves no trace) - Information Network - Can call for backup/intelligence in Takashima

Motivations & Philosophy

Surface Motivation: Revenge for brother's death

Deeper Truth: [Choose one or combine] 1. Guilt - Feels responsible for brother's death (should have protected him) 2. Identity - Revenge gives him purpose; without it, he's nothing 3. Justice - Genuinely believes Iseri is a criminal who must pay 4. Power - Revenge is excuse; really wants vault's contents 5. Duty - Promised brother/mother/someone he'd make this right

Philosophy: "Justice without law is just revenge. Revenge without purpose is just murder. I have both law and purpose."

Or perhaps: "You took someone precious from me. Now I'll take everything precious from you - your friends, your hope, your life. And only then will we be even."

Potential Redemption Path

If the GM wants to offer possibility of redemption:

What Would It Take: 1. Learn brother was corrupt - Undeniable proof the kill was justified 2. Face greater evil - Something worse than Iseri threatens everything 3. Fox's testimony - His former comrade convinces him 4. Akemi's forgiveness - If Akemi somehow isn't dead, or ghost/message 5. Iseri's sacrifice - Iseri offers to die to save Kazuya from himself

Would He Accept It: Probably not. But the option creates dramatic tension.

Cost of Redemption: - Turn on Circle/Tenka - Give up revenge - Help party stop vault crisis - Face justice for Akemi's murder - Lose everything he's built in Takashima

Kazuya is designed to be personal antagonist for THREE PCs simultaneously while tying into the larger vault conspiracy. His multi-layered threat makes him a significant Arc 2 villain worthy of the build-up.

Tenka

Tenka - The Last Oniwaban (Traitor)

Identity & Title

Name: Tenka
Title: The Last Oniwaban (alongside Aoshi, though he lost the right to the name)
Other Names: The Traitor, The Fallen Guardian, The One Who Broke

The Betrayal

What He Did

Tenka betrayed the Oniwaban clan to the Obsidian Circle, leading to: - The systematic massacre of the entire clan - The exposure of clan secrets and techniques - The loss of the vault's primary guardians - The death of everyone Aoshi knew and loved

Why He Survived

Tenka is the only Oniwaban besides Aoshi to survive the massacre because: - He orchestrated it - He gave the Circle the information they needed - He stood aside (or participated) while his brothers and sisters died - He earned his life through betrayal

Current Status

In Takashima

Tenka is currently in Takashima, positioned to: - Guard the vault for the Circle (or himself) - Prevent others from accessing it - Eliminate Aoshi if they appear - Serve his own mysterious agenda

Position & Cover

[To be determined - options:] - Official Position: Guard captain? City official? Military officer? - Criminal Underground: Enforcer? Shadow guild master? - Circle Agent: Open member? Deep cover operative? - Independent: Serving only himself, using Circle resources?

Relationship to Kazuya

Tenka and Kazuya are counterparts - parallel villains who serve as mirrors:

The Duality: - Tenka: Traitor to clan/family for [reason] - Kazuya: Traitor to assassin brotherhood for revenge

Potential Dynamic: 1. Allied - Work together to access vault 2. Rivals - Competing for vault's contents 3. Uneasy Partners - Use each other but don't trust 4. Unaware - Don't know about each other initially

The Mirror: Both villains force their PC counterparts to confront betrayal: - Aoshi must face Tenka (clan betrayer) - Fox must face Kazuya (brotherhood betrayer) - Both PCs must decide: Kill? Redeem? Understand?

The Why - Motivation for Betrayal

Possible Reasons (Choose one or combine):

Option 1: Corrupted by Shindarasu

  • Exposed to corruption through vault duty
  • Shindarasu whispered promises of power
  • Memory manipulation made him believe betrayal was right path
  • Wasn't fully willing - corrupted over time

Pros: Offers redemption possibility, ties to main villain Cons: Reduces personal agency, might feel like excuse

Option 2: Ambition & Power

  • Wanted power/knowledge the clan kept from him
  • Believed Oniwaban way was outdated/wrong
  • Circle offered what clan wouldn't
  • Fully willing and intentional

Pros: Clear villain, no moral ambiguity Cons: Less complex, harder to make sympathetic

Option 3: Survival & Cowardice

  • Circle threatened him specifically
  • Chose his life over clan's
  • Regrets it now but can't undo it
  • Living in guilt and self-hatred

Pros: Tragic villain, redemption possible Cons: Makes him weaker, less threatening

Option 4: Philosophical Disagreement

  • Believed vault should be used, not guarded
  • Thought Oniwaban secrecy was wrong
  • Genuinely believes Circle's goals are right
  • Willing traitor for "greater good"

Pros: Makes him ideological threat Cons: Requires fleshing out Circle philosophy

Option 5: Protecting Someone/Something

  • Circle held leverage over someone he loved
  • Had to betray clan to save [person/place/thing]
  • Still believes it was right choice
  • Would do it again

Pros: Complex motivations, moral gray area Cons: Requires developing the leverage

Option 6: The Visions Made Him Do It

  • Shikigo or Oni Babamon spoke to him first
  • Visions told him to betray the clan
  • Believes he's following divine will
  • Aoshi's visions are the same source

Pros: Ties to Aoshi's storyline directly Cons: Makes visions purely evil (removes ambiguity)

Relationship to Aoshi

Before the Betrayal

Who Was Tenka to Aoshi? (Choose one - most painful option)

  1. Aoshi's Mentor/Teacher
  2. Trained Aoshi in Oniwaban ways
  3. Father figure or respected elder

  4. Betrayal hits hardest: "You taught me everything"

  5. Aoshi's Brother/Sister (Blood or Sworn)

  6. Closest bond in the clan
  7. Grew up together, fought together

  8. Betrayal hits hardest: "We were family"

  9. Aoshi's Rival

  10. Competed for position/respect
  11. Push each other to improve

  12. Betrayal hits hardest: "I trusted you to be better"

  13. Aoshi's Best Friend

  14. Shared everything, no secrets
  15. Complete trust and loyalty

  16. Betrayal hits hardest: "I would have died for you"

  17. Aoshi's Former Love

  18. Romantic relationship (failed or hidden)
  19. Complicated by duty and tradition
  20. Betrayal hits hardest: "I loved you"

The Confrontation

When Aoshi and Tenka finally meet:

Tenka's Perspective: - "I did what I had to do" - "You don't understand the burden" - "The clan was already dying" - "I'm not your enemy" - "Join me, or die like the rest"

Aoshi's Perspective: - "You killed everyone" - "You betrayed everything we stood for" - "I trusted you" - "Give me one reason not to kill you now" - "The clan dies with us - there's no coming back"

Combat Capabilities

Oniwaban Techniques

As a former guardian, Tenka possesses: - All traditional Oniwaban combat arts - Oni-enhanced strength/abilities - Vault-specific knowledge and counters - Decades of experience

Advantages Over Aoshi

  • Experience: Older, more battles fought
  • Knowledge: Knows Aoshi's training (he may have trained them)
  • Preparation: Expects Aoshi might come
  • Resources: Circle backing, equipment, position
  • Ruthlessness: No moral limits anymore

Aoshi's Advantages

  • Righteousness: Fighting for fallen clan
  • Purity: Untainted by corruption (yet)
  • Hunger: Needs this more than Tenka does
  • Allies: Has the party backing them
  • Youth: Possibly younger, faster (if Tenka is older)

Signature Abilities

Oniwaban Secret Arts: - Oni's Wrath: Enhanced strength from oni heritage - Shadow Guardian Form: Defensive kata from vault duty - Ancestral Techniques: Clan-specific martial arts - Vault Walker: Knows vault layout and traps

Corrupted/Enhanced by Circle: - Tsurogami's Blessing: Additional power from the Woven Tyrant - Memory Theft: Can steal techniques by observing them - Shadow Step: Teleportation through shadows - Soulsteel Weapon: May wield corrupted Oniwaban blade

Connection to the Vault

Guardian Turned Infiltrator

Tenka knows: - All vault entrances (hidden and obvious) - Trap locations and how to disarm them - What seals protect what chambers - What treasures/secrets are inside - How to use the vault's power

The Obsidian Circle's Key

The Circle needed Tenka because: - Only Oniwaban could pass certain wards - Oni blood required to access some areas - Guardian knowledge irreplaceable - Traditional guardians would never cooperate

Current Role

Is Tenka: - Still working for Circle: Actively helping them - Playing both sides: Using Circle while pursuing own goals - Trapped: Can't escape Circle's hold - Regretting: Wants to undo what he's done - Independent: Used Circle, now working alone

The Shikigo/Oni Babamon Connection

Are the Visions Related?

Possibility 1: Same Source, Different Messages - Shikigo speaks to both Aoshi and Tenka - Gave Tenka one path (betrayal) - Giving Aoshi different path (redemption?) - Testing both to see who succeeds

Possibility 2: Opposing Forces - Shikigo guides Aoshi (true guardian spirit) - Oni Babamon corrupted Tenka (false/evil entity) - The vision conflict represents larger cosmic struggle - Aoshi must reject false visions to succeed

Possibility 3: Tenka Never Had Visions - He's lying about divine guidance - Using it as justification/excuse - Trying to confuse/corrupt Aoshi - The visions are unique to Aoshi

Possibility 4: Corruption of True Visions - Tenka received real visions but misinterpreted them - Circle's corruption twisted his understanding - Shindarasu interfered with the message - Aoshi risks the same corruption

Questions for Aoshi

When Tenka claims to have received the same visions: - Does Aoshi believe him? - Does this make Aoshi question their own visions? - Are the visions trustworthy at all? - What if Tenka is right?

Key Scenes to Plan

Scene 1: The Revelation

How does Aoshi learn Tenka is alive and in Takashima? - Evidence in investigation? - Direct encounter? - Someone tells them? - Recognizes Oniwaban technique in combat?

Scene 2: First Confrontation

Their first meeting face-to-face: - Combat immediately or talk first? - Private or with witnesses? - Does Tenka explain himself? - Can others stop them from killing each other?

Scene 3: The Truth Unveiled

Tenka's reasons are revealed: - Full confession? - Pieced together evidence? - Deathbed revelation? - Never fully explained?

Scene 4: At the Vault

When both Oniwaban are at the vault: - Do they work together against greater threat? - Fight each other while crisis unfolds? - Forced to use their connection to save others? - Guardian techniques required - only they know them?

Scene 5: Final Resolution

How does Tenka's story end? - Death by Aoshi: Justice for the clan - Death by Sacrifice: Redeems himself saving others - Captured: Lives but imprisoned/exiled - Redeemed: Joins party/becomes ally - Escapes: Survives for future arc - Consumed by Corruption: Becomes monster, must be put down

Scene 6: Aoshi's Choice

The moment that defines Aoshi: - Kill Tenka in revenge? - Spare him and risk more betrayal? - Understand his reasons? - Forgive the unforgivable? - Continue the cycle or break it?

Personality & Behavior

Surface Presentation

How Tenka appears to others in Takashima: - [Dignified? Haunted? Cold? Efficient?] - [Respected? Feared? Pitied? Unknown?] - [Obvious villain or hidden in plain sight?]

With Aoshi

When confronting the last of his clan: - Remorseful? Defiant? Nostalgic? Angry? - Does he want Aoshi's forgiveness? - Does he want Aoshi to join him? - Does he want Aoshi to kill him? - Does he want Aoshi to understand?

True Self

Beneath all masks: - Does he regret what he did? - Does he believe it was necessary? - Is he consumed by guilt or free of it? - Has corruption changed who he was? - Is there anything left of the guardian he was?

Unanswered Questions

  1. What is Tenka's exact relationship to Aoshi?

  2. Choose the most painful option for maximum impact

  3. Why did he betray the clan?

  4. This answer defines whether redemption is possible

  5. Where was Aoshi when the massacre happened?

  6. Does Tenka know Aoshi survived? Did he ensure it? Try to prevent it?

  9. Is he working with Kazuya?

  10. Allied, rivals, or unaware of each other?

  11. Did he have a choice?

  12. Was betrayal truly the only option, or does he tell himself that?

  13. Does he know about Aoshi's visions?

  16. Or has corruption/betrayal cost him some abilities?

  19. What would make him switch sides?

    • Threat to something he still cares about? Proof Circle lied? Nothing?

Integration with Other Storylines

Fox's False Memories

Do Fox's implanted memories contain information about: - The Oniwaban massacre? - Tenka's betrayal? - Vault defenses the Oniwaban protected? - How to contact/find Tenka?

Yasei's Hikari

Is Tenka aware that: - Hikari is fading? - The Oniwaban protected Hikari's portal? - His betrayal contributed to Hikari's weakening? - Deep Village suffered because of him?

Thornbringer's Quest

Does Tenka know: - The Well's true nature and location? - The One Tree's connection to vault? - How to save or destroy them? - Fox-kami's relationship to the vault?

Kanji's Investigation

Does Tenka's presence relate to: - Akemi's death? (Did Akemi investigate Oniwaban massacre?) - Kazuya's plans? - The tea house haunting?

Iseri's Story

Is there any connection between: - Tenka and Kazuya's alliance? - Oniwaban and the assassin brotherhood? - Guardian duty and vigilante justice?

Potential Redemption Arc

If redemption is possible, what would it require?

Stage 1: Recognition - Tenka must acknowledge what he did was wrong - Not just for survival or pragmatism - actually wrong - Face the weight of all those deaths

Stage 2: Truth - Reveal his true motivations honestly - No more lies, no more justifications - Accept Aoshi's (and party's) judgment

Stage 3: Atonement - Active steps to undo damage - Help stop Circle's vault plan - Restore Oniwaban honor somehow - Probably requires sacrifice

Stage 4: Acceptance - Even if redeemed, can never be Oniwaban again - Must live with what he did - Aoshi may never forgive him - Some sins leave permanent scars

Stage 5: New Purpose - If he survives, what does he do? - Become new guardian (elsewhere)? - Serve Aoshi's mission? - Wandering ronin seeking redemption? - Death may be the only true atonement

Character Build/Stats

[To be determined based on party level]

Suggested Level: CR 8-10 (elite difficulty for Aoshi's personal boss)

Archetype: Way of Shadow Monk / Fighter (Battle Master or Samurai)

Key Abilities: - High DEX, WIS, CON - Expertise in Stealth, Perception, Athletics - Oni racial traits (advantage on STR checks, darkvision, etc.) - Shadow Step, Pass Without Trace - Action Surge, Extra Attack (2-3) - Martial Arts die scaling - Stunning Strike - Defensive abilities (Patient Defense, Deflect Missiles)

Signature Moves: - Oniwaban Secret Technique: [Name] - Clan-specific ability - Traitor's Advantage - Knows how Aoshi fights - Vault Guardian's Ward - Defensive technique from protection duty - Oni's Heritage: [Name] - Racial power enhanced by training - Shadow of Betrayal - Corruption-enhanced ability

Legendary Actions (if appropriate): - Move without provoking opportunity attacks - Stunning Strike additional target - Defensive stance granting resistance

Philosophy & Dialogue

Sample Quotes:

On the Betrayal: "You think I wanted this? I carried that burden every day. But someone had to make the hard choice."

On the Visions: "Shikigo showed me the same path it's showing you now. Do you have the strength to see it through?"

On Aoshi Surviving: "I made sure you weren't there that night. If nothing else, let that mean something."

On Redemption: "There is no redemption for what I've done. Only consequences. And I've been running from them for too long."

On the Clan: "The Oniwaban were already dead. I just accepted it before you did."

On the Vault: "We swore to guard it with our lives. I chose to guard it with their lives instead. That's the difference between us."

Tenka is designed as Aoshi's ultimate test - the living embodiment of betrayal, the last connection to the fallen clan, and the choice between vengeance and understanding. His resolution will define what kind of Oniwaban Aoshi chooses to be.
