Towns of Shugane

Towns of Shugane

The various towns of Shugane each have their own unique character, role, and strategic importance. Spread across the main island, these settlements serve as vital hubs of commerce, defense, and culture, connecting the larger cities with the rural villages. Below is an overview of the twelve major towns of Shugane, each contributing to the prosperity and stability of the Shogunate in its own way.

Takayama (River Town, Central Plains)

  • Population: 7,500
  • Defenses: Takayama is surrounded by stone walls and guarded by a well-trained militia of around 300 soldiers. The town's position along the river makes it vulnerable to waterborne assaults, but watchtowers along the riverbanks provide early warnings of any incursions.
  • Commerce: The town is a major trade hub for goods transported via the river. Local industries include rice milling, textiles, and the production of fine ceramics, which are exported to nearby cities.
  • Organizations: The Takayama Trade Guild regulates the flow of goods and ensures fair trade practices, while the Brotherhood of the Silver Eel manages the town's river transport operations.

Yokosuka (Fishing Town, Eastern Coast)

  • Population: 4,200
  • Defenses: Yokosuka is fortified with wooden palisades and a small naval garrison of 100 soldiers. The town also maintains a fleet of 20 fishing boats that can be converted into makeshift patrol vessels if needed.
  • Commerce: The town's primary industry is fishing, known for its high-quality seafood, including salt-cured fish and dried seaweed. Yokosuka also supplies fish oil, used both for cooking and as a base component in alchemical mixtures.
  • Organizations: The Yokosuka Fishermen's Union wields significant influence, overseeing both the town's economic and political affairs. A small shrine dedicated to the Sea Kami, Kuraokami, protects sailors and fishermen.

Koganei (Castle Town, Southern Plains)

  • Population: 9,800
  • Defenses: Dominated by a large castle perched atop a hill, Koganei is heavily defended with stone walls, reinforced gates, and a standing garrison of 500 samurai. The castle serves as a key military outpost for the southern plains.
  • Commerce: The town's economy revolves around providing arms and armor for the Shogunate's forces. Blacksmiths, fletchers, and armorers are abundant, and Koganei is known for producing high-quality weapons.
  • Organizations: The Order of the Iron Hawk, a local samurai order, protects the town and its lord. The Koganei Armorer's Guild controls the production of weapons and armor.

Miyako (Port Town, Southwestern Coast)

  • Population: 6,300
  • Defenses: Surrounded by a high wooden palisade and guarded by a small naval detachment, Miyako has 150 soldiers stationed at its docks. A watchtower on the cliffs provides a vantage point for spotting approaching ships.
  • Commerce: As a port town, Miyako thrives on trade and fishing. It exports seafood, pearls, and coral, while importing luxury goods from other parts of Shuigari.
  • Organizations: The Miyako Merchant League governs all trade passing through the port, while the Mariners' Brotherhood protects sailors and ensures that Miyako's ships are well maintained.

Tsubasa (Mountain Town, Celestial Spine)

  • Population: 3,200
  • Defenses: Tsubasa is strategically located at a mountain pass, making it easily defensible with a small garrison of 200 warriors. The town is protected by natural rock formations and fortified barricades.
  • Commerce: Known for its production of rare minerals and precious gems, Tsubasa's miners extract valuable resources from the surrounding mountains. The town also produces enchanted jewelry and ceremonial weapons.
  • Organizations: The Tsubasa Miners' Guild controls the gem trade, while the Society of the Celestial Anvil manages the production of enchanted items.

Futaba (Fortified Town, Northern Hills)

  • Population: 8,400
  • Defenses: Futaba is a heavily fortified town, encircled by high stone walls and guarded by 400 soldiers. Its elevated position in the hills makes it a strong defensive position against potential incursions from the northern border.
  • Commerce: The town's primary industries include horse breeding and leatherworking. Futaba's horses are highly prized by the samurai for their endurance and speed.
  • Organizations: The House of the Golden Spur oversees the breeding and training of horses, while the Futaba Leatherworkers' Guild supplies armor and saddles to the Shogunate's armies.

Kameno (Market Town, Central Plains)

  • Population: 5,700
  • Defenses: Kameno is lightly defended, with only 100 town guards, relying on its strong trade connections for protection. The town has a modest stone wall and a central watchtower.
  • Commerce: Known as the "Merchant's Crossroads," Kameno is a bustling market town where goods from all over Shugane are traded. The town hosts a monthly fair that draws traders from across the island.
  • Organizations: The Kameno Trade Consortium controls the town's markets, and the Wayfarer's Lodge provides services and accommodations to traveling merchants.

Shinami (Fishing Town, Northeastern Coast)

  • Population: 3,900
  • Defenses: Shinami has basic fortifications, with wooden palisades and 80 town guards. A small fleet of fast coastal skiffs patrols the waters, protecting the town from raiders.
  • Commerce: Primarily a fishing community, Shinami is known for its smoked fish and shellfish. It also supplies fine seaweed and kelp used in various culinary and alchemical recipes.
  • Organizations: The Shinami Fishermen's Guild manages the town's fishing rights, and the Tidecaller's Circle performs rituals to honor the sea spirits.

Kawagata (River Town, Southern Plains)

  • Population: 4,800
  • Defenses: Kawagata has modest defenses, with a small wooden palisade and 150 town guards. Its position along the river makes it an important checkpoint for waterborne trade.
  • Commerce: The town is known for its rice production and river trade. It serves as a collection point for goods transported downstream to the larger cities.
  • Organizations: The Kawagata Rice Merchants' Guild controls the flow of grain, while the River Wardens ensure safe passage for trade barges.

Oda (Forest Town, Northern Edge)

  • Population: 3,500
  • Defenses: Oda is lightly fortified with wooden barricades and a small militia of 100 archers. The dense forests around the town provide natural protection.
  • Commerce: The town specializes in logging and the production of high-quality lumber. It also harvests rare herbs from the forest, used in various healing salves and potions.
  • Organizations: The Oda Foresters' Guild manages the logging operations, while the Circle of Verdant Spirits ensures sustainable harvesting practices.

Izanami (Monastery Town, Central Hills)

  • Population: 2,800
  • Defenses: Izanami is protected by a monastery militia of 150 warrior monks. The town is built around a central temple complex and is surrounded by stone walls adorned with spiritual wards.
  • Commerce: The town serves as a center for spiritual learning and pilgrimage. Its main exports include spiritual charms, herbal medicines, and sacred texts.
  • Organizations: The Brotherhood of the Sacred Flame manages the temple, while the Order of Tranquil Waters trains monks in both martial and spiritual arts.

Torihana (Border Town, Southern Coastline)

  • Population: 6,100
  • Defenses: Torihana is heavily fortified, with thick stone walls and a garrison of 300 soldiers. Its position as a border town makes it a critical defensive outpost against incursions from rival territories.
  • Commerce: The town is known for its production of salt and dried fish. Torihana also serves as a trade hub for goods entering Shugane from the southern isles.
  • Organizations: The Torihana Guard maintains the town's defenses, while the Saltmaster's Guild oversees the salt production and trade.

Worldbuilding

Akane Hiroshi

Akane Hiroshi

Role: Bodyguard and trusted lieutenant to Lord Ichiro Kagemura.

Appearance: A lithe woman in lacquered green-and-silver armor, with a calm but calculating demeanor. She carries a yari (spear) and a wakizashi.

Personality: Loyal and pragmatic, Akane quietly observes the mourners, looking for potential threats or political opportunities.

Notable Action: During the funeral, she keeps close to Kagemura but occasionally exchanges meaningful glances with Hiroto Masanori, hinting at an unspoken rivalry or shared history tied to Lady Hana's retinue.

The Rivalry between Akane and Masanori

  1. Shared History:
  2. Masanori and Akane were once sparring partners in their youth, both serving rival lords in the same region.
  3. During a skirmish, Akane defeated Masanori and left him humiliated. Worse, her intervention contributed to his lord's downfall, marking the beginning of Masanori's fall from grace.
  4. Masanori holds Akane responsible for his current status as a ronin-turned-retainer.

Arc 2 Master Plot Framework

Arc 2 Master Plot Framework

Core Concept

Arc 2 weaves together all PC backstories into a single interconnected conspiracy centered on Takashima, the Obsidian Circle's infiltration, and the hidden vault beneath the city containing the Well of Life and the One Tree.

The Central Mystery: The Vault Beneath Takashima

What It Is

A massive underground complex beneath Takashima containing: - The Well of Life - Ancient source of natural power - The One Tree - Primordial entity, currently as a seedling/sapling - Hikari's Light - A planar opening to the Radiant Realm providing everliving sunlight - Oniwaban Archives - Records of the fallen clan (before Circle destroyed them) - Ancient Seals - Protection and binding magic

The Ticking Clock

Hikari is fading. The planar opening to the Radiant Realm is closing, which means: - The One Tree is dying without its sunlight - The Well of Life is losing power - The vault's protections are weakening - The Obsidian Circle can finally access what's been hidden - Timeline: Unknown but urgent - When does Hikari close completely?

Why It Matters

  • Thornbringer: The Well and Tree are their quest
  • Yasei: Hikari's light sustains their village's connection to the kami
  • Aoshi: The Oniwaban were the vault's guardians
  • Fox: False memories contain vault location and Oniwaban secrets
  • Kanji: Akemi died protecting (or trying to access?) something connected to this
  • Iseri: The brother's revenge plot uses the vault as leverage

Individual Storylines

Kanji: Akemi's Accident

The Truth About Akemi Takahashi: Akemi was investigating something in Takashima when the "accident" occurred. This wasn't random - it was connected to the vault.

Possible Scenarios: 1. Akemi discovered the vault entrance and was killed by Circle agents to silence them 2. Akemi was trying to access the vault for their own reasons and triggered defenses 3. Akemi was working with/for someone trying to find the vault (Circle? Rival faction? Good intentions gone wrong?) 4. The accident was orchestrated to look like an accident, but was murder

Investigation Path: - Kanji arrives in Takashima and discovers Akemi's death wasn't an accident - Witnesses who saw something but were silenced or paid off - Akemi's belongings/notes that point toward the vault - Evidence that the Circle or another faction was involved - Climax: Kanji must choose - revenge or truth? Personal closure or stopping the conspiracy?

Complications: - What if Akemi wasn't innocent? What if they were Circle? - What if the person who killed Akemi had good reasons? - What if Kanji has to work with Akemi's killer to stop something worse?

Resolution Options: - Confront Akemi's killer (NPC to be determined) - Expose the conspiracy that caused the death - Complete what Akemi started - Choose to let go and focus on preventing more deaths

Thornbringer: The Well + The One Tree

The Discovery: Fox's false memories (when properly interpreted) reveal the vault's location beneath Takashima. Thornbringer's quest leads directly here.

The Situation: - The One Tree seedling/sapling is dying as Hikari's light fades - The Well of Life is losing potency - Without intervention, both will be lost forever - The Circle wants to corrupt the Tree or drain the Well

The Choice: Thornbringer must decide what to do with the Well and Tree: 1. Restore Hikari's light - But how? What's the cost? 2. Relocate the Tree - Can it survive the move? Where would it go? 3. Let nature take its course - Is death part of the cycle? 4. Sacrifice something personal - To save the Tree, what must Thornbringer give up?

Fox-Kami Connection: - Fox-kami DO know about the Well - they've been guarding the secret - They'll help Thornbringer but demand a price - Perhaps fox-kami are connected to the Radiant Realm portal - They may know how to restore Hikari's light

The Druid's Dilemma: - Saving the Tree may require urban destruction (vault is under the city) - The Circle's corruption has reached the Tree's roots - Natural death vs. artificial preservation - which honors nature? - The Well's power could save thousands - or corrupt them all

Aoshi: The Fall of the Oniwaban

The Massacre: The Oniwaban clan was systematically eliminated by the Obsidian Circle. This wasn't random violence - it was targeted assassination to: - Remove the vault's guardians - Steal their knowledge - Access what they protected - Eliminate those who could stop the Circle

Aoshi's Survivor's Guilt: Aoshi is the "Last Oniwaban" because: - They weren't there when it happened (away on duty? Exiled? Training?) - Or they were there but survived (hidden? presumed dead? betrayed?) - The weight: Everyone died. Aoshi lives. Why?

The Traitor: One Oniwaban survived by betraying the clan. This traitor: - Is in Takashima - Working with or manipulated by the Circle - Knows Aoshi survived - Will either try to kill them or recruit them - Has Oniwaban techniques and knowledge - Making them extremely dangerous - May not be fully willing - Blackmail? Corruption? False memories? Mind control?

Possible Traitor Identities: - Aoshi's mentor/teacher (most painful) - Aoshi's sibling/relative (blood betrayal) - Aoshi's former rival within the clan (jealousy/ambition) - Aoshi's closest friend (broken bonds)

The Confrontation: Aoshi must face the traitor and decide: 1. Kill them - Justice for the fallen clan 2. Redeem them - If they were corrupted/controlled, can they be saved? 3. Understand them - Were their reasons justifiable? 4. Join them - Could Aoshi be convinced the betrayal was necessary?

Connection to Visions: - Shikigo may be the ancestral spirit warning about the traitor - Oni Babamon may be connected to the Circle's corruption - The visions are trying to guide Aoshi to prevent total Oniwaban extinction - OR the visions are corrupted attempts to manipulate Aoshi into the Circle

The Vault's Guardians: The Oniwaban were guardians of the vault because: - Their oni heritage made them resistant to the Well's power - They took oaths to protect the One Tree - They were bound to the Radiant light of Hikari - Their destruction was necessary for the Circle to access the vault

Fox: False Memories Unlock Truth

The Cruel Irony: Fox's false memories of "Kenshin" actually contain REAL information hidden by Shindarasu: - Location of the vault - Details of the Oniwaban massacre - The traitor's identity - How to access the sealed chambers

How This Works: Shindarasu implanted false personal memories (Kenshin the brother) but had to hide them in REAL historical memories (Oniwaban massacre, vault location). When Fox unravels the false memories, they discover: - Kenshin never existed - But the "places we went together" are real locations - The "conversations we had" contain real information - The "secrets Kenshin knew" are actual Circle intelligence

The Painful Process: To extract the truth, Fox must: 1. Accept Kenshin is fake - Let go emotionally 2. Analyze the false memories clinically - Treat them as data 3. Separate real from false - What locations/people/events are real? 4. Risk further corruption - Diving into false memories may deepen their hold

What Fox Discovers: - The exact location of the vault entrance - The Oniwaban were massacred by the Circle (witnessed it?) - The traitor's identity and current location - Master Hideo's connection to all of this - Why Fox specifically was targeted for these false memories

The Question: Why did Shindarasu give Fox these specific false memories? Options: 1. Accident - Real information leaked into false memories unintentionally 2. Test - Seeing if Fox is clever enough to extract truth from lies 3. Bait - Leading Fox (and party) to the vault for Circle purposes 4. Sabotage - Another Circle faction trying to expose secrets

Master Hideo Connection: Fox's relationship to Master Hideo ties into this: - Hideo knew about the vault (his grandson is "the blood key") - Hideo may have known about the Oniwaban massacre - Hideo protected Fox somehow (gave them the knowledge in hidden form?) - Fox's memories of Hideo might also be partially false - how much is real?

Yasei: Hikari Fading

The Connection: The Deep Village of Hikari is spiritually connected to the Radiant Realm portal beneath Takashima. As Hikari fades: - The village loses kami connection - Spiritual protection fails - Vulnerability to attack increases - The people weaken and die

The Timeline: - Past: Hikari's light was strong, village thrived, kami answered - Recent: Light began fading, kami grew quiet, Yora-no-kiba attacked - Now: Village in ruins, kami silent, Yasei in Takashima where the source of Hikari is located - Future: If portal closes completely, any survivors will die

The Revelation: Yasei discovers that their village's "Hikari" (the light/deity they serve) is actually: - The Radiant Realm portal beneath Takashima - NOT local to their village but projected/connected remotely - Maintained by the One Tree and the Well - Being deliberately closed by someone (Circle? Other faction?)

The Horror: The attack on Deep Village wasn't random. Yora-no-kiba was: - Hired/manipulated by someone who knew Hikari was fading - Attacking a weakened village that was doomed anyway - Possibly trying to capture survivors for some purpose - Or eliminating witnesses who knew about Hikari's connection

The Stakes: To save any survivors and restore the village: 1. Restore Hikari's light - Reopen the Radiant portal fully 2. Find the survivors - Are they prisoners? Refugees? Dead? 3. Stop whoever is closing the portal - Circle? Other faction? 4. Accept the cost - What must be sacrificed to restore Hikari?

Yasei's Choice: If Hikari can only be partially restored or must be moved: - Save the village but doom something/someone else? - Let the village die to preserve the Tree/Well for the greater good? - Find a third option that saves both but costs Yasei everything?

Connection to Other PCs: - Thornbringer: Saving the Tree restores Hikari's light - Aoshi: The Oniwaban protected Hikari's portal (tied to duty) - Fox: Vault location = finding the source of Hikari - Kanji: Akemi may have been investigating Hikari's fading

Iseri Tetsuo: The Brother's Revenge

The Inciting Incident: The brother of the collections officer Iseri killed has arrived in Takashima and is setting everything in motion. This brother is: - Powerful - Has resources, connections, intelligence - Driven - Consumed by revenge but not stupid - Connected - Either works with the Circle or uses them

The Brother's Plan: The brother has discovered: 1. Iseri is traveling with a group heading to Takashima 2. The vault exists and contains something valuable 3. The party will investigate the vault (through their connections) 4. By manipulating events, he can: - Get revenge on Iseri - Use the party to access the vault - Profit from or weaponize what's inside - Destroy Iseri and everyone they care about

How He Sets Things in Motion: The brother orchestrates multiple events: - The troll encounter - His agents/hired muscle attack Iseri, intending to wound but not kill (he wants Iseri to suffer) - The four bodies - His men? Rival faction? Warning? - Kaoru's appearance - Coincidence or manipulation? Does brother know about Wild Lotus? - The tea house haunting - Is this connected to his plot? - Vault accessibility - He's weakening seals/guards to let party (and himself) in

The Brother's Identity: - Name: [To be determined] - Position: [Official? Criminal? Circle agent? Wealthy merchant?] - Resources: [What can he bring to bear?] - Weakness: [What's his blind spot?]

Was the First Kill Justified? The brother forces Iseri to confront this question: - The collections officer was doing his job (brutal but legal?) - Or was he genuinely corrupt and deserving death? - The brother has "evidence" either way (real or fabricated) - Iseri must decide if their first kill was justice or murder

The Confrontation: Eventually, the brother reveals himself and forces a choice: 1. Duel - One-on-one, winner takes all, let the party continue 2. Sacrifice - Iseri dies, party lives, vault secrets stay hidden 3. Exposure - Brother reveals Iseri's past to authorities/party 4. Corruption - Join the brother, turn on the party, access the vault together

Connection to Vault: The brother's revenge plot intersects with the vault because: - He needs something from the vault (power? Wealth? Weapon?) - OR he wants to destroy it (to harm Takashima authorities?) - OR he wants to lure Iseri into the vault to kill them there - OR someone else is using him, and he's a pawn

How The Storylines Interconnect

The Web of Connections

The Vault is Central:

                    THE VAULT BENEATH TAKASHIMA
                            |
            +---------------+---------------+
            |                               |
      THE ONE TREE                    THE WELL OF LIFE
            |                               |
      (Thornbringer)                  (Fox-kami knowledge)
            |                               |
    +-------+-------+               +-------+-------+
    |               |               |               |
HIKARI'S       ONIWABAN        FOX'S FALSE    AKEMI'S
 LIGHT         GUARDIAN         MEMORIES     INVESTIGATION
    |               |               |               |
(Yasei)         (Aoshi)          (Fox)          (Kanji)
    |               |               |               |
    +-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+-------+
                            |
                    ISERI'S BROTHER
                  (Sets Everything in Motion)

Timeline of Revelation

Early Arc 2 (Sessions 1-5): - Party enters Takashima - Meets Kaoru and Wild Lotus Society - Investigates tea house (Twice Cursed Samurai) - Discovers Akemi's death wasn't an accident (Kanji) - First hints that Hikari is fading (Yasei) - Iseri's brother makes first move (ambush? Message? Threat?)

Mid Arc 2 (Sessions 6-12): - Fox begins unraveling false memories, finds vault clues - Aoshi encounters evidence of Oniwaban massacre - Thornbringer learns Well is in Takashima - Kanji's investigation leads toward vault - Yasei discovers Hikari's light comes from beneath city - Brother's plot becomes clear - he's manipulating everyone - Revelation: All roads lead to the vault

Late Arc 2 (Sessions 13-18): - Party discovers vault entrance - Confronts traitor Oniwaban (Aoshi's storyline) - Finds evidence of Akemi's death/investigation (Kanji) - Reaches the Well and dying Tree (Thornbringer & Yasei) - Fox must use false memories to navigate vault - Brother makes his final move (Iseri confrontation) - Choice: What to do about Hikari, Tree, Well, and each other

Arc 2 Climax (Sessions 19-20): - Multiple simultaneous confrontations - Each PC faces their personal demon - Decisions about vault, Tree, Well, Hikari - Brother's true plan revealed and stopped/succeeded - Consequences ripple outward - Setup for Arc 3

Key NPCs to Develop

The Brother (Iseri's Nemesis)

  • Name: [To be determined]
  • Role: Revenge-driven manipulator
  • Connection: Sets everything in motion
  • Resources: [To be determined]
  • Final fate: [Player choice - death? Redemption? Escape?]

The Traitor Oniwaban (Aoshi's Nemesis)

  • Identity: [Someone personally painful to Aoshi]
  • Current allegiance: Obsidian Circle (willing or forced?)
  • Knowledge: Vault access, Oniwaban techniques, Circle secrets
  • Final fate: [Player choice - death? Redemption? Truth revealed?]

Akemi's Killer (Kanji's Target)

  • Identity: [Circle agent? Brother's associate? Traitor? Accident truly?]
  • Motivation: Why kill Akemi?
  • Current status: In Takashima? Dead already? Unaware of Kanji?
  • Final fate: [Player choice - justice? Revenge? Forgiveness? Understanding?]

Witnesses/Survivors

  • From Deep Village Hikari - Are there any? Where are they?
  • From Oniwaban Massacre - Besides Aoshi and traitor, any others?
  • From Akemi's Death - Who saw what really happened?
  • From First Kill - Anyone who knows what Iseri did?

Wild Lotus Society

  • Kaoru Sugimoto - What's her agenda? Truly helping or using party?
  • Other Members - Who else is in the society? Allies or obstacles?
  • Society's Knowledge - What do they know about the vault?

The Twice Cursed Samurai

  • Connection to vault? To Master Hideo? To any PC backstory?
  • Why haunting the tea house specifically?
  • What does he know about what's coming?

Major Decisions & Consequences

The Hikari Decision (Yasei & Thornbringer)

Options: 1. Fully restore Hikari - Costs: [Something major - life? Memories? Power?] 2. Partially restore - Enough to save Tree/survivors but not full strength 3. Relocate the portal - Move it to Deep Village? Elsewhere? Cost? 4. Let it close - Accept natural death, focus on other solutions

Consequences: - Full restoration might doom something else - Partial restoration creates temporary solution, future crisis - Relocation might break other protections/seals - Letting it close means Tree dies, Deep Village never recovers

The Well's Fate (Thornbringer)

Options: 1. Preserve it as is - Keep it hidden and protected 2. Share its power - Use it to heal/help people 3. Destroy it - Prevent Circle from corrupting it 4. Become its guardian - Personal sacrifice to protect it

Consequences: - Preservation maintains status quo but Circle will keep trying - Sharing might corrupt it or expose it to misuse - Destruction saves it from evil but eliminates potential good - Guardianship means Thornbringer can't leave/adventure

The Traitor's Fate (Aoshi)

Options: 1. Execute for betrayal - Justice for fallen clan 2. Attempt redemption - If corrupted/controlled, try to save them 3. Imprison/exile - Remove threat without killing 4. Understand and forgive - Learn their reasons, let go of revenge

Consequences: - Execution brings closure but ends possibility of truth - Redemption might restore ally but risks further betrayal - Prison creates future threat/escape plot - Forgiveness shows growth but may betray fallen Oniwaban

Akemi's Truth (Kanji)

Options: 1. Revenge on killer - Find and punish the responsible party 2. Expose conspiracy - Make truth public regardless of personal cost 3. Complete Akemi's work - Finish what they started 4. Let go and move forward - Accept that past is past

Consequences: - Revenge satisfies but doesn't bring Akemi back - Exposure might cause political chaos in Takashima - Completing work honors memory but risks same fate - Moving forward shows growth but leaves justice undone

The Brother's Fate (Iseri)

Options: 1. Kill him - End the threat permanently 2. Surrender to him - Sacrifice self for party/mission 3. Convince him - Show him first kill was justified/brother was worse 4. Work together - Find common enemy/cause

Consequences: - Killing continues cycle of violence - Surrender might not stop him anyway - Convincing requires proof and brother's willingness to listen - Working together might lead to genuine alliance or betrayal

The Master Twist

What if the Brother IS the Traitor Oniwaban?

This could tie multiple storylines together: - Collections officer was Oniwaban (deep cover or civilian relative) - Brother survived massacre by betraying clan - He's using revenge on Iseri as cover for Circle work - His real goal: Access vault for Circle using party - Aoshi and Iseri must work together to stop him - Personal betrayals stack: Brother, traitor, manipulator

Pros: - Unifies storylines elegantly - Single climactic confrontation - Forces Aoshi/Iseri bond - Simplifies NPC management

Cons: - Might feel too convenient - Reduces number of personal confrontations - Risks making some PCs feel secondary - Complex backstory to explain

Questions to Answer Before Arc 2 Starts

  1. What is Hikari exactly? Pure light? An entity? Portal's name? Kami?

  2. How long until Hikari closes completely? Weeks? Months? Unknown?

  3. What does the Circle want from the vault? Corrupt Tree? Drain Well? Destroy it? Use its power?

  4. Is Akemi dead or alive? If dead, when/how exactly? If alive, where/why hidden?

  5. What is the Traitor Oniwaban's name and relationship to Aoshi?

  6. What is the Brother's name and current position in Takashima?

  7. Does Master Hideo's grandson know about the vault? Is he the "blood key" to access it?

  8. What is the Twice Cursed Samurai's connection? Guardian? Failed guardian? Victim? Circle agent?

  9. How much does Kaoru/Wild Lotus know? About vault? Circle's plans? PC backstories?

  10. What is Shigeo's role in Arc 2? He has highest corruption - how does this tie in?

Climactic Scenes to Plan

Scene 1: The Vault Opens

  • How? What's required? Who succeeds?
  • Fox's memories are key but how exactly?
  • Master Hideo's grandson involved?
  • What's waiting inside?

Scene 2: The Dying Tree

  • Thornbringer and Yasei see it together
  • What does it look like? Feel like?
  • How do they know what to do?
  • Who or what opposes them?

Scene 3: Aoshi vs. Traitor

  • Location: In vault? At entrance? During another crisis?
  • Revelations during fight
  • Other PCs witness or separate?
  • How does it end?

Scene 4: Kanji Learns Truth

  • Who tells them? How?
  • Evidence or testimony?
  • Is killer present for confrontation?
  • What choice do they make?

Scene 5: Brother's Revelation

  • When does Iseri discover who's behind everything?
  • Public or private confrontation?
  • Does party know about first kill?
  • How does it end?

Scene 6: Simultaneous Crisis

  • Multiple storylines climax at once
  • Party must split up or prioritize
  • Impossible choices with no perfect answer
  • Consequences cascade

This framework should be treated as flexible. Player choices will shape the exact path, but these elements provide the structure for Arc 2's interconnected personal storylines.

Calendar of Shuigari

Calendar of Shuigari

Shuigari follows a lunisolar calendar guided by the three moons--Dendaro, Intara, and Tsukuyomi. Each year contains twelve months of thirty days, divided into three ten-day decads. Seasonal transitions are timed to celestial alignments, and every month carries a dominant spiritual theme that shapes rituals, markets, and travel.

Months at a Glance

Spring

  • Kaminatsu -- "Spring's Blessing": Renewal rites, temple petitions for bountiful crops, first pilgrimages of the year.
  • Haranami -- "Waves of Chaos": Unpredictable winds; farmers placate storm kami before sowing.
  • Sakuraji -- "Cherry Bloom": Hanami feasts, poetry competitions, vows of harmony.

Summer

  • Tenka -- "Heaven's Fire": Offerings to fire kami; warriors seek omens before campaigns.
  • Hisakata -- "Endless Sky": Explorers, merchants, and sky-priests hold navigation festivals.
  • Kaij? -- "Ocean's Heart": Coastal communities honor Ryujin with regattas and tide-blessing ceremonies.

Autumn

  • Momiji -- "Maple Leaf": Harvest festivals, ancestor offerings, communal storehouse feasts.
  • Tsukinami -- "Moonlight Path": Moonlit meditations and divinations--also the month when The Last Whisper of Steel begins.
  • Kuroame -- "Black Rain": Period of mourning and spiritual cleansing; shrines host purification rites.

Winter

  • Yukizora -- "Snow Sky": Sacred snow ceremonies, vows of quiet reflection.
  • Fubuki -- "Winter Storm": Communities gather around shared hearths; storytellers recount heroic endurance.
  • Setsunai -- "Frozen Heart": Year-end audits, reconciliations, and spiritual renewal before the cycle resets.

Annual Festivals & Observances

  • Spring Equinox (1 Kaminatsu): Renewal rites for farmers; priests bless seedlings with jade bells.
  • Cherry Blossom Feast (mid-Sakuraji): Hanami banquets, courtship promises, lantern-lit river floats.
  • Summer Solstice (5 Tenka): Fire dancers and blacksmiths reenact the forging of Soulsteel.
  • Ocean's Gratitude (Kaij? 15): Fishing fleets parade decorated boats; offerings returned to the tide.
  • Moonlit Reverence (Tsukinami 21): Held in honor of Tsukuyomi; divinations performed with mirrored pools.
  • Night of Falling Leaves (Kuroame 9): Memorial for those lost in the past year; paper leaves released on the wind.
  • First Snow Vigil (Yukizora 3): Children scatter rice along village borders to welcome protective kami.
  • Veil of Embers (Fubuki 27): Hearth ash is carried to shrines symbolising the burdens of the year.
  • Last Flame Ceremony (Setsunai 30): Final lantern extinguished at midnight to invite dawn's renewal.

Use this calendar to anchor session timelines, foreshadow omens, or tie regional customs to the moons' influence.

Currency and Trade Systems

Currency and Trade Systems of Shuigari

Overview

Shuigari's economy operates on a dual-value system combining rice-based tribute with metallic currency. The tension between traditional rice measurement and the rising importance of coined money reflects the broader conflict between tradition and innovation across the islands.

Standard Currency

The Koku System (Rice Standard)

The traditional measure of wealth and taxation throughout Shuigari.

Koku (?) - One koku = approximately 150 kg of rice (enough to feed one person for one year) - Used to measure: - Daimyo wealth and domain size - Samurai stipends - Tax obligations - Land value - A minor daimyo controls 10,000+ koku - A major daimyo controls 100,000+ koku - The Shogun's direct holdings exceed 4,000,000 koku

Coined Money

Ryo (?) - Gold Standard - Large gold oval coins stamped with the Shogun's mon (family crest) - Primary currency for major transactions - 1 ryo = approximately 1 koku of rice in value (though this fluctuates) - Used for: - Land purchases - Large-scale merchant deals - Daimyo-to-daimyo transactions - Hiring master craftsmen - Enchanted weapon purchases

Bu (?) - Silver Standard - Rectangular silver coins - 4 bu = 1 ryo - Used for: - Fine goods purchases - Artisan commissions - Inn stays (quality establishments) - Tool and weapon purchases - Monthly stipends for lesser samurai

Shu (?) - Gold/Silver Alloy - Small rectangular coins - 4 shu = 1 bu (16 shu = 1 ryo) - Used for: - Weekly provisions - Common merchandise - Sake and entertainment - Basic inn lodging - Everyday samurai expenses

Mon (?) - Copper/Bronze - Round coins with square hole (can be strung together) - 1,000 mon = 1 shu (approximately) - Used for: - Daily food purchases - Street vendor goods - Basic services - Peasant/commoner transactions - Temple offerings

Quick Reference Exchange Rates

1 Ryo = 4 Bu = 16 Shu = 16,000 Mon
1 Bu = 4 Shu = 4,000 Mon  
1 Shu = 1,000 Mon

Regional Variations

Takashima Prefecture

  • Iron Mon: Special copper coins alloyed with small amounts of iron, minted in Takashima
  • Slightly more valuable than standard mon due to iron content
  • Accepted at 1.1:1 ratio in other prefectures
  • Symbol of Takashima's metallurgical dominance

Hikosan (Capital)

  • Imperial Ryo: Gold ryo stamped with both Shogun and Emperor's seals
  • Used only in capital for official Shogunate business
  • Valued at 1.2 standard ryo due to political significance
  • Counterfeiting carries death penalty

Harado (Merchant Hub)

  • Trade Chits: Wooden or bamboo tokens issued by major merchant guilds
  • Redeemable for goods/services within guild networks
  • Allow merchants to avoid carrying heavy coin on long journeys
  • 1 chit = 1 ryo equivalent (backed by guild treasuries)

Port Cities

  • Harbor Notes: Paper certificates backed by merchant consortiums
  • Used for large ship cargo transactions
  • Denominations: 10, 50, 100, 500 ryo
  • Must be redeemed within 90 days or lose 10% value

Foreign Currency

Mainland Currencies (Pre-Sundering Legacy)

Dragon Marks (Ryugin ??) - Silver coins from the collapsed mainland empire - No longer minted but still circulate - Collectors and scholars prize them - 1 Dragon Mark = 3 bu (historical prestige value) - Often melted down for silver content

Western Trade Coins - Occasional foreign merchants bring coins from distant lands across the Sea of Mirrors - Accepted only at major ports - Must be assayed and exchanged for Shuigari currency - Exchange rate varies wildly (3:1 to 6:1 ratio depending on purity and port master's mood)

Taxation System

The Rice Tax (Nengu ??)

Primary form of taxation throughout Shuigari.

Standard Rate - Peasants owe 40-60% of rice harvest to their lord - Rate varies by prefecture and harvest quality - Collected twice yearly (after main and secondary harvests)

Collection Process 1. Village headman measures total harvest 2. Lord's tax collector verifies and records 3. Rice transported to daimyo's storehouse 4. Portion forwarded to Shogunate as tribute 5. Remainder used to: - Pay samurai stipends in rice - Maintain military reserves - Sell for coined money at market

Special Levies - War Tax: Additional 10-20% during military campaigns - Disaster Relief: May be reduced or suspended after famines/earthquakes - Infrastructure Tax: Extra rice for road/bridge/irrigation projects

Monetary Taxation

Merchant Taxes - 10% of gross trade value (paid quarterly) - Major guilds pay directly to Shogunate - Small merchants pay through local magistrates - Luxury goods taxed at 15%

Craft Taxes - Master artisans pay annual fee: 5 ryo - Journeymen pay annual fee: 1 ryo
- Apprentices exempt - Weapon smiths pay double (military importance)

Port Duties - Import/Export: 5% of cargo value - Docking fees: 1 bu per day for merchant vessels - Naval inspection: 2 shu per foreign ship

Mining Taxes - 30% of ore extracted goes to domain lord - Additional 10% to Shogunate for strategic metals (iron, steel) - Takashima's iron mines generate massive revenue through this system

Economic Classes and Typical Wealth

Peasant Farmers

  • Annual Income: 1-3 koku (subsistence)
  • Cash on hand: 500-2,000 mon
  • Lives entirely in mon economy
  • Rarely sees silver or gold

Artisans/Merchants

  • Annual Income: 5-30 koku equivalent
  • Cash on hand: 2-10 bu
  • Daily transactions in mon and shu
  • Larger deals in bu and ryo

Samurai (Lower Ranks)

  • Annual Stipend: 50-200 koku
  • Paid in rice, converts some to coin
  • Regular expenses: 3-6 shu per month
  • Debts common (living above means)

Samurai (High Ranks)

  • Annual Stipend: 500-3,000 koku
  • Receives mix of rice and coin
  • Monthly expenses: 5-20 ryo
  • Maintains household, servants, weapons

Daimyo (Minor)

  • Domain Revenue: 10,000-50,000 koku
  • Must pay:
  • Samurai retainers (30-40% of revenue)
  • Shogunate tribute (10-15%)
  • Infrastructure/military (20-30%)
  • Personal wealth: 100-500 ryo liquid

Daimyo (Major)

  • Domain Revenue: 100,000-500,000 koku
  • Similar percentage obligations but higher absolute numbers
  • Personal wealth: 1,000-10,000 ryo liquid
  • Can influence Shogunate policy through loans

Merchant Guild Masters

  • Annual Profits: 50,000-200,000 koku equivalent
  • Liquid Assets: 5,000-50,000 ryo
  • Politically powerless but economically vital
  • Secret loans to daimyo create leverage

Prices and Cost of Living

Food (Daily)

  • Bowl of rice: 5 mon
  • Fish/vegetables: 10-20 mon
  • Sake (cheap): 15 mon per flask
  • Sake (quality): 1 shu per flask
  • Full meal (common inn): 30-50 mon
  • Full meal (quality inn): 2-4 shu
  • Banquet (per person): 1-3 bu

Lodging

  • Common inn: 100 mon per night
  • Quality inn: 1 shu per night
  • High-class inn: 2-4 shu per night
  • Daimyo suite: 1+ bu per night

Clothing

  • Peasant work clothes: 200-500 mon
  • Merchant kimono: 1-3 shu
  • Samurai formal wear: 2-5 bu
  • Silk kimono (fine): 1-3 ryo
  • Master artisan commission: 5-20 ryo

Weapons & Armor

  • Simple iron sword: 2-4 shu
  • Quality katana: 3-8 bu
  • Master-forged katana: 5-20 ryo
  • Legendary blade: 100+ ryo (plus favors/quests)
  • Full armor (ashigaru): 1-2 bu
  • Full armor (samurai): 5-15 bu
  • Ceremonial armor: 3-10 ryo

Services

  • Healer (common ailment): 50-200 mon
  • Doctor (surgery): 1-5 shu
  • Scribe (letter): 20 mon
  • Scribe (contract): 1-3 shu
  • Fortune teller: 50-500 mon
  • Priest blessing: 100-1,000 mon
  • Onmyoji ritual: 1 bu - 5 ryo (depending on complexity)

Animals & Transport

  • Draft horse: 5-10 bu
  • War horse: 3-8 ryo
  • Ox: 2-4 bu
  • Palanquin rental: 500 mon per day
  • Cart rental: 200 mon per day
  • River ferry: 10-50 mon
  • Coastal passage: 1-5 shu

Tools & Equipment

  • Farming tools (set): 500-1,000 mon
  • Carpentry tools: 1-3 shu
  • Smithing tools (basic): 1-2 bu
  • Masterwork tools: 5-15 bu
  • Enchanting supplies: 2-10 ryo

Economic Challenges

Inflation

  • Prolonged warfare drains Shogunate treasury
  • More coin minted with less gold/silver content
  • Trust in currency declining
  • Some merchants demand payment in pure metal or rice

Counterfeiting

  • Rising problem in major cities
  • Criminal organizations (Emerald Lotus Syndicate) profit hugely
  • Penalties severe: death by crucifixion
  • Detection methods:
  • Weight testing
  • Sound testing (experts can hear fake coins)
  • Seal inspection
  • Merchant guild stamps

Debt Culture

  • Samurai commonly in debt to merchants
  • Code of honor prevents open commerce
  • Secret arrangements through intermediaries
  • Some samurai become ronin to escape debts
  • Daimyo accumulate massive loans to fund military

Regional Imbalances

  • Takashima's iron wealth vs. agricultural regions
  • Port cities accumulating coin, rural areas rice-poor
  • Merchant class growing wealthier than lower samurai
  • Threatens traditional social order

Money-Lending and Banking

Merchant Guilds

  • Function as unofficial banks
  • Lend to daimyo at 10-20% annual interest
  • Foreclose impossible (social class barriers)
  • Power through accumulation of uncollectable IOUs

Temple Banks

  • Buddhist temples provide small loans to commoners
  • 5-15% interest (lower than guilds)
  • Collateral: land, tools, family heirlooms
  • More ethical but limited capital

Pawnbrokers

  • Accept any collateral
  • 20-50% interest on short-term loans
  • Frequent customers: lower samurai, gambling addicts
  • Often fronts for criminal organizations

Black Market Economics

Shadow Market Rates

  • Stolen goods: 30-50% of legitimate value
  • Forbidden items: 200-500% markup
  • Smuggled foreign goods: 150-300% markup
  • Information: 1 shu - 10 ryo depending on value

Grey Tide Economy

  • Pirate gold (looted): Melted and recast
  • Contraband weapons: 150% normal price
  • Enslaved workers: 5-20 ryo per person (abhorrent but occurs)
  • Protection rackets: 10-30% of merchant profits

Obsidian Circle Resources

  • Massive hidden wealth (source unknown)
  • Can outbid legitimate buyers for artifacts
  • Pays premium for information: 3-5x normal rates
  • Recruiting bonuses: 10 ryo signing payment for skilled warriors
  • Operating budget suggests funding from powerful backer

Campaign Integration

Plot Hooks

  • PCs discover counterfeit ring
  • Daimyo's debt to merchant guild threatens domain
  • Shadow Market dealing in cursed artifacts
  • Rice tax creates peasant uprising
  • Foreign currency appearing in volume (trade route opening?)

Economic Warfare

  • Obsidian Circle manipulating rice markets
  • Daimyo bankrupting rival through trade manipulation
  • Merchant guild threatening to call in Shogunate's loans
  • Inflation causing social unrest

Treasure and Rewards

Use this system to make treasure meaningful: - 5 ryo is significant wealth to common folk - 50 ryo is life-changing money - 500 ryo could buy a small estate - 5,000 ryo could fund a minor rebellion

PC Expenses

Track silver and gold separately: - Daily living: mon and shu - Equipment upgrades: bu and ryo - Political bribes: ryo only - Information: all denominations depending on value

Deep Provinces

Deep Provinces

Ah, splendid choices! The Okug?ri (Deep Provinces) radiates an air of mystique and secrecy, perfectly capturing the enigmatic nature of these isolated shinobi sanctuaries. Likewise, the ranks Tsukiwaka (Moonling), Taiy?shi (Child of the Sun), and Rairy? (Thunder Dragon) evoke a graceful progression tied to celestial and natural power--a beautiful blend of spirituality and martial growth.

Let us formalize this structure into a cohesive framework, ensuring it feels consistent and rich in lore. Here's a refined version for easy integration:

Okug?ri (Deep Provinces)

In the rugged wilderness of Takashima Prefecture, shrouded in mist and mystery, lie the Okug?ri (Deep Provinces)--hidden enclaves of ancient martial and spiritual traditions. These sanctuaries were established by rogue clans, wandering mystics, and outcast samurai during the chaotic Age of Warring Daimyos. Over centuries, they have evolved into secretive hubs of power, guided by a delicate balance between the mortal and the spiritual realms.

The Okug?ri are fiercely protective of their independence, hiding from the prying eyes of the Shogunate and feudal lords. Each province is unique, shaped by the natural and spiritual forces of its environment, and their shinobi (known collectively as G?rijin, "People of the Deep Provinces") are renowned for their unparalleled skills in war, espionage, and mysticism.

The Three Great Ranks of the G?rijin

The Okug?ri measure progression through ranks that symbolize spiritual growth, martial refinement, and an increasingly intimate connection to the kami. These ranks are recognized across all provinces, though the specific trials and ceremonies to ascend vary by region.

Tsukiwaka (??, "Moonling")

  • Rank: Apprentice
  • Role: Novices who have begun their journey into the mystical and martial arts of the Okug?ri. They are compared to the crescent moon--fragile, untested, yet full of potential to grow and shine.
  • Duties:
  • Basic espionage, courier work, and assisting higher-ranked G?rijin.
  • Learning the fundamental arts of the province, such as hand-to-hand combat, spiritual rituals, and elemental techniques.
  • Completing physical and spiritual endurance tests to build resilience.
  • Symbolism: The crescent moon represents both new beginnings and the unseen--traits critical to a shinobi's survival.
  • Typical Gear: Simple robes, kunai, and training tools. No province crest is worn until promotion.

Taiy?shi (???, "Child of the Sun")

  • Rank: Journeyman
  • Role: Fully trained shinobi who serve as the backbone of the province. Taiy?shi are warriors and operatives skilled in combat, infiltration, and diplomacy. They are considered like the rising sun--bright, capable, and able to stand on their own.
  • Duties:
  • Leading small teams on missions, including sabotage, reconnaissance, and protection of the Okug?ri's secrets.
  • Mastering at least one advanced discipline (such as stealth, elemental manipulation, or ritual exorcism).
  • Mentoring Tsukiwaka to guide their early growth.
  • Symbolism: The sun signifies power, clarity, and maturity--traits expected of a Taiy?shi.
  • Typical Gear: Custom armor and weapons crafted to reflect their chosen discipline. They proudly wear their province's crest on their forehead protector, armor, or robes.

Rairy? (??, "Thunder Dragon")

  • Rank: Master
  • Role: The elite among the G?rijin, Rairy? are living legends within their provinces, their strength and wisdom akin to dragons commanding storms. They act as generals, spiritual leaders, and enforcers of the Okug?ri's will. Few ever reach this rank, and those who do are revered as avatars of their province's ideals.
  • Duties:
  • Leading large-scale operations or defending the province during times of crisis.
  • Teaching advanced techniques to Taiy?shi and developing new ones that blend their personal style with their province's unique traditions.
  • Serving as emissaries or negotiators when the Okug?ri must interact with the outside world.
  • Symbolism: The thunder dragon represents overwhelming power, wisdom, and the divine--embodying the apex of what it means to be G?rijin.
  • Typical Gear: Ornate armor and enchanted weapons, often forged from rare materials or imbued with the spiritual essence of their province's kami. Their gear is said to be as fearsome as their reputation.

Optional Specialized Rank: Yamikami (??, "Shadow Kami")

  • Rank: Secret Operative
  • Role: Yamikami are the shadowy elite--assassins, spies, and saboteurs who operate entirely in secrecy, even within their own province. They are seen as divine enforcers of balance, working unseen to eliminate threats and uphold their province's security. Some say Yamikami do not truly exist, but whispers persist that they are chosen directly by the kami.
  • Symbolism: The Shadow Kami's existence reflects the duality of creation and destruction, order and chaos. They are the sword and the shield in perfect harmony.

Rituals of Advancement

Advancing through the ranks is not simply a matter of skill; it requires trials that test not only the physical and mental fortitude of the shinobi but also their spiritual connection to their province's kami.

  1. Tsukiwaka to Taiy?shi - "The Rite of the Rising Sun": This trial often involves a week-long solo mission in hostile territory, a test of survival and resourcefulness. Upon success, the initiate is presented with the crest of their Okug?ri and sworn in as a Taiy?shi.
  2. Taiy?shi to Rairy? - "The Dragon's Ascent": This trial varies by province but usually involves facing a dangerous foe or performing a heroic deed that brings honor to the province. Many Rairy? must also demonstrate mastery over their kami's favored element.
  3. Becoming Yamikami - "The Shadow's Whisper": There is no formal trial; the Yamikami are chosen in secret by the Kage or the province's kami themselves. Those chosen disappear for months or years, returning as silent, ghost-like figures of unimaginable skill.

Example Provinces and Leaders

Would you like me to flesh out specific Okug?ri, their Kage-like leaders, or the spiritual elements that set each province apart? We could tie these rankings into provincial conflicts, rivalries, or their relationship with the Shogunate. Perhaps even a forbidden alliance with the yokai? Let me know how you wish to proceed!

Education and Literacy

Education and Literacy in Shuigari

Overview

Education in Shuigari is rigidly stratified by social class, reflecting the feudal hierarchy. While literacy rates are relatively high compared to medieval societies, access to advanced education remains a privilege of the samurai and merchant classes. The tension between traditional martial education and rising scholarly pursuits mirrors the broader conflict between old ways and innovation.

Literacy Rates by Class

Overall Statistics

  • Total Population Literacy: Approximately 35-40%
  • Urban Areas: 50-60% literate
  • Rural Areas: 20-30% literate
  • Gender Gap: Male literacy 45%, Female literacy 25%

By Social Class

Nobility and Samurai - Literacy Rate: 95-100% - Both men and women educated - Expected to master: - Classical texts - Poetry composition - Calligraphy - Military strategy treatises - Historical chronicles

Priests and Monks - Literacy Rate: 100% - Often the most educated class - Masters of: - Sacred texts - Philosophical treatises - Astronomical/calendar calculations - Medical knowledge - Ritual procedures

Merchants and Artisans - Literacy Rate: 60-80% - Functional literacy focused on: - Accounting and record-keeping - Contracts and agreements - Trade correspondence - Technical manuals - Price lists and inventories

Peasants and Laborers - Literacy Rate: 15-30% - Basic literacy when present: - Sign names - Read simple notices - Basic numeracy - Village records

The Writing System

Script Types

Kaisho (??) - "Standard Script" - Formal, block-style characters - Used for: - Official documents - Legal contracts - Imperial edicts - Shogunate decrees - Temple inscriptions - Taught to all samurai children - Takes years to master

Gyosho (??) - "Running Script" - Semi-cursive, faster writing - Used for: - Personal correspondence
- Poetry - Quick notes - Merchant records - Daily documents - Standard for educated adults - Balance of speed and elegance

Sosho (??) - "Grass Script" - Highly cursive, artistic - Used for: - Calligraphy art - Poetic works - Personal journals - Secret messages (hard to read if unfamiliar) - Mastery marks high education - Each calligrapher develops unique style

Kana (Syllabic Script) - Simplified phonetic characters - Easier to learn than full Kaisho - Used for: - Common communication - Women's writing (though educated women also learn Kaisho) - Children's early learning - Phonetic guides in texts - Combination of Kaisho and Kana standard in most writing

Specialized Scripts

Cipher Scripts - Used by ninja clans and Shogunate spies - Based on Kaisho but with substitutions - Each organization has unique cipher - Decryption requires key knowledge

Runic Scripts - Ancient characters used in magical/spiritual contexts - Onmyoji and priests learn these - Used for: - Spell scrolls - Protective talismans - Shrine inscriptions - Sealing rituals

Technical Notation - Specialized symbols for: - Metallurgy (temperature, alloy ratios) - Medicine (dosages, symptoms) - Architecture (measurements, materials) - Military (troop positions, signals)

Educational Institutions

Samurai Education

Domain Academies (Han-ko ??) - Established by each major daimyo - Located in castle towns - Attendance mandatory for samurai youth (ages 7-16)

Curriculum Includes: - Morning: Martial Training (3-4 hours) - Swordsmanship - Archery - Horsemanship - Spear work - Military strategy

  • Midday: Scholarly Studies (3-4 hours)
  • Reading classical texts
  • Writing and calligraphy
  • Mathematics and accounting
  • History and ethics

  • Poetry composition

  • Evening: Specialized Training (1-2 hours)

  • Tea ceremony
  • Music (flute, shamisen)
  • Go and shogi (strategy games)
  • Etiquette and protocol

Notable Academies:

Hikosan Imperial Academy - Most prestigious in Shuigari - Trains sons of high-ranking daimyo - Direct connection to Shogunate service - 200 students at any time - Faculty includes retired generals and scholars - Graduation rate: 85%

Takashima Mountain Academy - Emphasis on metallurgy and engineering - Combines martial and technical education - Students learn smithing alongside strategy - Famous for producing military engineers - 150 students - Graduation rate: 90%

Harado Mercantile Academy - Unusual: Accepts merchant class students alongside samurai - Focus on administration, logistics, diplomacy - Controversial but effective - 180 students - Graduation rate: 75%

Temple Schools (Terakoya ???)

Structure: - Run by Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines - Open to commoners (small fees) - Ages 7-14 - Classes held in temple buildings - 1 teacher per 20-40 students

Curriculum: - Reading (basic Kaisho and Kana) - Writing (practice with cheap paper, sand trays) - Arithmetic (abacus, basic math) - Moral education (religious texts) - Practical skills (measuring, record-keeping)

Distribution: - Nearly every village has access to terakoya - Urban areas may have multiple schools - Quality varies greatly by teacher - Approximately 40,000 terakoya across Shuigari

Costs: - Tuition: 100-500 mon per year - Writing materials: 200-400 mon per year - Additional for calligraphy lessons: 100 mon/month - Poor families may barter goods/services instead

Artisan Apprenticeships

The Apprentice System Not formal schools but structured education:

Age 10-14: Apprentice (Deshi ??) - Lives with master's family - Learns basics through observation and menial tasks - Minimal instruction, mostly imitation - No pay, receives food/shelter/clothing - Expected to master foundational skills

Age 14-20: Journeyman (Shokunin ??) - Practices craft under supervision - Begins receiving small stipend (500-2,000 mon/month) - May work for other masters to learn techniques - Travels to study with specialists - Produces work that can be sold

Age 20+: Master (Takumi ?) - Achieves mastery through examination or masterwork creation - Can establish own workshop - Takes own apprentices - Joins guild with full voting rights

Specialized Schools:

Takashima Smithing Guilds - Most rigorous weapons training in Shuigari - 10-year apprenticeship minimum - Only 1 in 5 apprentices achieve master rank - Secret techniques passed only to guild members - Written technical manuals (closely guarded)

Hikosan Calligraphy Academies - Accept both samurai and talented commoners - 5-8 year training program - Master calligraphers can earn 20-50 ryo annually - Prestigious career path for second/third sons

Ninja Clan Training

Structure: - Closed schools within hidden villages - Training begins at age 5-6 - Total immersion, no outside contact - Combines physical, mental, magical training

Curriculum: - Stealth and infiltration - Disguise and acting - Poison-craft and medicine - Cipher and code-breaking - Athletics and climbing - Weapons (concealed, improvised) - Espionage techniques - Regional dialects and customs

Literacy Requirements: - Must achieve high literacy (multiple scripts) - Learn specialized cipher systems - Study psychology and persuasion - Train in forgery and document creation

Duration: - 10-15 years before first mission - Lifelong learning and specialization - Dropout rate: 40% (reassigned to support roles)

Onmyoji and Magical Training

Imperial Onmyodo Bureau (Onmyoryo ???) - Official Shogunate magical institution - Located in Hikosan - Highly selective (accepts ~20 students every 3 years) - Entrance exam tests aptitude for spiritual sensitivity

Curriculum (8-12 years): - Classical cosmology and astrology - Divination techniques - Ritual procedures and protocols - Spirit negotiation and binding - Protective magic and exorcism - Calendar creation and astronomy - Geomancy and feng shui - Herbalism and alchemy - Advanced literacy (including runic scripts)

Graduation: - Final exam: Complex divination for Shogunate official - Success rate: 60% - Graduates receive rank of Junior Onmyoji - Assigned to daimyo courts or Shogunate service

Shrine Priesthood Training - Separate from Onmyodo Bureau - Each major shrine trains own priests/priestesses - Focus on specific kami traditions - 5-10 year training period - Emphasis on ritual purity and procedure - High literacy in sacred texts required

Women's Education

Samurai Daughters - Educated at home by tutors - Focus on: - Reading and writing (high level) - Calligraphy and poetry - Tea ceremony - Flower arrangement - Music (koto, shamisen) - Household management - Some martial arts (naginata common) - Etiquette and protocol

Elite Women's Academies - Several private institutions in major cities - Cater to daimyo daughters - Tuition: 50-200 ryo annually - Produce highly educated women - Graduates often become influential through marriage

Merchant/Artisan Daughters - Practical education - Learn family business - Basic literacy and numeracy - Focused on economic independence

Peasant Women - Minimal formal education - Some terakoya access - Literacy rate only 15-20% - Skills passed down mother to daughter

Libraries and Archives

Imperial Archives (Hikosan)

  • Largest collection in Shuigari
  • 50,000+ volumes
  • Includes:
  • Historical chronicles
  • Tax records (500+ years)
  • Legal precedents
  • Imperial genealogies
  • Military treatises
  • Access: Shogunate officials and approved scholars only

Domain Libraries

  • Each major daimyo maintains collection
  • 5,000-20,000 volumes typical
  • Focus on domain-specific records:
  • Local history
  • Tax records
  • Land surveys
  • Samurai genealogies
  • Military records

Temple Libraries

  • Buddhist temples often have significant collections
  • Medical texts
  • Philosophical works
  • Historical chronicles
  • Popular fiction
  • More accessible to public (for donation/fee)

Merchant Guild Archives

  • Trade records and contracts
  • Price histories
  • Ship manifests
  • Credit/debt ledgers
  • More recent (last 200 years typically)
  • Closely guarded (proprietary information)

Book Production and Cost

Manuscript Production

Hand-Copied Books - Monk scribes primary producers - 1 book takes 2-6 months to copy - Cost: 5-20 ryo depending on length/complexity - Only wealthy can afford private collections

Woodblock Printing - Increasingly common in last 100 years - Faster production once blocks carved - Popular works: poetry collections, practical manuals - Cost: 1-5 ryo per printed book - Making books more accessible

Materials: - Rice paper (washi): 200-500 mon per ream - Ink: 100-300 mon per stick - Brushes: 50-500 mon depending on quality - Binding: 100-200 mon per book

Popular Literature

Available to Literate Commoners: - Popular tales and folklore: 500-2,000 mon - Poetry collections: 1-3 shu - Practical manuals (farming, crafts): 1-2 shu - Religious texts: Donated by temples (free to copy)

Samurai Literature: - Military treatises: 3-10 bu - Classical poetry: 2-5 bu - Historical chronicles: 5-15 bu - Philosophical works: 3-8 bu

Rare and Valuable: - Ancient manuscripts: 50-500 ryo - Imperial edicts (originals): Priceless - Magical grimoires: 100-1,000 ryo - Master calligraphy: 20-200 ryo

Specialized Knowledge

Secret Techniques

Smithing: - Guild secrets passed orally - Written manuals exist but closely guarded - Require guild membership to access - Some techniques known only to 1-2 living masters

Martial Arts: - Sword schools (ryu) maintain scrolls of techniques - Makimono (scroll) passed headmaster to successor - Public demonstrations but secrets remain hidden - Some schools have "hidden techniques" unknown to outsiders

Onmyoji Magic: - Most powerful rituals not written down - Master-to-student oral transmission - Written texts often incomplete (intentionally) - True knowledge requires initiation

Literacy and Social Mobility

Education as Advancement

For Commoners: - Literacy opens merchant careers - Temple school graduates may become: - Scribes (500-2,000 mon/month) - Teachers (1-3 shu/month) - Low-level bureaucrats (2-5 shu/month) - Accountants (3-8 shu/month)

For Lower Samurai: - Advanced education necessary for advancement - Scholarship to prestigious academy changes family fortune - Literary talent can lead to adviser positions - Some become professional scholars (5-20 ryo annually)

The Examination System

Shogunate Civil Service Exam (Recent Innovation) - Introduced 50 years ago - Controversial (threatens hereditary privilege) - Open to samurai class only - Held every 3 years in Hikosan - Tests: - Classical literature - History - Ethics and philosophy - Poetry composition - Administrative law - Mathematics

Success Rates: - Only 10-15% pass - Successful candidates guaranteed Shogunate position - Positions: 5-20 koku stipend - Path to higher office - Some daimyo conduct own exams

Current Educational Trends

Tensions

Traditionalist View: - Too much literacy threatens social order - Commoners should focus on their station - Classical education sufficient for samurai - New subjects (foreign knowledge) corrupting

Reformist View: - Shuigari falling behind - Need technical education (engineering, medicine) - Merit should matter more than birth - Expand examination system

Emerging Changes

Western Learning (Rangaku ??) - Small but growing interest in foreign knowledge - Mathematics and science from across Sea of Mirrors - Controversial (foreign = impure to many) - Secret study circles in port cities - Some progressive daimyo sponsor research

Expanded Women's Education - More academies opening - Debate: Does female education destabilize families? - Some women becoming published poets/authors - Still far from equality but changing

Merchant Academies - Teaching administration, accounting, foreign languages - Filling gap in Shogunate education - Wealthy merchants funding these - Graduates often more practical than samurai academy students

Campaign Integration

Plot Hooks

  • Lost ancient text surfaces, multiple factions want it
  • PCs hired to infiltrate ninja school and steal technique scroll
  • Reformist teacher accused of corrupting youth
  • Magical grimoire stolen from temple library
  • Counterfeit Shogunate documents create diplomatic crisis

PC Backgrounds

  • Former samurai academy student (expelled for?)
  • Temple school teacher turned adventurer
  • Failed onmyoji exam candidate
  • Merchant guild scholar with forbidden knowledge
  • Ninja dropout with incomplete training

Knowledge Skills

Use education background to determine what PCs know: - Samurai academy: History, military strategy, etiquette - Temple school: Basic literacy, local lore, religion - Artisan apprentice: Trade techniques, guild politics - Ninja training: Espionage, poison-craft, disguise - Onmyoji training: Spirits, rituals, astrology

Treasure and Rewards

  • Rare books and scrolls
  • Secret technique manual
  • Forged documents
  • Library access
  • Tuition for follower/hireling
  • Scholarship for PC's child/sibling

Elemental Beasts of Shuigari

Elemental Beasts of Shuigari

Elemental beasts are manifestations of the islands' living ley lines. They emerge where kami influence is strong or where Shindarasu's corruption tears a rift. Use the following roster to flavour encounters, rituals, or side quests tied to fading magic.

Beast Element Habitat Hooks & Traits
Aokumo, the Mist Drake Air/Water Highland fog banks above Takashima Half-spirit dragon that condenses clouds into armour. Grants safe passage if offered wind chimes forged by Haruto the Blacksmith. Circle cultists seek its breath to shroud invasions.
Kurogane Titan Earth/Metal Deep mines near Kurogane-mura Massive construct animated by Daichi-no-kame's dwindling power. Awakens when Soulsteel forges are abused. Subdue or negotiate before it collapses tunnels.
Emberthorn Kirin Fire/Wood Tatsuhara thunder forests Antlered beast of living embers. Appears when balance between forest spirits and lightning rituals falters. Provides a spark needed to reignite failing shrines.
Suiren Lotus Turtle Water Sacred pools of Mizukawa Gargantuan turtle that blooms luminous lotus pads on its shell. Heals tainted water but is hunted by smugglers seeking to sell petals as panaceas.
Gale Lantern Foxes Air/Lightning Cliffside shrines along sea routes Packs of fox spirits carrying storm lanterns. They lure ships away from Circle blockades but turn mischievous if insulted.
Obsidian Ash Wyrm Fire/Earth Breathless Hollow fractures Shindarasu-corrupted serpent that feeds on memories. Slaying it yields shards needed for the Soulsteel sanctification ritual.

Using Elemental Beasts in Play

  • Shrine Maintenance: Elemental beasts can cleanse or further corrupt a shrine based on player choices, providing a living gauge for the state of the seal.
  • Ley Line Diagnostics: Tracking a beast's behaviour reveals where ley lines buckle or fade, guiding parties to priority sites.
  • Crafting Components: Harvesting scales, breath, or petals from willing beasts supplies rare reagents for Elemental Magic and Technology or advanced Soulsteel work.
  • Faction Bargaining Chips: Okug?ri leaders or Circle operatives trade services, alliances, or betrayals for access to a beast's domain.

Blend these creatures with yokai or mortal threats to emphasise that the natural world reacts to the campaign's escalating stakes.

Elemental Magic and Technology

Elemental Magic and Technology in Shuigari

As magic wanes, engineers, ritualists, and kami intermediaries experiment with hybrid solutions. This guide outlines the current state of elemental innovation--ripe for quests, crafting, or sabotage.

Leyline Devices

  • Lanterns of Continuance: Portable leyline detectors used by the Seekers of the Wheel. Glow brighter near intact nodes; flicker near corrupted sites.
  • Breath Engines: Proto-technological devices that harness wind kami to power mills or war fans. Malfunctions manifest as sudden gusts or vacuum pockets.
  • Aquifer Filters: Mizukawa artisans channel water kami through rune-etched pipes to cleanse polluted wells. Circle agents infect them with obsidian shards to poison villages.

Ritual Technologies

  • Elemental Batteries: Crystalline prisms storing excess elemental energy. Popular among shrine guardians but volatile; a failed check releases the stored element.
  • Kami Contracts: Written accords binding lesser kami to operate devices (e.g., storm gates, lantern arrays). Breaking the contract enrages the kami.
  • Rune Ferries: Lightning-etched boats run along charged rails across ravines. Depend on continuous offerings to avoid stranding travellers mid-crossing.

Current Challenges

  • Magic Dissipation: Devices lose charge faster; rituals require more offerings. Engineers seek elemental beast components (see Elemental Beasts of Shuigari) to stabilise them.
  • Circle Sabotage: Obsidian agents replace runes with corrupted glyphs, causing backlash or summoning Shindarasu fragments.
  • Resource Shortages: Emerald Lotus Syndicate hoards reagents, creating black markets for Stormglass, Moonvine sap, and volcanic ore.

Plot Hooks

  • Escort a rune-ferry convoy transporting refugees while Circle saboteurs attempt to overload the rails.
  • Retrieve lost research on elemental batteries before the Ghostwalkers seize it to halt technological progress.
  • Negotiate with a reluctant water kami to restart an aquifer filter vital to Takashima's food supply.
  • Track down counterfeit lanterns flooding the capital before they trigger fires in the shrine quarter.

Elemental technology reinforces the campaign's tension between tradition and adaptation. Treat it as both a tool and a potential hazard--especially when the Obsidian Circle twists the circuitry of faith.

Emerging Factions of Shuigari

Emerging Factions of Shuigari

Several movements exist outside the Empire's official registry. Some oppose the Obsidian Circle; others risk tipping the balance in their favour. These notes expand the hooks referenced in earlier planning documents.

The Blades of the Phoenix

  • Base: Nomadic, currently active along the southern trade roads.
  • Goal: Reignite the "phoenix cycle" by destroying old orders and guiding rebirth through controlled burns--both literal and political.
  • Methods: Guerilla strikes on granaries and bureaucratic archives they deem corrupt. Seek Soulsteel embers to forge a symbolic phoenix blade.
  • Campaign Use: Potential uneasy allies if convinced the Circle represents the true corruption. Their penchant for collateral damage can cause civilian backlash.

The Ghostwalkers

  • Base: Hidden monasteries within the Rei no Mori forest.
  • Goal: Maintain the silence between worlds. They believe the dwindling of magic is a correction and try to prevent mortals from meddling with seals.
  • Methods: Astral projection, dream infiltration, sabotage of rituals they deem reckless.
  • Campaign Use: Their information on Shindarasu's prison is unmatched, but they may sabotage shrine repairs if players fail to earn trust.

Emerald Lotus Syndicate

  • Base: Harado Prefecture ports; smugglers with polite etiquette.
  • Goal: Profit from the scarcity of ritual reagents while claiming to "stabilise markets."
  • Methods: Trade monopolies, counterfeit shrine incense, covert alliances with Circle quartermasters.
  • Campaign Use: Offer black-market resources or intel in exchange for access to ley nodes. Unmasking their Circle ties can sway public opinion in Harado.

The Way of the Flame

  • Base: Volcano monasteries near Mount Hoshigami.
  • Goal: Preserve martial traditions blessed by Izanami no Kagutsuchi. They fear Soulsteel misuse and train warriors to enforce responsible forging.
  • Methods: Trial-by-fire duels, confiscation of cursed blades, forging oaths.
  • Campaign Use: Provide advanced smithing techniques or blessings if the party dedicates a weapon to their order. Oppose the Obsidian Circle's desecration of furnaces.

The Crimson Maw

  • Base: River delta slums coined "Bloody Wharf."
  • Goal: Control river transport by wielding fear. They view Circle chaos as opportunity, not ideology.
  • Methods: River piracy, hostage-taking, intimidation of shrine caretakers for "protection fees."
  • Campaign Use: As antagonists in travel arcs or unwilling informants who can be flipped with leverage over their leadership.

Seekers of the Wheel

  • Base: Traveling philosophers charting the "Wheel of Seasons."
  • Goal: Categorise each spiritual phenomenon into an eight-spoke wheel model, proving every event repeats. Believe they can predict when the seal fails.
  • Methods: Archive exchanges, prophecy lectures, infiltration of temple libraries.
  • Campaign Use: Their research can forecast Circle offensives or reveal unknown shrines. If corrupted, they may rationalise Shindarasu's release as "the next turn of the wheel."

Integrate these groups as quest patrons, rivals, or complications when the party seeks allies against the Circle. Each can anchor side arcs or introduce moral dilemmas aligned with Shuigari's themes.

Fauna of Shuigari

Fauna of Shuigari

Shuigari's wildlife reflects the archipelago's balance between spirit and sword. Creatures often carry cultural meaning, appear in omens, or lend their traits to local craftsmanship. Use the table below to bring the natural world to the forefront of encounters and downtime scenes.

Creature Type Description Habitat Cultural Notes
Ashwing Raven Bird Charcoal raven with ashen wingtips and a keen mimicry call. Takashima Prefecture highlands Considered heralds of change; feathers anchor divination charms.
Riverguard Turtle Reptile Massive freshwater turtle cloaked in moss and algae. Minashima river valleys Villagers carve shells into ceremonial shields representing patience.
Skyflash Hawk Bird of prey Sleek hawk with lightning-streaked plumage and uncanny speed. Kisato plateau and trade routes Employed as message hawks by scholars and magistrates.
Flamehorn Yak Mammal Mountain yak whose horns glow faintly at night. Takashima alpine passes Horn shavings fuel rituals for safe travel; beasts haul forge supplies.
Crimson Fang Tiger Mammal Rare tiger with crimson striping and elongated sabre fangs. Furenhoku tundra forests Sightings are omens of either great fortune or impending disaster.
Sea Blossom Dolphin Aquatic mammal Playful dolphin patterned like blooming petals. Sea of Mirrors Fisherfolk credit pods with guiding ships through treacherous shoals.
Moonlit Koi Fish Silver-scaled koi that glow under moonlight. Temple ponds across Hikosan Released during moon festivals to honor Tsukuyomi.
Amberback Boar Mammal Hefty boar with amber carapace-like bristles. Frostwood outskirts Hunts are dedicated to local kami; tusks carved into protective talismans.

Sprinkle these beasts into travel montages, merchandise lists, or lore dumps to reinforce Shuigari's blend of mysticism and pragmatism.

Flora of Shuigari

Flora of Shuigari

Name Type Properties Region Cultural/Medicinal Use
Jadeleaf Fern Medicinal Herb Known for its anti-inflammatory and healing properties; its sap accelerates wound recovery. Hisui no Mori (Minashima) Used in salves and poultices by healers and monks; considered sacred by local kami worshippers.
Frostiron Moss Moss Retains warmth when dried; often used as insulation or a natural heat source in cold climates. Furenhoku (Celestial Spine) Lined in boots and clothing for miners and hunters to prevent frostbite.

Food and Drink of Shuigari

Food and Drink of Shuigari

Shuigari's cuisine mirrors its geography: mountain villages favor hearty fare that wards off alpine winds, coastal prefectures celebrate the day's catch, and the capital indulges in refined dishes served alongside fragrant teas. Use the following spreads to ground tavern scenes, festival banquets, or downtime visits to the market.

Signature Dishes

Dish Type Description Region Cultural Notes
Rice Bowl (Gohan) Staple Steamed rice served with pickled greens or miso broth. Nationwide Forms the foundation of every meal regardless of class.
Takashima Iron Stew Hearty stew Root vegetables, mountain herbs, and smoked meat simmered overnight. Takashima Prefecture Favored by miners and smiths; often shared after long forge shifts.
Yuzu-Glazed Fish Seafood Grilled river fish lacquered with sweet-tart yuzu glaze. Harado Prefecture Served during harbor festivals and family gatherings among sailors.
Forest Mushroom Hotpot Communal stew Wild mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu simmered in savory broth. Shugane & surrounding forests Hunters bring ingredients as tribute to local kami before sharing the meal.
Mountain Yak Dumplings Snack Steamed dumplings filled with spiced yak and mountain leeks. Takashima Prefecture Packed by travelers crossing the Frostwood passes; sold in roadside stalls.
Celestial Sunrise Porridge Breakfast Millet porridge with ginger, honey, and sun-dried peaches. Hikosan Prefecture Served to visiting dignitaries before morning petitions at court.
Crimson Berry Skewers Street food Skewered berries brushed with rice syrup and toasted sesame. Coastal markets Sold at lantern festivals; rumored to grant good fortune in romance.
Hunter's Skewer Trail ration Charred strips of boar or stag with coarse salt and pepper. Takashima & Frostwood Outpost Standard ration for rangers and patrols; often paired with hot sake.
