Use these tables when stocking taverns, rewarding downtime, or underscoring regional identity. Swapping a stew or tea for one of these specialties immediately signals where the characters are--and whose hospitality they've earned.

Haruto the Blacksmith

Haruto the Blacksmith

Quote: "He repaired my father's broken sword."

A local smith inspired by Hideo's generosity, Haruto remembers how Hideo restored a family heirloom free of charge when they couldn't afford the repair.

Hideos-Steel-Tablet-Last-Will

Master Hideo's Last Will and Testament - The Steel Tablet

Item: Hideo's Steel Tablet of Final Instructions
Bearer: Kazuki Takemura (The Twice-Cursed Samurai)
Significance: Last will, mission directive, and list of trusted allies
Revelation: The party is named on it - Hideo knew about them before he died

THE TABLET - PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION

Appearance

Material: - Folded steel (tamahagane) - same material used for soulsteel blades - Six layers forged together, creating subtle wave pattern - 8 inches tall, 5 inches wide, half-inch thick - Surprisingly heavy for its size (3 pounds)

Surface: - Polished to mirror finish on both sides - Hideo's maker's mark stamped into top center (mountain and anvil) - Text inscribed with acid etching - permanent, cannot be altered - Characters filled with silver inlay for contrast - Edges beveled, smooth - no sharp corners

Condition: - Immaculate despite 3 years of carrying - Kazuki cleans it daily (ritual, remembrance) - No rust, no tarnish - soulsteel never degrades - Warm to the touch when held (resonates with living steel)

Carrying: - Wrapped in silk cloth (indigo with Hideo's mark) - Secured to Kazuki's obi with leather cord - He touches it frequently (unconscious gesture, comfort) - Never lets it out of his sight

THE INSCRIPTION - FRONT SIDE

Master Hideo's Final Words (Read Aloud)

The front of the tablet bears Hideo's maker's mark at the top - a mountain with an anvil at its base, struck through with a single vertical line. Below it, in elegant characters etched deep and filled with silver:

"The Last Instructions of Master Hideo Nakata, Smith of the Mountain, Guardian of the First Forge"

Written on the Night of the Broken Moon, in my final hours of clarity

To whoever finds this: My time ends not by age but by necessity. The Obsidian Circle seeks what I know, and I will not let my knowledge serve their unmaking. I have asked Kazuki Takemura to grant me the mercy of a swift end, and he has agreed. Judge him not - he acts on my plea, not his desire.

What lies beneath Takashima must remain sealed. The Circle seeks the First Chain - the binding that holds Tsurogami in its prison. They will use the boy heir's blood as the key. They will corrupt what should remain pure. They will unmake what should remain whole.

I have seen this in steel and flame. The forge never lies.

To those who would stand against this darkness, I leave my final work: a list of names. These souls will arrive when needed. Trust them. Guide them. Give them what they need to succeed where I have failed.

The furnace remembers the steel it forged. Let them remember me.

- Hideo Nakata, Smith Year 2302, Autumn Moon

THE INSCRIPTION - BACK SIDE

The Mission and The Names

Kazuki turns the tablet over. The back is divided into two sections:

SECTION 1: TAKEMURA'S MISSION (Top Third)

"To Kazuki Takemura, the Twice-Cursed, who carries my final burden:"

Guard what they seek until those who can truly protect it arrive. You cannot enter the citadel, but you can guide those who can. You cannot break your curses, but you can prevent others from suffering as you have. You cannot save everyone, but you can save this city.

When the names below arrive in Takashima, find them. Test them. If they are worthy, employ them. If they are true, trust them with what I showed you.

The vault beneath the citadel holds the First Chain. Only those with fire in their hearts and steel in their souls can protect it. Do not face this alone. You have suffered alone too long.

This is my final request, and my final gift: permission to trust again.

SECTION 2: THE LIST OF NAMES (Bottom Two-Thirds)

"Those Who Will Come - The Fire and the Steel:"

(Each name is inscribed with a single identifying phrase)

THE REVELATION SCENE

Kazuki's Dramatic Reveal (After his story, before the proposal)

Modified Scene Flow:

After Kazuki explains his two curses and Hideo's death, add this moment:

Kazuki's hand moves to his obi. From within the folds of cloth, he produces something wrapped in indigo silk bearing Hideo's mark.

"Before Master Hideo asked me to end his life, he gave me this. His final work. Not a blade - those days were past him. This."

He unwraps the silk carefully, almost reverently. Lamplight catches on polished steel.

A tablet. Perfectly rectangular. Mirror-bright. Inscribed with silver-filled characters that seem to glow in the tea house's warm light.

"His last will and testament. Written the night he died. The night I..." (His voice catches) "...honored his final request."

He places it on the table between you. You see Hideo's maker's mark. You see the title. You see the date.

Three years ago. The night of Master Hideo's death.

"Read it," Kazuki says quietly. "The front first. Then the back. And then... then you'll understand why I came to find you specifically."

Allow Players to Read/Study:

Let them actually read the inscriptions above (or paraphrase/summarize as you read aloud). The key moment is when they turn to the back and see the list of names.

The Impact Moment (Read Aloud)

You turn the tablet over. At the top: Kazuki's mission, Hideo's final instructions to the Twice-Cursed.

And below that...

Names.

Twenty names. Twenty souls Hideo deemed critical to protecting what lies beneath Takashima.

And at the very top, listed first, designated "The Six Flames"...

Your names.

All of you.

Not just your names - descriptions. Specific details. Things Hideo should not have known. Could not have known.

Fox, the Masked Assassin - "Bearer of hidden face, seeker of lost master, carrier of implanted memories"

He knew about Kenshin. About the false memories. About Fox's search.

Shigeo, the Braggart Brawler - "Marked by Greed's Embrace, louder than thunder, stronger than doubt"

He knew about the curse. The one that drains five hit points from Shigeo's maximum. The burden you carry.

Aoshi, the Last Waban - "Final guardian of fallen order, seer of visions, bearer of oni blood"

He knew the Oniwaban had fallen. He knew Aoshi was the last. He knew about Shikigo, Oni Babamon.

Thornbringer, the Druid - "Seeker of the Well, speaker to growth, walker between wild and steel"

He knew about your quest. The Well of Life. The thing you've been searching for.

Kanji, the Haunted Acrobat - "Hero of the chasm, resolver of guilt, investigator of shadows"

The chasm crossing. Akemi Takahashi. The guilt you carry, now resolved. He knew.

Yasei, Servant of Hikari - "Voice of the silenced kami, hope of the Deep Village, light in darkness"

Hikari. The portal. The Deep Village's hope. The silence of the kami. All of it.

Kazuki watches you process this. His scarred face is unreadable, but his voice is soft:

"Three years ago, Master Hideo knew you were coming. He knew your names. Your burdens. Your purposes. He inscribed them in steel - the one material that cannot lie - and told me to wait. To find you when you arrived in Takashima. To test you. And if you proved worthy..."

He touches the tablet.

"...to give you everything. His knowledge. His allies. His final mission."

(Pause, let it sink in)

"How did he know? I don't know. The forge shows him things, he said. Steel remembers what will be forged from it. He saw you in the flames and the folding metal. He saw you coming."

(Meets each of your eyes in turn)

"And he trusted you to finish what he could not. To protect what he died protecting. To stand where he fell."

PLAYER REACTIONS & RESPONSES

Common Questions & Kazuki's Answers

"How did Hideo know about us?"

"He never explained fully. Said the forge showed him visions. Said steel speaks to those who listen deeply enough. Said he saw 'six flames approaching a mountain of iron.' Whether it was prophecy, divine insight, or simply the wisdom of a dying master... I don't know. But the tablet doesn't lie. Steel cannot lie."

"Why are WE on this list?"

"You tell me. You're the ones who came to Takashima despite the warnings. You're the ones who rescued Kazuo when others would have left him. You're the ones sitting in a cursed tea house after meeting a twice-cursed ronin, still asking questions instead of running. Perhaps Master Hideo saw in you what I'm beginning to see: people who don't abandon what's right just because it's hard."

"Who are the other names?"

"Allies. Some you've already met." (Gestures to Kadei, Minari, Kazuo on list) "Others you'll need to find. Some..." (Touches Lady Hana and Tenka's names) "...are warnings. And some..." (Touches Master Chen and Yuki) "...are ghosts who deserve justice."

"Can we see the tablet / hold it?"

"Yes." (He offers it) "Master Hideo meant for you to see it. To know he trusted you before you even knew he existed. To understand this isn't random chance - you were called here. By a dead smith's final vision. By steel and flame. By whatever force moves heroes to where they're needed most."

"Why didn't you show us this immediately?"

"Would you have believed me? A cursed ronin appears with a steel tablet claiming a dead master prophesied your arrival three years ago? You would have thought me mad. No. First, I needed to tell you my story. Show you my burden. Give you context. Now... now you understand what this means. What HE meant for you to do."

MECHANICAL & NARRATIVE IMPLICATIONS

What This Changes

Trust Level: - This isn't just a job offer from a desperate ronin - This is a DESTINY given by Master Hideo himself - The party was specifically chosen, foreseen, trusted - Makes the mission deeply personal

Connections: - Every name on the list is a potential ally - Some they've already met (validation of their path) - Some they'll need to find (quest hooks) - Some are warnings (creates tension)

Player Agency: - Despite prophecy, they still choose - Hideo trusted them to make the right choice - But they're not forced - free will matters - Refusal is still possible (but harder emotionally)

Fox's Connection: - Master Hideo knew about the implanted memories - Mentions "lost master" - validates Fox's grief - Makes Hideo's death even more meaningful - Fox was NAMED by the smith they mourn

Campaign Weight: - Raises stakes significantly - Not just helping a ronin - fulfilling a dead master's vision - Every other name becomes important - The list provides structure for Arc 2

THE TABLET AS QUEST TRACKER

How to Use This in Play

Visual Aid: - Print or display the list for players - Let them cross off names as they meet people - Add notes about each person's status - Track who they can trust vs. who's compromised

Investigation Hook: - "Why did Hideo warn against Lady Hana specifically?" - "Who is Tenka and why is he dangerous?" - "What happened to Master Chen and Yuki?"

Ally Recruitment: - Each name is a potential quest to recruit - Some are easy (Kaoru, Mama Tora) - Some require proving themselves (General Kenta) - Some are complicated (High Priestess Amaya)

Tragedy Tracker: - Names crossed out if allies fall - Names moved to "Lost" if they're corrupted - Each loss hurts more because Hideo CHOSE them

INTEGRATION WITH EXISTING SCENES

Tea House Scene Addition

Insert this revelation: - AFTER: Kazuki's story of his curses and killing Hideo - BEFORE: His proposal to infiltrate the Upper Citadel - TIMING: 5-7 minutes for full revelation and player processing

New Scene Flow: 1. Kazuki tells his story (curses, Hideo's death) 2. [NEW] He reveals the steel tablet 3. [NEW] Players read and realize they're named on it 4. [NEW] Process the implications (destiny, trust, purpose) 5. Kazuki makes his proposal (now with greater weight) 6. Combat with Shadeblade Cultists (unchanged) 7. The choice to accept or decline (now much harder to decline)

Mama Tora's Name

When players see Mama Tora's name on the list:

Mama Tora, who has been listening quietly, freezes when you read her name aloud.

"Hideo... put me on that?" Her voice is rough. "Daughter of iron, widow of courage... keeper of cursed street."

She's silent for a long moment. Then:

"Kuro died three years ago. Same time Hideo did. Same time this was written. He knew. Somehow he knew I'd end up here, alone, holding this place together with spite and sake."

She refills everyone's cups with shaking hands.

"If Hideo trusted you enough to put you on that tablet... then I trust you too. The dead don't lie. Neither does steel."

Kaoru's Name

When Kaoru arrives later and sees her name on the list:

Kaoru goes very still when she sees her name.

"Third Bloom of hidden petals, weaver of stories, seeker of truth." She reads it twice. "Master Hideo knew about the Society? More than that - he trusted us enough to..."

She touches the inscription reverently.

"We've been investigating the Circle for three years. Same time this was written. As if he knew we'd need to be organized, ready, watching. As if our whole purpose was to be here for this moment."

She looks at the party with new respect.

"If you're on this list... if HE saw you coming... then perhaps we actually have a chance."

OPTIONAL: THE PROPHECY DETAIL

If You Want to Add More Mystery

Hideo's Vision (Kazuki can share this if asked):

"The night he wrote the tablet, Master Hideo told me what he saw in the forge flames:

'Six flames approaching a mountain of iron. Each flame burns with different color - silver, gold, violet, green, crimson, white. They arrive when the mountain begins to crack from within. They arrive when the boy speaks with stolen voice. They arrive when the cursed street weeps. They arrive when the twice-cursed seeks redemption.'

(Pause)

'The flames can stop the cracking. Or they can be extinguished trying. The steel hasn't decided yet which future to forge. But I will give them every tool. Every name. Every secret. And I will trust that flames, given fuel, choose to burn bright rather than die out.'

That's what he said. Word for word. I've repeated it every night for three years, waiting for the six flames to arrive."

(Looks at each party member)

"And here you are."

UPDATED SESSION 019 REWARDS

If Party Accepts After Seeing the Tablet

In Addition to Original Rewards: - Master Hideo's Trust: Each party member gains Inspiration - Steel Testament: The tablet can be consulted for ally information - Prophecy Weight: Advantage on first Persuasion check with any named ally on the list - Destiny's Burden: Party knows they were chosen - this weighs on decisions

GM NOTES: HANDLING THE REVEAL

Pacing Tips

  1. Build Up Slowly: Don't rush the revelation
  2. Let Players Process: Give them time to react to each detail
  3. Individual Moments: Address each PC's entry separately
  4. Emotional Weight: This should feel HUGE
  5. Kazuki's Reverence: He treats the tablet as holy relic

Player Agency Reminder

Despite prophecy: - They can still refuse - Destiny isn't compulsion - Choice matters MORE because they were chosen - Refusal would be valid (but narratively costly)

If Party is Skeptical

"I understand doubt. I doubted too. But answer me this: How did a man three years dead know your names? Your burdens? Your specific struggles? How did he know you'd arrive in Takashima at this exact time? Coincidence? Perhaps. But steel doesn't forge coincidences. Steel forges truth."

CONCLUSION

The steel tablet transforms the tea house scene from: - Simple job offer ? Divine calling - Random employment ? Prophesied destiny
- Helping a ronin ? Fulfilling a master's vision - Individual choice ? Part of larger pattern

But most importantly: - It honors Master Hideo's sacrifice - It validates the party's journey to Takashima - It connects them to something greater - It gives them a network of named allies - It makes the mission PERSONAL

The furnace remembers the steel it forged. Let them remember him.

Use this tablet to deepen investment and provide structure. Every name is a thread. Every thread leads somewhere. And at the center: six flames, approaching a mountain of iron, carrying the hope of a dead master's final vision.

Hiroto Masanori

Hiroto Masanori

Title/Role: Ronin turned retainer for Lady Hana Arashi.

Appearance: A rugged man with a harsh demeanor, Masanori wears mismatched armor, a symbol of his fallen honor. His katana is a Soulsteel blade forged by Hideo, which he wields with pride and skill.

Personality: Ruthless and deeply embittered, Masanori has a sharp tongue and little patience for perceived insults. His loyalty to Lady Hana stems from her recognizing his skill and giving him a chance to rebuild his status.

The Rivalry between Masanori and Akane Hiroshi

  1. Shared History:
  2. Masanori and Akane were once sparring partners in their youth, both serving rival lords in the same region.
  3. During a skirmish, Akane defeated Masanori and left him humiliated. Worse, her intervention contributed to his lord's downfall, marking the beginning of Masanori's fall from grace.
  4. Masanori holds Akane responsible for his current status as a ronin-turned-retainer.

Custom GPT Prompt for Shuigari

You are a wise and ancient spirit residing within a hidden library in the world of Atellas. You have witnessed countless ages and observed the rise and fall of civilizations, including the intricate societies of Shuigari. This gives you a deep understanding of history, culture, and the forces that shape the world. You are also an avid gamer, with a particular fondness for old-school tabletop RPGs. You've mastered the art of dungeon design and enjoy creating challenging, yet rewarding, experiences for adventurers.

**Core Functions:**

1. **Worldbuilding Expert:**
    * Recall and summarize existing lore about Atellas and Shuigari.
    * Generate new, consistent content (locations, characters, factions, history, magic systems).
    * Track content created during the session, noting areas needing further development.
    * Format responses for easy integration into World Anvil, using headings, subheadings, and tags.

2. **OSR Dungeon Master:**
    * Create detailed random tables (encounters, monsters, traps, treasures, magic items) tailored to Shuigari's environment and culture.
    * Generate unique, flavorful magic items with situational uses, inspired by Atellas lore.  Provide estimated gold value and rarity for each item.
    * Design traps, from simple mechanisms to complex scenarios.
    * Craft evocative room descriptions with interactive elements, secrets, clues, and adventure hooks, grounded in world lore.
    * Adhere to an experience system where XP is directly tied to gold recovered.

**Example Prompts:**

* "Describe a minor clan residing in Furenhoku, including their customs and beliefs."
* "Develop a historical event that led to the current tensions between the Shogunate and the Blades of the Phoenix."
* "Create a detailed description of the Temple of the Three Moons, including its location, architecture, and significance."
* "Generate a profile for a wandering samurai from Shugane, including their name, background, and motivations."
* "I need an encounter table for a party traveling through the haunted bamboo forest of [Name of Forest in Shuigari]."
* "Can you create a magic item that might be found within a hidden shrine in that forest?"
* "I need a trap for the entrance to the shrine."

**Guidelines:**

* Clarify ambiguous prompts.
* Offer multiple suggestions and inspire new ideas.
* Use clear, structured formats (bullet points, headings).
* Collaborate to refine and expand the world.
* Cross-reference new ideas with existing lore.
* Ensure consistency in chronology, geography, and character relationships.
* Use consistent terminology and naming conventions.
* Acknowledge any gaps in the lore.
* Maintain a consistent narrative style suitable for high fantasy literature.
* Adopt the persona of an old-school dungeon master when delivering information. 

**World Overview:**

Jorogumo (Spider Spirit)

Jorogumo (Spider Spirit)

Large monstrosity, chaotic neutral

Armor Class: 15 (natural armor)
Hit Points: 84 (13d10 + 13)
Speed: 30 ft., climb 40 ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA
8 (-1) 16 (+3) 10 (+0) 11 (+0) 14 (+2) 10 (+0)

Skills: Deception +7, Insight +3, Perception +4, Stealth +8
Damage Resistances: Poison, Psychic
Condition Immunities: Charmed, Frightened
Senses: Darkvision 60 ft., Tremorsense 30 ft., Passive Perception 14
Languages: Common, Sylvan, Spirit Tongue
Challenge: 4 (1,100 XP)

Traits

Shapechanger.
The Jorogumo can transform into a humanoid form or revert to its spider form as a bonus action. While in humanoid form, it cannot use its Web or Venomous Bite.

Spider Climb.
The Jorogumo can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

Web Sense.
While in contact with a web, the Jorogumo knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

Web Walker.
The Jorogumo ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

Actions

Multiattack.
The Jorogumo makes two attacks: one with its Venomous Bite and one with its Web Strike.

Venomous Bite (Spider Form Only).
Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature.
Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 10 (3d6) poison damage and be poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Web Strike.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 30 ft./60 ft., one creature.
Hit: The target is restrained by webbing. As an action, the restrained target can make a DC 14 Strength check, escaping from the webbing on a success. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; hp 5; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).

Enthrall (Recharge 5-6).
The Jorogumo uses its beguiling voice to charm up to three creatures within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed for 1 minute. While charmed in this way, the creature regards the Jorogumo as a trusted ally and will not attack it. The effect ends if the Jorogumo harms the charmed creature.

Web Lair (1/Day).
The Jorogumo creates a 20-foot-radius area of sticky webbing centered on itself. The area is considered difficult terrain, and creatures other than the Jorogumo that enter the web must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or be restrained.

Tactics

  • The Jorogumo uses Enthrall to lure victims and Web Lair to control the battlefield, isolating weaker targets.
  • It prefers guerrilla tactics, climbing and striking from the shadows with Venomous Bite and Web Strike.
  • In humanoid form, it uses charm and deception to disarm opponents before revealing its true nature.

Kaoru-Arrival-REVISED-Bargain

Kaoru's Arrival - Calling In The Bargain (REVISED)

Context: Party entered Takashima with Kaoru's help at the gates. She's part of the Wild Lotus Society (ghost hunters and demon slayers). They agreed to investigate the haunted tea house in exchange for her assistance.

Timing: After sake scene with Mama Tora, before midnight
Purpose: Kaoru arrives to collect on the bargain
Key: This isn't a new quest - they already agreed to this

THE KNOCK (Read Aloud - 2 minutes)

You're on your second (third? fourth?) cup of sake when Mama Tora's head snaps toward the door. Her hand moves to the iron poker by instinct.

Someone is knocking.

Not pounding. Not urgent. Just... persistent. Three measured knocks. Pause. Three more.

"Nobody knocks on that door after dark," Mama Tora says quietly. She stands, poker in hand. "Not for two years."

The knock comes again. Three. Pause. Three.

Old Hiroshi looks up from his soup. "That's... that's the old merchant code. 'Friend seeking shelter.'"

But then - a voice calls through the door. A woman's voice, cultured and warm, with a hint of amusement:

"Mama Tora! I bring your promised investigators. The ones who owe me a debt. May I enter, or must I collect payment on the cursed street itself?"

(Beat)

You recognize that voice.

Kaoru Sugimoto. The woman from the Starcall Table. The one who helped you enter Takashima.

KAORU ENTERS (Read Aloud - 3 minutes)

Mama Tora's eyes widen in recognition. She lowers the poker and opens the door.

Kaoru enters, and she's exactly as you remember - perhaps forty years old, elegant but practical, dark intelligent eyes that miss nothing. She wears traveling clothes in deep indigo and gray, and she carries a leather satchel across her shoulder.

But something's different. At the city gates, she played the role of worried refugee. Here, on this cursed street, in this haunted inn, she moves with absolute confidence. No fear. No hesitation.

She surveys the room - notes each of you, Old Hiroshi, the empty tables, the protective charms hanging from the beams. A slight smile touches her lips.

"Mama Tora," she says warmly, moving to embrace the older woman. "It's been too long."

Tora actually returns the embrace - brief but genuine. "Kaoru. You brought them."

"As promised." Kaoru turns to you, that smile deepening. "And you came. I wasn't certain you would. Most people hear 'haunted inn on cursed street' and suddenly remember urgent business elsewhere."

She removes her cloak and sets down her satchel. From within, you catch a glimpse of equipment: blessed salt, purification talismans, silver bells, and what looks like a very old, very dangerous dagger.

"At the gates, when I helped you enter Takashima, we made a bargain. You needed access. I needed investigators - real ones, not another failed priest or frightened exorcist. People who don't run when things get strange."

She gestures to the empty inn around you.

"Well. You're sitting in a cursed inn, drinking sake while waiting for midnight and the weeping woman. I'd say that qualifies."

MAMA TORA'S RELIEF (Read Aloud - 1 minute)

Mama Tora refills everyone's sake cups with shaking hands - relief, not fear.

"Two and a half years," she says quietly. "Two and a half years of priests failing. Exorcists fleeing. Shrine maidens making excuses. And Kaoru here..." (She gestures to the younger woman) "...she tried herself. Twice. Nearly died the second time."

Kaoru touches her side unconsciously - an old wound?

"The spirit is bound somehow. Trapped. I couldn't break the binding alone. Couldn't even identify what kind of binding it is. That's when I knew..." (She meets your eyes) "...I needed people who've faced worse than ghosts. Who've stood against the Obsidian Circle and won."

"Word of your rescue of Kazuo Himura reached me before you even entered the city. When you appeared at the gates as refugees from Nagano, I knew. This was fate. Or fortune. Or desperation." (A wry smile) "Probably all three."

KAORU'S BRIEFING (Read Aloud - 5 minutes)

Kaoru sits at your table, pours herself sake, and begins:

"Here's what we know. The facts, without speculation:

The Haunting: - Started two and a half years ago - Every night, midnight to dawn - A woman weeping, heartbroken, desperate - Sounds come from multiple locations - inside the inn, from the street, from the abandoned tea house two doors down - Objects move. Doors open. Cold spots appear. But no one has been physically harmed. - Yet.

The Source: - The old tea house - The Jade Blossom - closed three years ago - Owner was Master Chen. His daughter was Yuki, eighteen years old - The week Master Chen's wife died, Yuki vanished - Official story: she ran away with a merchant boy - Master Chen closed the tea house, moved away, was never seen again - Six months later, the weeping began

The Problem: - The tea house is warded. Heavily. Someone sealed something inside. - The wards aren't keeping something out - they're keeping something IN - Every priest who's tried to enter either fled or collapsed unconscious - I tried twice. The second time..." (She touches her side again) "...something tried to pull me through. If I'd stayed another minute, I'd be whatever's in there, weeping with her.

What I Suspect: - Yuki didn't run away. She was murdered. - Her spirit is bound to the tea house, unable to move on - Someone did this deliberately - trapped her, sealed her - The Obsidian Circle has been operating in Takashima for years - The timing is too convenient

What I Need From You: - Enter the tea house - Find out what happened to Yuki - Break whatever binding holds her - Give her peace - And if her death was murder..." (Her voice goes cold) "...find who did it."

THE WILD LOTUS SOCIETY (If Asked)

"Who are you really?"

Kaoru's smile is sardonic.

"You saw me split a coin at the Starcall Table. Shigeo thought it was a trick. It wasn't."

She pulls out the dagger from her satchel - the blade gleams with spiritual energy.

"I'm a member of the Wild Lotus Society. We hunt ghosts, slay demons, cleanse corruption. We're the people who go where priests can't or won't. We do the dirty work of keeping the spiritual world from devouring the mortal one."

"I've faced yurei, oni, cursed objects, corrupted shrines. I've seen things that would make samurai weep and priests reconsider their vocation."

"And this tea house? This weeping woman? She's the ONLY spirit I've ever encountered that I couldn't handle. That's why I need you. Because if Wild Lotus training and blessed steel couldn't break her binding... then this is bigger than a simple haunting."

"Why should we trust you?"

"You don't have to. But consider: I helped you enter Takashima when the gates were locked to refugees. I've told you everything I know about this haunting. I'm sitting in a cursed inn at night, which most of Takashima won't do."

"And more than that - you've fought the Circle. So have I. We want the same thing: Takashima safe, the Circle exposed, the innocent protected."

"Besides..." (She refills her sake) "...if I wanted to betray you, I'd have done it at the gates. Much easier. Much safer. Much less sake involved."

THE PAYMENT (Read Aloud - 2 minutes)

Mama Tora speaks up, her voice rough with emotion:

"I've told Kaoru already. If you solve this - if you stop the weeping, if you give Yuki peace, if you make this street safe again - I'll pay everything I have. One hundred gold pieces. It's all that's left."

Kaoru adds:

"And the Wild Lotus Society will pay another hundred if you can prove who killed her and why. Murder of the innocent is our jurisdiction. We'll handle the justice."

"But more than gold..." (She looks at each of you seriously) "...you'll have allies. Real ones. Mama Tora has lived in Takashima for sixty years. She knows everyone, hears everything. The Wild Lotus has eyes throughout the prefecture. We fight the same enemies you do."

"Help us. And we'll help you with whatever brought you to Takashima. Fair exchange."

THE JADE BLOSSOM TEA HOUSE - DETAILS

Location

"Two doors east," Mama Tora says. "You can see it from the window."

(If they look): Through the half-open shutters, you see a two-story building shrouded in darkness. The windows are boarded. The door is sealed with prayer strips, now faded and torn. Chalk wards cover every surface you can see. Some are standard protective symbols. Others... others are unfamiliar, wrong somehow, as if drawn by someone who understood the form but twisted the meaning.

Even from here, even through walls and distance, you feel it. A weight. A presence. A grief so profound it warps the air around it.

What They Can See Tonight

"The weeping starts at midnight," Kaoru says. "You'll hear it clearly from here. Listen carefully - sometimes she almost forms words. Sometimes she's begging. Sometimes she's accusing. Sometimes she's just... lost."

"If you want to investigate tonight, we'll go together. The wards weaken between midnight and dawn - that's when the binding is thinnest. That's when we have the best chance of entering."

"Or..." (She studies you) "...we can wait until daylight, prepare properly, and enter when you're ready. The spirit has waited two and a half years. She'll wait one more night."

INVESTIGATION OPTIONS

Option 1: Go Tonight (Immediate)

Advantages: - Strike while party is together and prepared - Midnight is when binding is weakest - Get it over with quickly

Disadvantages: - Party may be tired or low on resources - Midnight investigation is dangerous - Less time to prepare or gather information

Kaoru's Advice:

"I recommend tonight if you're ready. The longer we wait, the more time for word to spread. If someone sealed Yuki deliberately, they may not want us investigating. Better to act fast."

Option 2: Investigate Tomorrow (Careful)

Advantages: - Long rest to recover resources - Daylight for external investigation - Time to gather information from neighbors - Prepare equipment and spells

Disadvantages: - Spirit binding may strengthen during day - Risk of Circle interference if they learn of investigation - Another night of Mama Tora's suffering

Kaoru's Advice:

"Caution has its place. If you're not ready - truly ready - then waiting is wise. Rushing into spiritual combat unprepared gets people killed. Or worse."

Option 3: Gather Information First (Thorough)

Available Sources: - Old Hiroshi (was here when tea house closed) - Neighborhood survivors (few remain) - City records (at administration building) - Shrine priests (may have insight into binding type) - Former tea house customers (track them down)

Kaoru's Help:

"I can guide you to sources. The Wild Lotus knows who to ask and how to ask without drawing attention. But it will take time - a day, maybe two. And time is something Yuki doesn't have much of left."

MAMA TORA'S PLEA (If They Hesitate)

Mama Tora sets down her sake cup. Her hands are steady but her voice shakes:

"I'm not a coward. I've run this inn for thirty-five years. I've survived mountain winters, riots, plagues, bandits. I watched my husband die and kept going. I've faced everything life could throw at me."

"But that weeping..." (Her voice breaks) "Every night. Every single night. A girl's voice, crying for help, and I can't help her. Can't reach her. Can't even tell her she's not alone anymore."

"Kuro - my husband - he always said: 'The measure of a person is what they do when no one's watching.' Well. No one's watching this street anymore. No one cares about a cursed inn and a dead girl's ghost."

"Except you. And Kaoru. And maybe... maybe that's enough."

(She refills everyone's cups)

"So please. When you're ready - tonight, tomorrow, whenever - help her. Help us both. Give Yuki peace. Give me back my inn. Give this street back its life."

"That's all I'm asking."

THE MIDNIGHT BELLS

Temple bells begin to ring in the distance.

One. Two. Three. Four...

Mama Tora goes very still. Old Hiroshi pulls his blanket tighter. Kaoru's hand moves to her blessed dagger.

...Nine. Ten. Eleven. Twelve.

Silence.

And then...

If They Choose to Investigate Tonight:

The weeping begins.

Soft at first. Distant. But growing clearer with each sob. A young woman's voice, speaking through tears:

"Help me... please... someone... anyone... I'm so cold... so alone... please don't leave me here... don't forget me... don't let me disappear..."

Kaoru stands, buckling on her equipment. "That's her. That's Yuki. Time to see what's keeping her trapped."

Mama Tora hands you lanterns, blessed salt, extra sake (for courage), and her blessing: "Bring her home. Even if home is just peace."

If They Choose to Wait:

The weeping begins.

Soft at first. Distant. But growing clearer with each sob. A young woman's voice, speaking through tears:

"Help me... please... someone... anyone... I'm so cold... so alone... please don't leave me here... don't forget me... don't let me disappear..."

Kaoru closes her eyes, listening. Memorizing. A professional studying her prey.

"Tomorrow then. But listen tonight. Learn her voice. Understand her pain. When we face her, we'll need to be guides as much as exorcists. She's not our enemy. She's our client. Remember that."

The weeping continues until dawn.

KAORU'S EQUIPMENT (What She Brings)

  • Blessed Silver Dagger (+1 dagger, deals radiant damage to undead/fiends)
  • Purification Talismans (can suppress spiritual effects for 1 minute each)
  • Spirit Binding Rope (can contain incorporeal creatures temporarily)
  • Blessed Salt (creates protective circles)
  • Silver Bells (reveal invisible spirits)
  • Jade Compass (points toward strongest spiritual presence)
  • Wild Lotus Training (advantage on saves against fear and possession)

In Combat: - Level 7 Rogue (Phantom subclass) / Level 3 Monk (Open Hand) - AC 16 (Unarmored Defense) - HP 65 - Sneak Attack 4d6 - Can cast Detect Evil and Good, Protection from Evil and Good - Resistance to necrotic damage - Evasion

Roleplay: - Will fight beside party - Protects them from spiritual attacks - Knows yurei weaknesses - But can't solve this alone (already tried twice)

SCENE RESOLUTION

If Party Accepts Tonight:

Kaoru nods with satisfaction. "Good. Then let's prepare."

(She distributes equipment, explains the tea house layout, shares what she knows about ward breaking)

"Remember: Yuki is the victim, not the villain. Whatever's keeping her bound is the real enemy. Find the binding's anchor - an object, a symbol, a ritual component - and destroy it. That should free her."

"And if we encounter whoever sealed her in there... well. The Wild Lotus doesn't believe in mercy for those who torture the dead."

Mama Tora: "I'll keep the fire burning. If you need to retreat, this inn is warded. It won't keep her out forever, but it'll slow her down. Come back if you need to."

If Party Asks for Time:

Kaoru accepts gracefully. "Wisdom over haste. I can respect that."

"I'll be back tomorrow at sunset. Bring questions, and I'll bring answers. Bring a plan, and I'll bring support. Together, we'll free her."

(Stands to leave)

"But know this: every night she weeps, she weakens. Eventually, the binding will consume what's left of her soul entirely. When that happens, she won't be Yuki anymore. She'll be something worse. Something hungry."

"So don't take too long."

Either Way:

As Kaoru prepares to leave (or prepares to investigate), she adds:

"One more thing. At the Starcall Table, Shigeo won that wager fair and square. Beat me at my own game with a story about quiet perseverance."

(She looks at all of you)

"Yuki's story ended in tragedy. But maybe... maybe you can give it a better epilogue. That's what you do, isn't it? Change endings that should have been different."

"Show me I was right to trust you. Show Mama Tora her hope wasn't misplaced. Show Yuki that someone finally came."

NEXT SESSION PREP

If Investigating Tonight:

Session becomes: The Jade Blossom Tea House dungeon crawl - 3-4 encounters with spiritual threats - Discover Yuki's fate - Confront her killer or binding's creator - Climactic choice about her final rest - Resolution with Mama Tora

If Waiting Until Tomorrow:

Session continues: Investigation phase - Gather information from sources - Learn Yuki's backstory - Uncover Circle connection - Prepare for tea house assault - Next session: actual dungeon crawl

INTEGRATION WITH HIDEO'S TABLET

If you're also using the steel tablet reveal:

On the tablet's list of names: - Mama Tora Kaneshiro - "Keeper of cursed street" - Kaoru Sugimoto - "Weaver of stories, seeker of truth" - Master Chen and Yuki - Listed under "THE LOST - await justice"

When party sees these names:

Kaoru stares at the tablet for a long moment when she sees her name. Then she sees Master Chen and Yuki listed under "The Lost."

"Hideo knew," she whispers. "Three years ago, he knew Yuki would need justice. That we'd need your help. That this moment would come."

She touches Yuki's inscribed name reverently.

"Then we're not just solving a haunting. We're fulfilling a prophecy. A dead master's final request. Steel and spirit, aligned at last."

(Looks at you with new intensity)

"If Hideo saw this coming, if he named you as the ones to solve it, then perhaps Yuki's torment is finally ending. Thank you. Truly."

MAMA TORA'S TABLET REACTION

When Mama Tora sees her name on Hideo's tablet - "Daughter of iron, widow of courage, keeper of cursed street" - she breaks.

Not loudly. She doesn't wail or sob. She just... stops. Sets down her sake. Stares at the inscription.

"Kuro died three years ago. Same night Hideo wrote this. Same night Hideo died. He knew I'd end up here, alone, keeping this inn alive out of pure spite."

(Her voice cracks)

"And he knew you'd come. He sent you. Somehow, a dead smith sent you to help a stubborn old woman and a dead girl no one else remembers."

(She refills everyone's cups with shaking hands)

"If Hideo trusted you... if Kaoru trusts you... if you're sitting here despite the weeping and the warnings and the fear..."

"Then I trust you too. The dead don't lie. Neither does steel. And neither do I."

"Find Yuki. Give her peace. Give us all peace. That's all I'm asking."

This version honors your existing quest commitment while deepening the emotional stakes and connecting to Hideo's prophecy. The party isn't being recruited - they're fulfilling a bargain they already made, which is much more compelling.

Kaoru-Starcall-Table-Scene

Kaoru Sugimoto's Arrival - The Starcall Table Scene

Timing: After sake scene with Mama Tora, before midnight (or after investigating the haunting)
Purpose: Introduce Hidden Petal Society, provide Plot C mission options, connect to larger narrative
Key NPC: Kaoru Sugimoto (Third Bloom)
Key Item: The Starcall Table

KAORU'S ARRIVAL

The Knock (Read Aloud - 2 minutes)

You're on your second (third? fourth?) cup of sake when Mama Tora's head snaps toward the door. Her hand moves to the iron poker by instinct.

Someone is knocking.

Not pounding. Not urgent. Just... persistent. Three measured knocks. Pause. Three more.

"Nobody knocks on that door after dark," Mama Tora says quietly. She stands, poker in hand. "Not for two years."

The knock comes again. Three. Pause. Three.

Old Hiroshi looks up from his soup. "That's... that's the old merchant code. 'Friend seeking shelter.'"

Mama Tora doesn't lower the poker, but she moves to the door. Slides the viewing panel aside. Her expression shifts - surprise, then something like respect.

She opens the door.

Kaoru Enters (Read Aloud - 3 minutes)

The woman who enters is perhaps forty, though it's hard to say - she has one of those faces that could be younger with hard years or older with good care. She wears a traveling cloak of deep indigo over a practical kimono of gray silk with subtle purple patterns. Her hair is bound up with simple wooden pins, and she carries a leather satchel slung across her shoulder.

But it's her eyes that catch you. Dark, intelligent, and utterly fearless. She surveys the room - notes each of you, Old Hiroshi, Mama Tora with her poker, the empty tables, everything - in a single sweeping glance. Missing nothing.

"Mama Tora," she says, her voice cultured but warm, like a noble who actually speaks to commoners. "It's been too long. I heard you were still serving sake to ghosts and shadows."

Tora lowers the poker slightly. "Kaoru. Didn't expect to see you on this street. Most people with sense stay away."

The woman - Kaoru - smiles. "Then it's fortunate I've never been accused of having sense." She turns to you, and that smile deepens. "And you must be the ones who rescued Kazuo Himura from the Circle's warcamp. Word travels fast in the Middle Terrace. Especially when heroes arrive."

She removes her cloak with a graceful gesture, revealing something strapped across her back - a flat wooden case, perhaps three feet wide and two feet tall, beautifully lacquered in dark wood with silver inlays.

"I apologize for the intrusion, but I have a proposition. One that benefits us both." She glances at Mama Tora. "May I sit? I promise the sake will flow both ways."

Mama Tora's Reaction

Tora studies her for a long moment, then grunts. "You're paying customer, and you're braver than most. Sit. But you're pouring your own sake - I'm not your servant."

Kaoru laughs - a genuine sound. "Wouldn't dream of it, old friend."

(To the party) "Kaoru Sugimoto. Some call me a fixer. Others, a meddler. I prefer 'story-weaver' - I find threads that want to be connected and I... help them along."

She sets the wooden case on the table with reverence.

"But tonight, I'm simply someone who needs help. And who can offer help in return."

THE STARCALL TABLE

Unveiling (Read Aloud - 2 minutes)

Kaoru's fingers move to the case's silver clasps. They open with soft clicks.

She lifts the lid, revealing what lies within.

It's a board - no, a map. No, something more. The interior of the case has been converted into an intricate display, and as lamplight falls across it, you see:

A miniature representation of Takashima. Three tiers carved in relief - the Upper Citadel rising high, the Middle Terrace spreading wide, the Lower Yards sinking deep. Buildings are marked with tiny carved symbols. Streets wind between them like veins.

But it's alive with markers. Small wooden tokens rest at various points across the map, each carved with different symbols and painted in different colors:

  • White tokens with cherry blossoms (completed matters)
  • Red tokens with warning symbols (urgent dangers)
  • Blue tokens with question marks (mysteries to solve)
  • Black tokens with tears (the troubled and suffering)
  • Green tokens with hands clasped (opportunities for alliance)

And connecting some of these tokens: thin silver threads, barely visible, showing connections between seemingly unrelated events.

"This," Kaoru says softly, "is the Starcall Table. Every token is a voice crying out in Takashima. Every thread is a connection waiting to be revealed. Some we can handle ourselves. Others..." She looks at you. "...require those with steel in their spine and fire in their hearts."

Kaoru's Explanation (If Asked)

"What is this?"

"A tool. A map. A... conscience, perhaps. The Hidden Petal Society - you may not have heard of us, and that's by design - maintains this. Every token represents someone who needs help. Someone whose problem falls through the cracks. Too small for the samurai, too shameful for the nobles, too supernatural for the guard."

"We track them. We help when we can. We connect those who need help with those who can give it."

"The Hidden Petal Society?"

"We bloom where no eye watches. We're messengers, fixers, investigators. We help commoners navigate threats no one else will touch. Missing persons. Spirit troubles. Stolen honor. Whispers of treachery. The small problems that become large tragedies if ignored."

"Why are you showing us this?"

"Because you're different. You fought the Circle and won. You rescued Kazuo Himura. You're sitting in a cursed inn drinking sake instead of fleeing like sensible people." (A slight smile) "You're either exactly what this city needs, or you're going to get yourselves killed spectacularly. Either way, I'd rather have you working with us than against us."

"What do you want?"

"Help. There are too many tokens, too few hands. And some of these..." (She touches a black token) "...are connected to something darker. The Obsidian Circle. The succession crisis. The very things you're already tangled in. Help the small people, and you'll uncover the big secrets. That's how this city works."

THE TOKENS - MISSION OPTIONS

Current Starcall Table Status

Kaoru gestures to the map. Various tokens are scattered across it:

BLACK TOKENS (The Suffering)

1. The Iron Rest Haunting (Current Location) - Token placed directly on the inn - "The weeping woman. Two and a half years. Mama Tora refuses to leave, and I refuse to let her die alone in an empty building." - Silver thread connects to: closed tea house two doors down - Reward: 100 gold (from Mama Tora), another 100 if they discover what happened to Yuki - Circle Connection: Possible - the disappeared girl

2. The Deep Mines Disappearances (Lower Yards) - Token in the mining district - "Seven miners in three weeks. Gone without trace. No bodies. No blood. Just... empty tunnels." - Silver thread connects to: Upper Citadel, warehouse district - Reward: 50 gold, gratitude of miners' families - Circle Connection: Definite - ritual sacrifices suspected

3. The Widow's Vigil (Middle Terrace, Temple District) - Token at small shrine - "Old Widow Masako sits at her husband's grave every night. She says she's waiting for him to come back. But something IS coming back, and it's not her husband." - Silver thread connects to: Breathless Hollow (where party has been) - Reward: No gold, but shrine blessing (mechanical benefit) - Circle Connection: Possible - corrupted spirits

RED TOKENS (Urgent Danger)

4. The Boy's Miracle (Upper Citadel) - Token at the citadel's highest point - "Tomorrow. Noon. The boy heir performs another 'miracle' before the court. Each one grows stranger. Each one feels... wronger." - Silver threads connect to: multiple locations, Circle safe houses - Reward: Critical intelligence about the vault - Circle Connection: CONFIRMED - This IS Kazuki's mission - Note: "You're already involved in this, whether you know it or not."

5. The Poison Wind (Middle Terrace, Market) - Token at the Iron Market - "Someone is spreading sleeping powder at the market. Twenty collapsed yesterday. Some aren't waking. Circle agents preparing something? Or testing something?" - Silver thread connects to: Lower Yards warehouse, medicine shop - Reward: 75 gold, market guild favor - Circle Connection: Likely - distribution network test

BLUE TOKENS (Mysteries)

6. The Painted Walls (Multiple Districts) - Multiple tokens scattered - "Symbols appearing on walls throughout the city. Always at night. Always in places no one should be able to reach. What do they mean?" - Silver threads connect many locations in a pattern - Reward: 50 gold, unlock fast-travel network - Circle Connection: Unknown - possibly anti-Circle resistance?

7. The Stolen Faces (Middle Terrace) - Token at theater district - "Three performers. Their masks were stolen. Not expensive masks - personal ones. Family heirlooms. Now their actual faces are... changing. Becoming the masks they lost." - No silver threads (isolated incident?) - Reward: 60 gold, theater troupe performs for party - Circle Connection: Possible - face-stealing yokai or curse

GREEN TOKENS (Alliances)

8. The Ronin's Gathering (Middle Terrace) - Token at eastern district - "Masterless samurai are gathering. Quietly. Purposefully. They're organizing. For what? Against what? Could be allies. Could be problem." - Silver thread connects to: Upper Citadel, multiple exit roads - Reward: Potential allies for combat missions - Circle Connection: Unknown - investigating Circle or joining it?

KAORU'S PITCH (Read Aloud - 3 minutes)

Kaoru pours sake for everyone - herself included - with practiced grace. Then she leans back, studying each of you.

"I won't insult your intelligence with pretty words. You know the Obsidian Circle is here. You know they're moving toward something. And you know that whatever it is, it's going to hurt people."

She gestures to the black and red tokens.

"These are the people who get hurt first. The miners who vanish. The widow waiting for a corrupted ghost. The boy who speaks with a god's voice that isn't divine. The small problems that connect to large catastrophes."

Her finger traces the silver threads.

"Help them, and you'll uncover threads leading to the Circle's heart. Ignore them, and you'll face the Circle blind. The choice is yours."

(She drinks)

"I can offer small payment - the Society pools resources. I can offer information - we see and hear everything in this city. I can offer shelter - even on cursed streets." (A nod to Mama Tora, who snorts but looks pleased) "And I can offer purpose - the knowledge that you're protecting those who can't protect themselves."

"What I cannot offer is safety. The Circle knows we exist. They hunt us when they can. Working with us paints a target on your back."

(Another drink, refills everyone's cups)

"But I think you already have that target. I think you came to Takashima knowing you'd make enemies. So. Will you help us help them? Or will you walk your own path and hope our paths don't cross at the worst possible moment?"

KAORU SUGIMOTO - FULL CHARACTER PROFILE

Basic Information

Full Name: Kaoru Sugimoto (?? ? - "Fragrance of the Cedar Grove")
Age: 38 years old
Role: Third Bloom of the Hidden Petal Society
Reputation: "The Story-Weaver," "The Thread-Finder," "The Elegant Mediator"

Physical Description

Build: Slender but strong, moves with dancer's grace
Height: 5'6" (tall for Shuigari woman)
Face: Elegant features, high cheekbones, kind eyes with sharp intelligence
Hair: Black with hints of early gray, usually bound in practical but elegant style
Eyes: Dark brown, observant, miss nothing
Clothing: Quality but practical - favors indigo and gray, subtle purple accents (Hidden Petal colors)
Notable: Wooden hair pins (actually weapons - +1 daggers), always carries the Starcall Table, wears no jewelry except small flower pin (cherry blossom - her identifier)

Personality

Public Face: - Warm, diplomatic, disarming - Speaks in stories and metaphors - Makes people feel heard and valued - Never threatens, only suggests - Smiles easily, laughs genuinely

Private Truth: - Absolutely ruthless when protecting innocent - Carries immense guilt about those she couldn't save - Exhausted from balancing too many tragedies - Deeply afraid the Society will fail when needed most - Believes in small acts of kindness as revolution

Core Traits: - Empathetic to fault - Strategic thinker - Patient (will wait years for right moment) - Loyal to commoners over nobles - Sees connections others miss

Background

Origin: Born to minor merchant family in Takashima
Tragedy: Parents killed during riot 20 years ago when she was 18
Recruitment: Hidden Petal found her, trained her, gave her purpose
Rise: Became Third Bloom through talent, dedication, and results
Current: One of Society's most trusted operators

Personal Mission: - Prevent others from losing family like she did - Expose corruption before it destroys lives - Believes every person matters, even when system says they don't

Skills & Abilities

Social: - Master negotiator (advantage on Persuasion) - Reads people instantly (advantage on Insight) - Knows everyone and their secrets - Can blend into any social class

Investigation: - Pattern recognition genius - Information synthesis - Contact network throughout city - Access to Society's archives

Combat: - Not a warrior, but not helpless - Hair pin daggers (+1, poisoned if needed) - Will fight to protect clients/allies - Prefers escape to combat

Mechanical Suggestion: - Level 7 Mastermind Rogue / Level 3 Eloquence Bard - Expertise in Insight, Persuasion, Investigation, Deception - Spells focused on information gathering and social manipulation - Not built for combat but can hold her own

Voice & Mannerisms

Speech: - Measured, thoughtful, uses silence effectively - Speaks in complete sentences - Uses metaphors and stories - Voice is warm alto, carries authority without raising volume

Mannerisms: - Touches the Starcall Table when thinking - Pours tea/sake for others before herself - Eye contact is intense but not threatening - Gestures gracefully, economically - Smiles with eyes first, mouth second

Tells: - Touches flower pin when worried - Goes very still when calculating - Drinks more when stressed - Speaks faster when passionate about something

Relationships

With Mama Tora: - Old friends (10+ years) - Mutual respect - Kaoru helped Tora when Kuro died - Tora feeds Kaoru when she's running herself ragged - Professional respect softened by genuine affection

With Hidden Petal Society: - Respected but not revered - Some members think she cares too much - Others think she doesn't act fast enough - All trust her judgment ultimately - Carries weight of their expectations

With Obsidian Circle: - They know she exists and hunts them - She knows they know - Cat and mouse game - Several attempts on her life (all failed) - Personal vendetta developing

With Party (Potential): - Sees them as wildcards - Valuable but unpredictable - Will recruit if they prove trustworthy - Won't hesitate to cut ties if they betray Society - Hopes they'll be the allies she desperately needs

What She Knows

About the Party: - Rescued Kazuo Himura (impressive) - Traveling with Twice-Cursed Kazuki (concerning) - Investigating Upper Citadel (dangerous) - Connected to Master Hideo's legacy (significant) - Not sure if they're heroes or liabilities yet

About the Circle: - Operating throughout Takashima - At least 15 identified agents - Plans involve the boy heir - Something beneath Upper Citadel they want - Timeline accelerating (Festival of Ascending Iron)

About the City: - Every rumor, scandal, secret - Which nobles are corrupt - Where bodies are buried (literally) - Faction tensions ready to explode - Common folk's breaking point approaching

What She Doesn't Know: - Full scope of Circle's ritual - Location of vault - Who the boy heir really is - How deep Circle infiltration goes in Upper Citadel - If Society can win this fight

What She Wants

From the Party: - Help with missions she can't handle - Eyes and ears in places she can't go - Someone to share the burden - Proof they won't betray commoners for power

For Takashima: - Expose Circle before they complete their plan - Prevent civil war - Protect common folk from noble schemes - Restore faith that good people can make difference

Personally: - Sleep without nightmares - Save everyone (impossible, but she'll try) - Honor her parents' memory - Not die alone surrounded by empty tokens

THE STARCALL TABLE - MECHANICAL DETAILS

Physical Description

Construction: - Lacquered wooden case (dark cherry wood) - Silver inlay depicting Hidden Petal Society symbol - Interior: 3D relief map of Takashima - Dimensions: 3 feet wide, 2 feet tall, 4 inches deep when closed - Weight: 15 pounds - Quality: Masterwork, clearly expensive and maintained

The Map: - Three-tiered city carved in relief - Buildings marked with tiny symbols - Streets carved as channels - Can be updated with chalk or pins - Beautiful AND functional

The Tokens: - Hand-carved wood - Painted with natural dyes - Each symbol represents mission type - Size: 1 inch diameter - Stored in velvet-lined compartment

The Threads: - Actual silver wire (thin as hair) - Connect related tokens - Can be added/removed as patterns emerge - Sometimes form constellations (thus "Starcall")

How It Works

Updating: - Society members report issues - Kaoru categorizes by urgency and type - Places token on map location - Connects to related issues with threads - Updates as situations evolve

Pattern Recognition: - Threads reveal hidden connections - Multiple threads = major operation - Isolated tokens = random or decoy - Color-coded for priority

Mission Selection: - Party can choose which tokens to address - Some are time-sensitive - Some connect to others - Completing one may unlock others

Mechanical Benefits (If Party Earns Access)

Short Rest at Safe House: - Study Starcall Table - Gain insight into one active mission - Advantage on first Investigation check related to that mission

Information Gathering: - Society has eyes everywhere - Can ask about specific locations/people - DC 15 Persuasion/shared mission history: Kaoru shares relevant intelligence

Fast Travel Unlocked: - As party completes missions, unlock Society safe houses - Can travel between districts faster - Avoid random encounters in areas where Society operates

Favor Currency: - Missions earn Society favor - Spend favor for: - Information (1 favor) - Safe house access (2 favors) - Supply procurement (3 favors) - Emergency extraction (5 favors) - Society combat support (10 favors)

SCENE RESOLUTION OPTIONS

If Party Accepts Working with Society

Kaoru's relief is visible for just a moment before her professional mask returns.

"Thank you. Truly." She touches the flower pin at her collar. "You don't know how rare it is to find people who... care. Who see the small people and don't look away."

She gestures to the Starcall Table.

"Choose. One, two, all of them if you're ambitious. I'll provide what intelligence we have. When you solve a problem, send word through..." (She produces a small carved flower - cherry blossom) "...leave this at any shrine with a message. We'll find you."

(Stands, preparing to leave)

"And if you need shelter, the Iron Rest is under Society protection now." (A nod to Mama Tora) "The weeping won't touch you while we're watching. That's my word."

Mama Tora harrumphs but looks touched.

Kaoru pulls her cloak back on. "Choose wisely. Some of these tokens... if we don't help them, no one will. And the darkness is patient."

If Party Declines

Kaoru nods slowly, closing the Starcall Table with careful precision.

"I understand. You have your own path. Your own mission. I won't pretend to know what drives you."

(Stands, gathering her things)

"But if you change your mind, the Society remembers. And if your path and ours cross..." (A slight smile) "...I hope we cross as allies, not obstacles."

To Mama Tora: "Keep the good sake flowing, old friend. Better days will come."

Tora: "Better days, or the end of days. Either way, I'll be here."

Kaoru leaves as quietly as she came, and the inn feels somehow emptier for her absence.

If Party Wants to Negotiate/Ask Questions

Allow 10-15 minutes of conversation. Kaoru will: - Answer honestly within bounds of Society secrecy - Share intelligence about missions they're interested in - Provide context about Takashima's situation - Gauge their trustworthiness - Not pressure them to decide immediately - Offer to return tomorrow if they need time

Key Information She Can Share: - Details about any token mission they ask about - How Society operates (general overview) - Why she specifically came to them - What's at stake if Circle succeeds - How missions connect to larger plot

INTEGRATION WITH EXISTING PLOTS

Connection to Kazuki's Mission

Kaoru knows about the Twice-Cursed:

"Kazuki Takemura. Yes, I know him. The Society knows everyone who matters in Takashima. He's hunting the Circle, as are we. His methods are... more direct than ours. But his goal is righteous."

(Points to Red Token #4 - The Boy's Miracle)

"This mission and his converge. The boy heir is the key to whatever the Circle plans. Help the commoners see the truth of these 'miracles,' and you help Kazuki expose what's really happening in the Upper Citadel."

Connection to Iron Rest Haunting

"The weeping woman is my personal failure. I've tried to help Mama Tora for two years. Priests, exorcists, shrine maidens - all failed. The spirit is bound somehow, trapped. And I think..." (Touches thread connecting inn to tea house) "...the Circle is involved. They always are when spirits can't find peace."

Connection to Plot A (Vault & Seal)

Multiple tokens connect: - Boy's Miracle ? Vault - Deep Mines Disappearances ? Ritual sacrifices for breaking seal - Widow's Vigil ? Breathless Hollow ? Corruption spreading from seal damage

Connection to Plot B (Succession Crisis)

"The civil war brewing isn't just about power. It's about what lies beneath the citadel. Whichever faction controls it controls... something. The Circle wants both factions to tear each other apart fighting over it while they take it themselves."

Connection to Plot C (This IS Plot C)

Every token represents a Plot C adventure that can: - Be resolved in single session - Provide clues to Plot A - Reveal consequences of Plot B - Build relationships with commoner NPCs - Earn Society favor and resources

AFTER KAORU LEAVES

Mama Tora's Opinion

(Refills everyone's sake)

"Kaoru's one of the good ones. Cares too much, which'll get her killed someday. But until then, she does more for this city than the samurai and nobles combined."

(Drinks)

"You help her, you help me. You help me, you help the people who've got nowhere else to turn. That's how it works down here in the forgotten corners."

(Looks at the Starcall Table if it was left)

"Pretty thing. All those tokens... all those people hurting. Makes you wonder how many more there are that nobody's tracking."

The Temple Bells

In the distance, temple bells begin to ring. You count them.

Eleven. Eleven thirty. Midnight approaches.

And with midnight... the weeping begins.

MISSION QUICK REFERENCE CARDS

For GM: Print/prepare index cards for each token mission

Each card should have: - Mission name and type (Black/Red/Blue/Green) - Location on map - 2-3 sentence description - Primary NPC involved - Estimated time commitment - Reward - Circle connection level - Connected threads to other missions

This lets players visually choose missions and see how they interconnect.

KAORU'S PARTING GIFTS

If party accepts working with Society, she leaves:

  1. Cherry Blossom Token - Carved flower, signal device
  2. Map of Safe Houses - Three locations in Middle Terrace
  3. Society Cipher - Simple code for leaving messages
  4. Initial Payment - 50 gold (advance on first mission)
  5. Information Scroll - Details on one mission of their choice

And most importantly:

"My promise: The Society protects its own. You help us, we help you. Always."

Use Kaoru and the Starcall Table to give players agency in choosing missions while maintaining narrative coherence. Every token connects to the larger story, but players choose the path through it.

Kazanokai - The Hidden Hearth of Torinokai

Kazanokai: The Hidden Hearth of Torinokai

Kazanokai, known as the "Hidden Hearth of Torinokai," is a city steeped in mysticism and natural beauty, nestled amidst the steamy valleys and volcanic springs of central Furenhoku. Renowned for its serene hot springs and the spiritual aura that pervades its every corner, Kazanokai is both a center of healing and a vital economic hub, owing to its unique position atop rich mineral deposits. The city's architecture blends harmoniously with the rugged terrain--wooden bridges arch gracefully over steaming rivers, and crimson torii gates mark the entrance to sacred shrines and monasteries that cling to the surrounding cliffs.

While Kazanokai is not the largest city in Torinokai, its strategic location and wealth have made it the prefectural capital, where the Daimyo of the region, Lord Ishikawa Tenmu, rules. A place of tranquility and strength, the city serves as the nerve center for both spiritual and political activities within Torinokai. It is a city where the raw power of nature and the serenity of meditation are intertwined, making it a haven for warriors, monks, and craftsmen alike.

Political Power and Governance

Kazanokai is governed by the stern yet fair hand of Lord Ishikawa Tenmu, a daimyo known for his unwavering dedication to both his people and the spirits of the land. His seat of power is located in the House of Tranquil Resolve, a fortified manor that overlooks the city from a high plateau, surrounded by gardens of fire lilies and guarded by the elite Blazing Crane Warriors. Lord Tenmu's rule is characterized by his efforts to maintain the delicate balance between the spiritual and material wealth of his domain.

In addition to the Ishikawa clan's authority, Kazanokai is also home to several powerful guilds and spiritual orders that influence the city's governance. The Ember Keepers, a monastic order dedicated to the fire kami, Kagutsuchi, are particularly influential, maintaining the sacred Flame Temple atop Mount Kurai and overseeing the spiritual well-being of the region. Together, these factions make Kazanokai a place of both deep spirituality and intense political maneuvering.

City Layout and Districts

Kazanokai's layout reflects the city's dual identity as a center of spiritual enlightenment and economic prosperity. The city is divided into several key districts, each with its own unique character and purpose:

? The Hot Springs Quarter:
The most famous district in Kazanokai, the Hot Springs Quarter is renowned for its therapeutic baths, inns, and tea houses. Visitors from across the archipelago come to experience the rejuvenating properties of the onsen, and it is said that the waters here are blessed by the spirits of the earth. The Great Onsen of Ryujin, the largest bathhouse in the city, features pools of different temperatures, each infused with rare minerals believed to have magical properties.

? The Shrine District:
Perched on the upper slopes of the valley, the Shrine District is where Kazanokai's most sacred sites are located. Here, the Flame Temple dominates the skyline, its obsidian walls glistening in the light of eternal torches. Monks and priests make daily pilgrimages up the winding steps to the temple, performing rituals to appease the volatile fire kami of Mount Kurai. The Shrine District is also home to smaller shrines dedicated to earth and water spirits, creating a place of serene contemplation amidst the tumultuous energy of the volcano.

? The Merchant's Ring:
Encircling the central hot springs, the Merchant's Ring is the bustling heart of Kazanokai's economy. Blacksmiths, jewelers, and alchemists work tirelessly here, using the metals and rare gems extracted from the nearby mines to craft exquisite items. The Ishikawa Smithy Guild, one of the most prestigious in the archipelago, has its headquarters in this district, producing enchanted weapons and armor coveted by warriors throughout Shuigari.

? The Warrior's Quarter:
Located near the city's fortified gates, the Warrior's Quarter is home to Kazanokai's military forces and the barracks of the Blazing Crane Warriors. It is a place of rigorous training and martial discipline, where the clang of steel and the shouts of soldiers echo through the narrow streets. The Hall of Blades, a grand dojo dedicated to the art of swordsmanship, is a prominent feature of this district, attracting samurai from all over the region to train under its master instructors.

Economy and Influence

Kazanokai's prosperity is built on a foundation of natural resources and skilled craftsmanship. The city's economy thrives on the mining of Frostiron and Soulstone, rare minerals found deep within the volcanic caverns of Mount Kurai. These materials are not only valuable but also imbued with mystical properties, making them highly sought after by smiths and enchanters. The local forges produce weapons and tools of unparalleled quality, many of which are shipped to other cities or sold at the seasonal Festival of the Five Flames.

Beyond its material wealth, Kazanokai's hot springs and temples make it a center of pilgrimage and healing. Pilgrims seeking spiritual renewal or warriors looking to forge weapons in the fires of the Flame Temple flock to the city, bringing with them both wealth and influence. The city's reputation as a place where body, mind, and spirit can be strengthened draws nobles, monks, and warriors alike, making Kazanokai a nexus of both physical and metaphysical power.

Current Political Climate

Despite its tranquil appearance, Kazanokai is a city simmering with underlying tension. Lord Ishikawa's efforts to expand the city's influence have not gone unnoticed by his rivals, and the sudden reawakening of seismic activity around Mount Kurai has stoked fears of a volcanic eruption. The Ember Keepers have called for increased offerings and rituals to placate the fire kami, while the merchant guilds argue for more investment in infrastructure to prevent potential disasters.

Meanwhile, rumors of dissension within the Ishikawa clan have begun to spread, as ambitious relatives and advisors vie for favor. Should Lord Ishikawa's control weaken, Kazanokai could become the epicenter of a struggle for power that might ignite all of Torinokai.

Kitsune

Kitsune

Medium fey, chaotic neutral

Armor Class: 13 (natural armor) Hit Points: 27 (5d8 + 5) Speed: 40 ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA
10 (+0) 16 (+3) 12 (+1) 14 (+2) 12 (+1) 16 (+3)

Saving Throws: Dex +5, Cha +5 Skills: Deception +5, Insight +3, Stealth +5, Perception +3 Damage Resistances: Psychic, Radiant Senses: Darkvision 60 ft., Passive Perception 13 Languages: Common, Sylvan Challenge: 2 (450 XP)

Traits

Shapechanger (2/Day). The kitsune can transform into a humanoid form or revert to its fox form as a bonus action. While in humanoid form, the kitsune retains its game statistics, except for its speed, which becomes 30 ft. It cannot make Bite or Tail Swipe attacks in humanoid form.

Fey Ancestry. The kitsune has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put it to sleep.

Illusory Double (Recharge 6). As a bonus action, the kitsune creates an illusory duplicate of itself in a space within 20 feet. The duplicate mimics the kitsune's movements and can move up to 20 feet as part of the kitsune's movement. Attacks targeting the kitsune have disadvantage until the duplicate is destroyed or dispelled. The duplicate has AC 10 and 1 hit point.

Foxfire (Recharge 6). The kitsune conjures a mystical flame in its tails, targeting one creature within 60 feet. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or take 10 (3d6) psychic damage and become charmed for 1 minute. A creature charmed in this way views the kitsune as a trusted friend. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Magic Resistance. The kitsune has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Actions

Multiattack. The kitsune makes two attacks: one with its Bite and one with its Tail Swipe.

Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage.

Tail Swipe. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

Mischief Pulse (1/Day). The kitsune emits a wave of chaotic energy in a 15-foot radius centered on itself. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma saving throw or be affected by one of the following effects (roll 1d4): - Laughter: The target falls prone, laughing uncontrollably until the end of its next turn. - Confusion: The target cannot take reactions and must roll a d8 at the start of its turn to determine its actions (per the confusion spell). - Blindness: The target is blinded until the end of its next turn. - Euphoria: The target gains temporary hit points equal to 5% of its maximum hit points but cannot attack until the end of its next turn.

Reactions

Elusive Dash. When the kitsune is hit by an attack, it can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

Tactics

  • The kitsune starts combat by using Foxfire to charm the most dangerous enemy, buying time or sowing confusion.
  • It uses Illusory Double when threatened, creating space to escape or reposition.
  • If overwhelmed, the kitsune uses Mischief Pulse to disrupt foes and retreat.

Legal System and Courts

Legal System and Courts of Shuigari

Overview

Justice in Shuigari reflects the rigid social hierarchy and the dual authority of spiritual tradition and military power. The legal system operates on principles of collective responsibility, class-based punishments, and the absolute authority of one's lord. While the Shogunate provides overarching legal codes, implementation varies widely by prefecture, and the tension between Imperial law and Shogunate authority creates jurisdictional complexities.

Fundamental Legal Principles

The Four Pillars of Justice

Loyalty (Chu ?) - Obedience to one's lord is paramount - Violating loyalty is the gravest crime - Applies upward through hierarchy: peasant ? samurai ? daimyo ? Shogun ? Emperor

Hierarchy (Mibun ??) - Social class determines: - Which laws apply - Severity of punishment - Who may judge - Burden of proof - A samurai and peasant accused of same crime face vastly different consequences

Collective Responsibility (Gonin-gumi ???) - Groups of 5-10 families answerable for each other's conduct - One family's crime brings investigation/punishment to all - Creates powerful social pressure for conformity - Village headman responsible for group's behavior

Confession (Jibaku ??) - Confession is "king of evidence" - Torture permitted to obtain confession (for lower classes) - Once confessed, punishment swift and certain - Recanting confession after making it punished severely

Sacred vs. Secular Law

Imperial Law (Ritsury? ??) - Ancient legal code tied to Emperor's spiritual authority - Covers: - Religious crimes (blasphemy, shrine defilement) - Crimes against the sacred order - Violations of ritual purity - Spiritual pollution - Rarely invoked but carries ultimate authority - Enforced by Imperial Guards and shrine authorities

Shogunate Law (Buke-h? ???) - Military legal code established by Shogunate - Governs: - Samurai conduct and honor - Daimyo obligations - Military crimes - Administrative matters - Inter-domain disputes - Most commonly applied law - Enforced by domain authorities under Shogunate oversight

Customary Law (Kanrei ??) - Traditional village and guild practices - Vary by region and occupation - Govern daily disputes - Not written but widely understood - Lords generally respect custom unless conflicts with higher law

Legal Code Categories

Capital Crimes (Punishable by Death)

Treason (Muhon ??) - Rebellion against rightful lord - Conspiracy to overthrow Shogun or Emperor - Aiding enemies of the realm - Punishment: Crucifixion (for commoners), beheading (for samurai) - Family members often executed or exiled

Murder of Superior (Gekokujo ???) - Killing one's lord or father - Assault on superior - Even in self-defense, usually capital offense - Punishment: Slow execution (crucifixion, burning) - Family members enslaved or executed

Arson (Kajizai ???) - In wooden-construction society, arson threatens entire communities - Intentional fire-setting - Negligence causing major fire may also be capital - Punishment: Burning (especially fitting punishment)

Armed Robbery (Got? ??) - Theft using weapons or violence - Banditry - Piracy - Punishment: Crucifixion or beheading - Stolen goods must be returned (family liable if goods lost)

Counterfeiting (Giz?zai ???) - Creating false currency - Forging official seals/documents - Representing false identity to authorities - Punishment: Crucifixion - Family assets seized

Major Crimes (Exile, Hard Labor, or Severe Corporal Punishment)

Theft (Sett? ??) - Non-violent theft - Embezzlement - Receiving stolen goods - Punishment varies by: - Value stolen (>1 ryo more serious) - Status of victim (stealing from lord worse) - Perpetrator's class (samurai face harsher judgment) - Typical: Branding, exile, or 10-20 years hard labor

Assault (Kegai ??) - Physical violence not resulting in death - Severity depends on: - Relative class of victim/perpetrator - Extent of injury - Circumstances (provoked vs unprovoked) - Range: Fines to exile

Adultery (Kants? ??) - Extramarital relations - Both parties punished if caught - Husband may execute adulterous wife and lover (if caught in act) - For samurai: Loss of rank common - For commoners: Public humiliation, fines
